mod_air.title: Air and gases: balloons, air pressure, hot air, smoke, wind, flight
mod_air.text:
### Air and gases: balloons, air pressure, hot air, smoke, wind, flight
Air items (category Air) and how to set them up. The room's air is 101.3 kPa at the scene's room_temp; settings {air: false} makes a vacuum (balloons pop, cards fall, suction cups let go, smoke stops, planes and kites drop like stones). Wind comes from a fan (its stream keeps full speed for about 5.6 fan diameters, then fades) or a breeze (fluids module: a steady wind over the whole table from where it stands; put it at the upwind edge). party-balloon (anchor: its middle; a ball 25 cm across with the default 8 L of air): gas air|helium, fill_l litres put in (an 11-inch, 28 cm balloon holds 11.5 L at its rated size and pops past about 25 L), size (rated diameter), tied (false = it lets its air out of its neck and flies the other way: its neck points along its own −y, so angle −90 sends it RIGHT, 90 LEFT, 0 UP), pump_lps (a hand pump in its neck from t = 0: it grows until it pops; put it on the table with place {on: table}: its pump stands under it), prick_at (s: a pin pops it), string_m + weight_g (a string down to a weight; 0 g = tied to a fixed hook). Air balloons sink slowly (about −3 g net), helium ones rise (+5 g net for 8 L) and on a string pull up on their weight: a 3 g weight is carried away, a 20 g one holds. A small balloon (size 0.12, fill_l 0.3) fits in a vacuum jar: put it in with place {inside: <jar id>} (it rests on the jar's floor, no drop); pumped down it swells (Boyle: at 50 kPa its gas takes about twice the room), and below about 25 kPa it pops (fill_l 0.3 in size 0.12; more gas pops it at a higher pressure). In the jar's thin air its lift is the jar's: even swollen it does not float up. Its gas also warms or cools toward the air round it (Charles: over a hot plate, beside ice): it swells or shrinks a little over some seconds (a 15 s time constant); on a surface over 150 °C it pops. In no air or over-filled it is shown as filled while held, then swells and bursts within 0.3 s of the release. Goals: swells {item, at_least_x} / shrinks {item, at_least_x} (its volume, end against start), pops, jets {item, toward} for an UNTIED balloon flying on its own air (balloon rocket: tied false, place angle_deg -90 to go right; a tied balloon never passes jets: never check a balloon rocket with a plain distance goal). (A balloon rocket riding a string line is the mechanics module's balloon-rocket; an untied party-balloon flies free.) hot-air-balloon (anchor: the middle of its launch stand's base, on the table; the envelope (0.9 m) sits over a heat gun on two wire posts, its top about 1.12 m above the table): it lifts off once the air inside is hot enough (tissue paper 0.9 m: above about 58 °C; start_c 65 by default, heater_w 1500 keeps heating it while its mouth is within 60 cm of the gun), rises, cools through its skin and sinks back. tether_m holds it at that height; heater_off_s switches the gun off; payload_g weighs it down; envelope 'plastic bag' is lighter (lifts above about 39 °C). An unheated one (heater_w 0, start_c = room) stays on its stand. incense-stick (anchor: its holder's bottom, on the table; the smoke leaves its tip 23 cm up): its smoke shows the air moving: it rises in still air, is blown along a fan's stream (put the stick 0.3-0.8 m in front of the fan, the tip at the fan's height or within its stream) and rises fast over hot things (a hot plate, a pan of hot water, the hot-air balloon's heat gun: put the stick right beside it, its tip within a few cm of its edge, so the smoke drifts into its plume) or sinks under cold ones (ice). To show smoke rising faster over a hot thing than in the room, use two sticks lit at the same time, one by the hot thing and one far from it, and the goal rises_faster {a: the stick by the hot thing, b: the room's stick}; start the water hot (a saucepan's water_temp_c 80-90): a hot plate takes minutes to warm (time_lapse) and barely changes the smoke in a few seconds. With ice water in the pan instead the smoke beside it rises about as in the room (cold air sinks down and off the pan, under the smoke, not through it): say so, and do not plan a goal that the cold pan's stick rises slower; smoke_drifts {item, toward} only says which way one stick's smoke goes. anemometer (anchor: its foot; cups at `height`): reads the wind there (put its cups at the fan's height: fan centre y − 0.03 − the anemometer's own y). wind-tunnel (anchor: the middle of its floor's top, on the table; 1.2 m long, 0.3 m inside, its fan box at the upwind end): an even stream at `speed` blowing `blows` through it from t = on_at: a container: put a wind meter, an incense stick, light things or a kite in it with place {inside: <tunnel id>}. vacuum-jar (anchor: its plate's bottom, on the table; inside 30 × 35 cm by default): a container: put things in it with place {inside: <jar id>}: they are set on its floor under its glass top (a small balloon; a card-glass with stand_height 0.1, its stand and all, in a jar at least 0.3 wide and 0.35 high; a suction-cup with height 0.25 and load_kg 1 or less: they must fit inside). From pump_at the pressure falls (by 63 % every pump_s seconds) toward lowest_kpa; vent_at lets the air back in. Inside it the engine's drag and buoyancy follow its pressure too (a feather falls like a coin in a hard vacuum), and a sound source in it (the waves module's buzzers and bells) is heard less as it is pumped; the waves module's own bell-jar is a jar for air items too (a balloon in it swells as it is pumped). vacuum-tube (anchor: its base's bottom, on the table; 1.5 m tall, 30 cm inside, pumped from 0 s down to 0.1 kPa with pump_s 0.4): the coin-and-feather tube: a feather (mechanics' feather, kind craft) and a coin (coin-flat) side by side inside it near its top with place {on: air, x: the tube's x − 0.07 for the feather (it is 15 cm long) and + 0.09 for the coin, y_m: tube height − 0.15}, NOT held (nothing moves before the scene's release, and a held thing gets a pull-pin post drawn inside the tube), and the scene's release after the pump is done (release 2.5 for pump_s 0.4): pumped they land together (goal lands_together {a: feather, b: coin}); a second tube with pumped false (the control, its air the room's) lets the feather drift down far behind (goal lands_first {a: coin, b: feather}). Only the inside of a jar or tube is a vacuum; settings {air: false} makes the whole scene one. card-glass (anchor: its stand's base; the glass's mouth stand_height above it): the air's push (about 330 N on a 7 cm mouth) holds the card up under an upside-down glass of water; with water 0 (no seal) the card falls at the release; in a vacuum jar it falls when the pressure drops to about 10 kPa. suction-cup (anchor: its stand's base): a cup stuck under a sheet with load_kg hanging from it; it holds about 35 kPa × its area on glass (5 cm: 69 N, about 7 kg; 8 cm: 176 N), 30 kPa on glazed tile, 10 kPa on a painted wall, nothing on wood; heavier, it lets go at the release. steam-can (anchor: its stove's foot; its dish of cold water `gap` m to the right): a can boiled boil_s seconds (steam drives its air out) is dunked mouth-down at dip_at by tongs (it takes 1.3 s) and crushed by the air; boil_s 0 = the control, it is not crushed. A warm bath crushes it too: the can buckles once its inside is about 8.7 kPa under the room's 101.3 kPa (92.6 kPa), and the steam in it condenses to water's vapour pressure at the bath's temperature, 2.3 kPa at 20 °C, 47 kPa at 80 °C, 70 kPa at 90 °C, 85 kPa at 95 °C: every bath up to about 95 °C crushes a boiled can (a hotter bath crushes it less hard); only a nearly boiling bath (97 °C or more) or an unheated can (boil_s 0) stays whole. So a cold vs warm bath comparison is crushed both times (the cold one harder); plan 'crushes' for both, never 'is not crushed' for the warm one. paper-airplane (anchor: its balance point; place {on: air, y_m: the throw height, e.g. 1.2-2.0}): thrown at the release at launch_speed (5 m/s) and launch_angle (5°) toward `facing`; it glides and lands (distance_m: where it touched down; it stops within about 15 cm there, so a measuring tape on the floor reads the same): from 1.5 m a dart flies about 4-5 m, a glider (broad wings) 8-11 m, a balsa glider 10-14 m (give it room: a wide table or floor and a wide stage). elevator (tail flaps up, 5°) trims it: more up = slower and flatter until it stalls; nose_clips make it nose-heavy: steadier, faster, shorter. To compare two planes (a fair test: one thing different), stage them on ONE floor lane: both thrown from the same height (the same y_m) toward the same side, one 0.3 m behind the other (or one after the other), never one lane floating in mid-air (a raised lane needs real supports under it): in this side view two planes share one flight path, and they pass through each other (they never collide). Goal glides_farther {a, b} (a lands farther than b), plus a glides goal for each if you like; add plan.tune knobs for a plane that must reach a mark: launch_speed (3-8 m/s), launch_angle (0-15°), elevator (0-10°). kite (anchor: the foot of the stake its line is tied to, on the table): it flies downwind (`toward`, right by default) on line_m of line when a wind of 2.5 m/s or more reaches it: add a breeze blowing toward that side (place the breeze at the upwind edge of the table); no wind, it falls. bridle 0.3 (where the line pulls, from its nose); too far back (0.45) it flips and falls. Readings: balloon diameter_cm, pressure_kpa (over the outside air), volume_l, lift_g (net: + rises, in the air round it), thrust_n, popped, gas_c; hot-air inside_c, lift_n, net_g, height_m; smoke drift_m (+ right), rise_m; anemometer wind_ms; jar and tube pressure_kpa; card holding (1/0), push_n, inside_kpa, outside_kpa, water; cup holding, hold_n (most it can hold), pull_n; can crushed (0…0.7 of its volume), inside_kpa, temp_c; plane distance_m, speed_ms, height_m, flying, aoa_deg; kite height_m, line_angle_deg, pull_n, wind_ms, flying.
  - goal pops {item, before_s?, expect?}: a party-balloon pops (overfilled, pricked, or in a vacuum), by before_s if given; expect false: it must NOT pop (a control)
  - goal lifts_off {item, at_least_m?, expect?}: it goes UP in the air: its moving parts rise at least at_least_m (default 0.2 m) above where they started, at some time (a helium balloon, a hot-air balloon; not mechanics' rises, which is a machine lifting its load); expect false: it must NOT rise that much (an unheated or air-filled control)
  - goal crushes {item, before_s?, expect?}: a steam-can is crushed by the air (at least 5 % of its volume pushed in); expect false: it must NOT be (the unheated control)
  - goal stays_held {item}: a card-glass's card or a suction-cup is still held up by the air at the end (magnetism's holds is for magnets)
  - goal lets_go {item, before_s?}: a card-glass's card falls or a suction-cup lets go (by before_s if given)
  - goal glides {item, at_least_m?}: a paper-airplane flies at least at_least_m (default 1 m) along the floor before it lands (to compare two planes use measure's farther {a, b} or two glides goals)
  - goal kite_flies {item, at_least_m?, expect?}: a kite stays at least at_least_m (default 0.5 m) above its stake through the last 30 % of the run; expect false: it must NOT (no wind)
  - goal wind_reads {item, at_least?, at_most?}: an anemometer's reading at the end is within those m/s
  - goal glides_farther {a, b, by_m?}: paper-airplane a lands farther from where it was thrown than paper-airplane b (b must have landed; by at least by_m, default 5 cm): a fair test of two planes
  - goal rises_faster {a, b}: a rises faster than b over the same run: two incense-sticks' smoke (a's mean rise over the run's second half at least 5 cm and 20 % more: smoke by a hot pan vs in the room), or two balloons (a higher at the end)
  - goal jets {item, toward?: left|right|up|down, at_least_m?, expect?}: an UNTIED party-balloon (tied false) flies on its own air's jet at least at_least_m (default 0.5 m) toward that side (sideways either way if not given); a tied one never passes; expect false: it must NOT (the tied control)
  - goal swells {item, at_least_x?, measure?: volume|diameter}: a balloon (or another thing with a volume reading) ends at least at_least_x times (default 1.05) its starting volume (or width), or was just before it popped: Boyle (a vacuum jar pumped down), Charles (warmed)
  - goal shrinks {item, at_least_x?, measure?: volume|diameter}: it ends at 1/at_least_x (default 1/1.05, 95 %) of its starting volume (or width) or less: cooled (ice), its air let out, a jar let back up
  - goal smoke_drifts {item, toward: left|right|up|down}: an incense-stick's smoke goes that way on average (right/left: 5 cm or more sideways; up: 10 cm or more up and more up than sideways; down: it sinks)
  - knob party-balloon.fill_l: more gas makes it bigger (and nearer popping: it bursts past about 1.3 × its rated size, so in a weaker vacuum it needs more gas to pop); more helium lifts more
  - knob party-balloon.tied: untied, its air rushes out of its neck and it flies the other way (a balloon rocket); tied, it keeps its air
  - knob party-balloon.gas: helium (0.17 kg/m³) is far lighter than air (1.2 kg/m³): a helium balloon rises, an air one sinks
  - knob party-balloon.weight_g: the string's weight holds a helium balloon down only if it outweighs the balloon's net lift (about 5 g for 8 L)
  - knob party-balloon.size: a bigger balloon holds more gas before it pops
  - knob party-balloon.pump_lps: a faster pump fills it sooner, so it pops sooner
  - knob hot-air-balloon.heater_w: more heat warms the air inside faster: hot air is lighter, so it lifts off sooner
  - knob hot-air-balloon.start_c: the hotter the air inside, the lighter it is (ρ ∝ 1/T) and the more it lifts; in a short run this is what counts, since even a 1500 W heat gun warms its air only about 1.5 °C a second
  - knob hot-air-balloon.size: a bigger envelope holds more hot air for its paper (lift grows as the volume, weight as the area)
  - knob hot-air-balloon.payload_g: every gram it carries needs more hot air to lift
  - knob hot-air-balloon.envelope: a plastic-bag envelope (11 g/m²) is lighter than tissue paper with its seams (20 g/m²)
  - knob paper-airplane.launch_speed: a faster throw carries it farther, up to a point: too fast and it climbs, stalls and dips
  - knob paper-airplane.launch_angle: a slightly upward throw stretches its glide; too steep and it stalls
  - knob paper-airplane.elevator: up flaps raise its nose: slower, flatter glides until it stalls; down flaps make it dive
  - knob paper-airplane.nose_clips: weight on the nose makes it steadier but faster and steeper
  - knob paper-airplane.design: broad glider wings or a balsa glider glide much farther than a narrow dart
  - knob kite.line_m: a longer line flies it higher (if the wind reaches up there)
  - knob kite.bridle: the line's point sets its angle to the wind: near 0.25-0.35 it flies; too far back it flips over
  - knob kite.tail_m: a tail's drag keeps it pointing into the wind (steadier)
  - knob suction-cup.load_kg: it lets go once the weight's pull beats the air's push on it (Δp × its area)
  - knob suction-cup.diameter: the air's push grows as the cup's area: an 8 cm cup holds 2.6 times a 5 cm one
  - knob suction-cup.surface: smooth glass or tile seals well; paint leaks; rough wood does not seal at all
  - knob card-glass.water: with no water nothing seals the card and it falls; any water seals it and the air holds it
  - knob steam-can.boil_s: the steam pushes the air out: with no boiling there is only air inside and the can is not crushed
  - knob steam-can.bath_c: colder water condenses the steam to a lower pressure: a harder crush
  - knob vacuum-jar.lowest_kpa: the lower the pressure inside, the more a balloon swells and the sooner a card or cup lets go
  - knob vacuum-jar.pump_s: a faster pump takes the air out sooner
  - knob vacuum-tube.lowest_kpa: the less air is left in it, the less drag a feather in it meets: at 0.1 kPa it falls with the coin
  - knob vacuum-tube.pump_s: a faster pump empties it before the drop
  - knob wind-tunnel.speed: the air through it moves at this speed: drag and lift grow as its square
  - knob anemometer.height: its cups read the air where they are: put them in the fan's stream
  - e.g. "Show that a helium balloon rises but a balloon of air sinks.": two party-balloons side by side in the air at y 1.0 (gas helium vs air); goals lifts_off {helium one, at_least_m 0.5} and moves {air one}
  - e.g. "Blow up a balloon with a pump until it pops.": a party-balloon with pump_lps 2 on the table, seconds 10; goal pops {item}
  - e.g. "Hot air rises: a tissue-paper hot-air balloon over a heat gun.": a hot-air-balloon on the table (tether_m 1 to keep it in view); goal lifts_off {item, at_least_m 0.5}
  - e.g. "Air pressure holds a card under an upside-down glass of water; with no water the card falls.": two card-glass items (water 0.8 vs 0); goals stays_held {full}, lets_go {empty}
  - e.g. "A kite flies in the wind.": a breeze (speed 4) at the table's left edge and a kite (toward right) staked at x 0.4; goal kite_flies {item, at_least_m 0.8}
  - e.g. "Steam in a can condenses and the air crushes it.": a steam-can (boil_s 30) and an unheated control (boil_s 0) side by side; goal crushes {hot can}
  - e.g. "Pump the air out of a jar with a small balloon in it: it swells, then pops.": a vacuum-jar and a small party-balloon (size 0.12, fill_l 0.3) inside it on its floor; goals swells {balloon, at_least_x 1.5} and pops {balloon}
  - e.g. "Does the card stay on the glass of water in a vacuum?": a vacuum-jar (0.3 wide, 0.35 high) with a card-glass inside it (stand_height 0.1: it fits, stand and all); goal lets_go {card-glass}
  - e.g. "Which paper plane flies farther, a dart or a glider?": a dart and a glider on one floor lane, thrown from the same height 1.5 m, the glider 0.3 m behind the dart (they pass through each other); a wide stage; goal glides_farther {a: glider, b: dart}
  - e.g. "A coin and a feather fall together in a vacuum tube.": a pumped vacuum-tube and a control tube (pumped false), each with a craft feather and a coin side by side near its top (not held); release 2.5 s (after the pump); goals lands_together {feather, coin} in the pumped tube, lands_first {coin, feather} in the control
  - e.g. "Smoke rises faster over a pan of hot water than in the room.": a saucepan of water already hot (water_temp_c 90), an incense stick right beside it (its tip 9 cm from the pan's middle edge), another incense stick far off in the room, lit at the same time; goal rises_faster {a: the pan's stick, b: the room's} (about 0.77 against 0.37 m)
  - e.g. "Let go of a blown-up balloon without tying it: it shoots off.": an untied party-balloon (tied false, place angle_deg -90 so its neck points left and it flies right) in the air; goal jets {item, toward right, at_least_m 1}
### party-balloon — Party balloon · dynamic
A latex party balloon. The gas inside (air or helium) fills it until its pressure (the room's + the rubber's) matches the gas law PV = nRT: more gas, a warmer room or less air outside (a vacuum jar) make it bigger, and past 1.3 times its rated size it pops. Air in it is heavier than the air it pushes aside, so it sinks slowly; helium floats it up (on a string it pulls up on its weight). Untied, its jet sends it flying the way its neck does not point; on a pump it grows until it pops; pricked, it pops. Its gas warms or cools toward the air round it (over a hot plate it swells a little, by ice it shrinks); it pops on a surface over about 150 °C. In no air, or over-filled, it swells and bursts as soon as it is let go. Facts: 11-inch latex · 8 L of air · 25 cm · 3 g of rubber.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.246 × 0.246 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: gas: *air* | helium; fill_l: L =8 [0…40]; size: m =0.28 [0.12…0.45]; tied: bool =true; pump_lps: L/s =0 [0…2]; prick_at: s =-1 [-1…20]; string_m: m =0 [0…2]; weight_g: g =20 [0…500]; color: *red* | blue | yellow | green | orange | purple | pink | white | silver | black.

### hot-air-balloon — Model hot-air balloon · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A tissue-paper (or plastic-bag) hot-air balloon on a launch stand over a heat gun. Hot air is lighter than the room's air (ρ ∝ 1/T at the same pressure), so once the air inside is hot enough its lift beats the envelope's weight and it rises; away from the heat gun it cools through its skin and sinks back. Bigger, lighter or hotter rises faster. Facts: 0.9 m tissue envelope · 50 g · rises above about 58 °C inside.

### incense-stick — Incense stick (smoke) · static (fixed in place)
A burning incense stick whose smoke shows how the air moves: it rises in its own warm plume, is carried off by a fan's stream or a breeze, rises faster over hot things (a hot plate, a lamp, a hot drink, a heat gun) and sinks over cold ones (ice). No air, no smoke. Facts: 10 puffs a second, each lasting 4.8 s.

### anemometer — Wind meter (anemometer) · static (fixed in place)
A cup anemometer on a pole: it reads the air's speed at its cups (a fan's stream, a breeze) and its cups spin with it. Facts: reads m/s at its cups.

A clear-topped wind tunnel with a fan at its upwind end: an even stream of air through it at `speed`. Put things inside it to test them in a steady wind: a wind meter reads it, smoke shows it, a kite or a paper airplane on its floor meets it, light things blow along. Facts: 1.2 m × 30 cm · 5 m/s.

### vacuum-jar — Vacuum jar · static (fixed in place)
A glass bell jar on a vacuum pump's plate. From `pump_at` the pump takes the air out: the pressure inside falls toward its lowest. Things inside feel it: a balloon swells and pops, a card falls off an upside-down glass of water, a suction cup lets go. Facts: 30 × 35 cm inside · pumps from 0.5 s.

### vacuum-tube — Vacuum tube (coin and feather) · static (fixed in place)
A tall clear tube on a vacuum pump's base: its pump takes the air out of it from `pump_at`. Inside it the air's drag and buoyancy fall with the pressure, so a feather and a coin let go together at its top (held, released after the pump is done) fall together in the pumped tube; with its air (pumped false) the feather drifts down far behind the coin. Only the inside of the tube is a vacuum: the room keeps its air. Facts: 1.5 m × 30 cm inside · pumped down from 0 s.

### card-glass — Upside-down glass of water and card · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A glass of water held upside down by a clamp with a card over its mouth. The air pushes up on the card far harder than the water weighs (about 390 N on a 7 cm mouth), so the card stays: the trapped air stretches only a fraction of a millimetre. With no water (no seal), or with the air gone (a vacuum, a vacuum jar pumped down), the card falls and the water pours out. Facts: 7 cm glass · 80 % full · index card. Moving parts ≈8.51 g.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the stand's base. Outline at defaults: 0.22 × 0.46 m; from the anchor x −0.11…+0.11, y +0…+0.46.
Props: water: =0.8 [0…1]; diameter: m =0.07 [0.05…0.1]; height: m =0.12 [0.08…0.16]; card: *index card* | playing card | cardboard | plastic lid; stand_height: m =0.3 [0.1…0.6].

Notes: also called: air pressure, card trick, upside down glass, water, atmospheric pressure, vacuum, glass of water.
### suction-cup — Suction cup holding a weight · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A suction cup pressed onto the underside of a sheet (glass, tile, painted board or wood) with a weight hanging from it. It is held up by the air's push on it (the room's pressure over the partial vacuum under it): a 5 cm cup on glass holds about 69 N (7 kg). Heavier, it lets go; on wood it never sticks; in a vacuum jar it falls. Facts: 5 cm cup on glass · holds about 7 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the stand's base. Outline at defaults: 0.3 × 0.628 m; from the anchor x −0.15…+0.15, y +0…+0.628.
Props: diameter: m =0.05 [0.02…0.1]; surface: *glass* | glazed tile | painted wall | wood; load_kg: kg =1 [0…10]; height: m =0.6 [0.25…1.2].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): holding (Holding: 0 no, 1 yes), hold_n (Most it can hold, N), pull_n (Pull on it, N).
Surface: material suction cup vinyl; bounce 0.1, friction 1, rolling 0.05, side 0.
Notes: also called: suction cup, air pressure, vacuum, sticks, hook, atmospheric pressure, weight.
### steam-can — Can crushed by air pressure · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A soda can with a little water boiled in it on a camping stove: its steam pushes the air out. At `dip_at` tongs turn it mouth-down into a dish of cold water: the steam condenses, the pressure inside falls to a few kPa, and the room's air (101 kPa) crushes it with a bang. Not boiled, nothing happens. Facts: 355 mL can · boiled 30 s · dunked at 1 s into 2 °C water. Moving parts ≈1.43 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the stove's foot. Outline at defaults: 0.58 × 0.182 m; from the anchor x −0.1…+0.48, y +0…+0.182.
Props: boil_s: s =30 [0…120]; bath_c: °C =2 [0…90]; dip_at: s =1 [0.2…10]; gap: m =0.35 [0.25…0.6].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): crushed (Crushed), inside_kpa (Pressure inside, kPa), temp_c (Inside, °C), steaming (Steaming: 0 no, 1 yes).
Surface: material can aluminium; bounce 0.2, friction 0.4, rolling 0.002, side 0.
Notes: also called: can crush, air pressure, steam, condensation, implosion, atmospheric pressure, vacuum, soda can.
### paper-airplane — Paper airplane · dynamic
A folded paper airplane (or a balsa glider) thrown at the release: its wings' lift holds it up while drag slows it, so it glides down and lands some metres away. Throwing faster or a little higher, a glider's broad wings, a little up-bent tail or a paper clip on the nose (steadier) change how far it goes. It needs air: in a vacuum it falls like a stone. Facts: A4 dart · 5 g · thrown at 5 m/s.
Anchor (x, y): its balance point (where it is thrown from). Outline at defaults: 0.279 × 0.035 m; from the anchor x −0.148…+0.131, y −0.022…+0.013.

Notes: acts at the scene's release time; also called: paper airplane, paper plane, glider, lift, drag, flight, wings, balsa glider, aerodynamics, dart.
### kite — Kite · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A diamond kite on a line tied to a stake. Wind on its face lifts it and pushes it downwind; its line holds it, so it climbs until lift, drag, its weight and the line's pull balance; its tail keeps it steady. It needs wind blowing toward `toward` (a breeze, or a big fan): no wind, it falls. Facts: 70 cm diamond · 1.5 m line · 1 m tail. Moving parts ≈22.4 g.

mod_circuits.title: Circuits and electricity
mod_circuits.text:
### Circuits and electricity
A circuit is a closed LOOP from a battery's + back to its − through the parts: current flows only when every part of the one path is joined and closed. Parts: battery (AA cells in a holder: 1.58 V each fresh, kind AA/D/9V/lantern 6V, cells 1-6), bulb (2.5 V 0.3 A torch bulb: about 2 x AA lights it fully, 1 AA dimly, 9 V burns it out), led (one way only: + is its anode; needs a resistor of about 68-150 Ω on 3 V or it burns out over 30 mA), switch (knife: switched over at flip_at s, default 1 s; push: closed while something weighing at least its force rests on its button, or between press_from and press_to), resistor (ohms), dimmer (a rheostat turned during the run from knob to knob_to), buzzer (+ to −, sounds from 2 V), motor (drives a propeller that blows to the right, a paddle or a disc; 'geared' turns slowly and strongly; swapping its wires reverses it), tester (two copper probes 1.5 cm apart: a metal object laid across them closes the loop; plastic, wood, rubber, glass do not), meter (multimeter: volts across a part, or amps in the loop), solar-panel (light on its face makes current: sun W/m², or 0 indoors with a lamp near it), hand-generator (cranked at rpm from start_at).
WIRES are items of type "wire" with no place of their own: props {a: item id, a_end: "+" | "-", b: item id, b_end: "+" | "-"} (an end left unset is joined as current flows round the loop: a battery's + to a part's +, that part's − on to the next part's + or back to the battery's −) ("+" is a part's first terminal: a battery's +, an LED's anode, the right screw of a bulb, switch, resistor or tester; "-" its second). A wire end left without an item is a free end: the loop is open there. Several wires may share one terminal (parallel branches). A simple loop: battery + → wire → part + ; part − → wire → battery −. Series: parts one after another in the one loop (each gets part of the voltage: two bulbs in series are dim); parallel: each part on its own pair of wires across the battery (each gets the full voltage). A wire straight from + to − is a short circuit.
ELECTROMAGNETISM (with the magnetism module's magnets and compasses): electromagnet (an iron nail wound with 5-500 turns, held point down in a clamp in mid-air: wire it in a loop with a battery, a switch and an ammeter; current makes the nail a magnet, its point a north pole for current in at +; on 2 AA it takes about 4-5 A, so the digest may call the loop nearly a short: that is real; hang paper clips under its point as a held chain touching it, and it holds them while switched on, goal holds {magnet: the electromagnet}). coil (200 turns on a tube, 4 cm bore, held in a clamp; axis vertical or horizontal): wire a galvanometer (a meter, mode "galvanometer": centre zero, 0.5 mA full scale) across its two leads, then drop a bar magnet through it (the magnet angle 90, held: true, its middle 15-25 cm above the coil's middle, the coil's middle 15-25 cm above the table so the magnet falls clean through) or push one in: a voltage is induced only while the magnet moves (none while it rests), one way going in and the other coming out (goal induces {coil}); a stronger magnet (neodymium), more turns or a faster magnet: more voltage. straight-wire (Oersted's experiment: a bare copper wire stretched between two clamps in mid-air; runs "over": left to right, in_front 1.2 cm in front of the picture, so put a compass at the wire's own x and y and its needle is just behind the wire, as a compass under a wire; runs "through": straight through the picture, compasses round it point round it): wire it with a battery, a switch and a resistor of about 1 Ω (2 A: 40 µT 1 cm away, twice Earth's 20 µT); the needle swings when the current flows (goal deflects {compass}), the other way when it is reversed. A lead (a wire item) lies in the picture and makes its field across the picture, which turns no needle in it: use the straight wire for a wire's field.
SOLAR INDOORS: a solar-panel with sun 0 and a light on its face: the heat module's desk lamp with its target the panel (a 150 W halogen 20 cm off gives about 300 W/m² as sunlight), or a flashlight aimed at it; its current follows the light the optics module traces onto it (a shadow, a mirror, a lens count). Outdoors: its own sun prop (1000 W/m² full sun, at sun_angle), or the optics module's "sunlight" item with the panel's sun 0 (not both: they add up; the space module's "sun" is a star for orbits).
LAYOUT: put the parts on the table in a row, about 12-20 cm apart, each "on": "table" (their bases are 1-2 cm tall); or for a readable lesson picture, a circuit-board item (60 x 40 cm, on the table) with every part "mount": "board" placed "on": "air" at heights inside the board (a loop drawn as a rectangle: battery at the bottom, bulb at the top). A test object for the tester goes "on": "<tester id>" (it lies across the probes). Readings (light, current, voltage, rpm, sound, reading) and events ("Bulb lights at 1.02 s") come from the run.
  - goal lights {item: a bulb or LED, at_least?, before_s?}: it glows with at least at_least (default 0.1) of its full light over the run's last 0.5 s (with before_s: it first does by then)
  - goal stays_dark {item: a bulb or LED}: it never lights (stays under 0.1 of its full light all run): an open loop, an insulator, a reversed LED
  - goal glows_brighter {a, b: bulbs or LEDs}: a ends at least 5 % brighter than b (series vs parallel, more cells)
  - goal buzzes {item: a buzzer, before_s?}: it sounds (for at least 0.03 s; by before_s if given)
  - goal spins {item: a motor or hand generator, at_least_rpm?}: it turns at least at_least_rpm (default 30) over the run's last 0.5 s, either way
  - goal current {item: any circuit part, at_least_a?, at_most_a?}: its current (A) over the run's last 0.5 s is within the bounds (no bounds: any current at all)
  - goal conducts {item: a tester}: the object across its probes conducts at the run's end (current flows through it)
  - goal deflects {compass, at_least_deg?, at_s?}: a compass's needle ends turned at least at_least_deg (default 15°) away from north, where the Earth's field alone points it (over the run's last 0.5 s, or at at_s): a straight wire's current (Oersted), an electromagnet, a magnet brought near (a beam bending is bends)
  - goal induces {coil, at_least_mv?, before_s?}: a voltage of at least at_least_mv (default 1 mV, either way) is induced in a coil at some moment (by before_s if given): a magnet moving in or out of it
  - knob wire.a (a link): closes or reroutes the loop at that end
  - knob wire.b (a link): closes or reroutes the loop at that end
  - knob wire.a_end: which terminal decides the direction of the current through a part (an LED, a buzzer, a motor) and whether the loop closes
  - knob wire.b_end: which terminal decides the direction of the current and whether the loop closes
  - knob wire.length: a wire stretched past its length comes off its terminal
  - knob battery.cells: each AA cell adds 1.58 V: more voltage, more current, a brighter bulb or a faster motor (too many burn a bulb out)
  - knob battery.charge_pct: a run-down battery gives less voltage
  - knob bulb.rating: a bulb is brightest without burning out at its rated voltage
  - knob led.color: LEDs of different colours need different voltages: red about 2 V, blue and white about 3.2 V (on 3 V a blue LED takes a safe current without a resistor; a red one burns out)
  - knob resistor.ohms: more resistance, less current (an LED needs enough to stay under 30 mA, little enough to light)
  - knob dimmer.knob_to: turned up, more resistance: the bulb dims
  - knob dimmer.knob: where the knob starts sets the first brightness
  - knob switch.closed: a closed switch completes the loop
  - knob switch.flip_at: when the switch is switched over
  - knob switch.force: a push switch closes only under at least this weight
  - knob buzzer.volts: a buzzer sounds from two thirds of its rated voltage
  - knob motor.kind: a geared motor turns slowly and strongly, a hobby motor fast, a solar motor on very little current
  - knob motor.size: a bigger propeller moves more air but slows the motor
  - knob tester.gap: the test object must touch both probes
  - knob solar-panel.sun: its current is proportional to the light on it
  - knob solar-panel.tilt: it makes most current facing the light
  - knob hand-generator.rpm: its voltage is proportional to how fast it is turned
  - knob solar-panel.x: a lamp's light on it falls off as 1/distance²: nearer the lamp, more current
  - knob coil.turns: the induced voltage is proportional to the turns (Faraday's law); more turns also more resistance
  - knob coil.diameter: a narrower bore hugs the magnet: more of its flux through each turn (it must still let the magnet through)
  - knob electromagnet.turns: more turns, more field for the same current (n·I), until the nail's iron is full
  - knob straight-wire.in_front: its field falls off as 1/distance: nearer the needle, a bigger swing
  - knob straight-wire.length: a longer wire is a little stronger at its middle and has a little more resistance
  - e.g. "Show a battery lighting a bulb when a switch is closed.": battery (cells 2), switch (knife, flip_at 1: it closes at 1 s) and bulb on the table about 20 cm apart; wires battery + → switch −, switch + → bulb −, bulb + → battery − (one loop); goal lights {item: bulb}
  - e.g. "Compare two bulbs in series with two bulbs in parallel.": two circuits side by side, each with its own battery (2 AA): series = battery + → bulb 1 → bulb 2 → battery − (three wires); parallel = each bulb on its own pair of wires straight across the battery (four wires); goal glows_brighter {a: a parallel bulb, b: a series bulb}
  - e.g. "Test whether a coin and an eraser conduct electricity.": per test object its own loop battery → bulb → tester → battery, the object placed on the tester (place {on: tester id}) across its probes; goals lights {item: the coin's bulb} and stays_dark {item: the eraser's bulb}
  - e.g. "A battery-powered fan blows a ping-pong ball along the table.": battery and motor (drives propeller: it blows to the right) on the table, wires battery + → motor +, motor − → battery −, a ping-pong-ball 20 cm to the motor's right; goals spins {item: motor} and moves {item: ball, min_m 0.1}
  - e.g. "A ball rolls onto a doorbell button and the buzzer sounds.": battery → push switch (style push, force 0.3 N) → buzzer → battery, a tennis-ball held 30 cm above the button; it drops on it at the release and closes the switch while it rests there; goal buzzes {item: buzzer}
  - e.g. "A desk lamp shines on a solar panel that runs a motor (indoors, no sun).": the heat module's lamp (bulb halogen, power_w 150, head_height 0.25, target: the panel) on the table, the solar-panel 30 cm to its right with sun 0 (indoors: only the lamp's light), a motor (kind solar, drives propeller) beside it, wires panel + → motor +, motor − → panel −; goal spins {item: motor} (the panel reads about 270 W/m² of sunlight's worth, the motor 1500 rpm)
  - e.g. "Oersted's experiment: a compass under a wire swings when the current is switched on.": battery (2 AA) → switch (flip_at 1.5) → resistor (1 Ω) → straight-wire (runs over, place on air y_m 0.06) → back to the battery (2 A: 40 µT 1 cm away); a compass at the straight wire's own x and y_m (its needle just behind the wire, as under it); goal deflects {compass, at_least_deg 20} (it swings to about 50°)
  - e.g. "Drop a magnet through a coil and watch a galvanometer flick (electromagnetic induction).": coil (turns 200, axis vertical, place on air y_m 0.2), a bar-magnet (length 0.06, material neodymium) held above it (held: true, place on air, same x, y_m 0.42, angle_deg 90) that falls through it at the release (0.5 s), a meter (mode galvanometer) on the table wired across the coil's two leads (coil + → meter +, meter − → coil −); goal induces {coil, at_least_mv 10} (it peaks over a volt; the needle flicks one way going in, the other coming out)
  - e.g. "Switch on an electromagnet wired to a battery and an ammeter: it holds paper clips while the current flows.": battery (2 AA) → switch (closed true, flip_at 0) → meter (mode amps) → electromagnet (turns 50, place on air y_m 0.244: its 5 cm nail's point 21.9 cm up) → back to the battery; a paper-clip chain (count 6, spacing 0.0345, held: true, place {on: air, the electromagnet's x, y_m 0.11425, angle_deg -90}: its top clip at the nail's point; for another y_m put the chain's middle 0.13 m below the nail's middle); release 0.3; goals holds {magnet: the electromagnet, count 1, items: [the chain]} and current {item: the electromagnet, at_least_a 1} (about 4.6 A); with flip_at 1 it lets them go at 1 s
### battery — Battery · dynamic
Alkaline cells in a holder (2 x AA = 3 V). Its + terminal is on the right, − on the left; wires join them to the rest of a circuit. Facts: 2 x AA · 3.2 V fresh · 0.4 Ω inside. Moving parts ≈40.8 g.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the holder. Outline at defaults: 0.059 × 0.024 m; from the anchor x −0.029…+0.029, y −0.0088…+0.015.

### hand-generator — Hand generator · dynamic

### electromagnet — Electromagnet (wired) · static (fixed in place)
An iron nail wound with turns of enamelled copper wire, held point down in a clamp, with two leads to wire into a circuit (a battery, a switch, an ammeter). Current through its coil makes the nail a magnet that picks up paper clips: more current or more turns, stronger, until the iron is fully magnetized; no current, it lets them go. Current in at + makes its point a north pole; swap the leads to swap the poles. Facts: 50 turns · 0.045 Ω · iron core.

### coil — Coil of wire · static (fixed in place)
A coil of enamelled copper wire on a cardboard tube (200 turns, 4 cm bore), held in a clamp, with two leads. Move a magnet in or out of it, or drop one through it, and a voltage is induced while the magnet moves (none while it is still): a galvanometer wired to it flicks one way as the magnet goes in and the other way as it comes out. Faster, a stronger magnet or more turns: more voltage. Facts: 200 turns · 4 cm bore · 6 Ω.

### straight-wire — Straight wire · static (fixed in place)
A bare copper wire stretched straight between two insulated clamps, with a terminal at each end. Current through it makes a magnetic field round it (Oersted): a compass needle behind it swings across the wire when the current flows, the other way when the current is reversed, back when it stops. Its field 1 cm away is 20 µT per amp (Earth's is about 20 µT), so it takes amps: a battery straight across it (briefly) or through a few ohms. Facts: 30 cm · 14 AWG copper · 20 µT/A at 1 cm.

An upright pegboard behind the circuit, facing you, so a circuit reads at a glance: put parts on it with Stands on: board (they stay where they are put) and wire them in a loop. Facts: 60 x 40 cm.

mod_energy.title: Energy devices: paper windmills (pinwheels) and model wind turbines in a fan's wind, generators lighting LEDs, windmills and waterwheels winding up loads, battery cars
mod_energy.text:
### Energy devices: paper windmills (pinwheels) and model wind turbines in a fan's wind, generators lighting LEDs, windmills and waterwheels winding up loads, battery cars
Devices that turn one form of energy into another (4-PS3-4). pinwheel (a paper windmill: its sails on a straw axle through a wooden post; anchor: the middle of its foot's bottom: place {on: "table", x}) and wind-turbine (a classroom model turbine: a round wooden base with + and − terminals, an aluminium tower, a nacelle holding a KidWind generator, a crimping hub of `blades` flat blades `blade_length` × `blade_width` at `pitch`; anchor: the middle of its base's bottom: place {on: "table", x}). Their rotors FACE THE WIND along the table: `facing` left means the wind must come from the left (a fan on its left blowing right; a breeze "to the right"). Their shaft is `height` above the table (pinwheel 0.3 m, turbine 0.45 m): give it the fan's middle height. A fan standing on the table (place {on: "table", x}) has its middle diameter/2 + 6.5 cm up (a 40 cm fan: 0.265 m, a 50 cm fan: 0.315 m) and blows a round jet 0.9 × its diameter across, full speed for about 6 diameters: put the rotor 30-60 cm from the fan's face, its sails or blades inside the jet (the outer parts of a rotor wider than the jet get little wind; a breeze item gives the whole table the same wind). `yaw` 20-35° turns the rotor's face toward the viewer (much clearer in the picture) at a cost: it takes the wind's share along its shaft (cos of the angle), about cos² less torque. Numbers (blade-element momentum with flat blades; the KidWind generator's measured 2.13 V at 720 rpm and 38 Ω): a 20 cm paper windmill turns about 1200 rpm free in a 4 m/s wind and 1500 in 5 m/s (its sail tips about 3 times the wind's speed); a model turbine (3 blades × 15 cm at 20°) in a 5 m/s breeze about 900 rpm free, about 700 rpm in front of a 50 cm fan at 5 m/s, giving 1.9 V: a red LED needs about 1.8 V (650-700 rpm) and lights dimly there, brightly with a 6 m/s fan; pitch 10-30° turns best (45° turns slowly, 0° not at all); more blades give more torque at low speed. Wire a turbine's generator like a battery: its + (right terminal) to the LED's + and the LED's − back to its − (current goes out of +). A paper windmill's sails are too weak to turn a generator fast enough to light an LED (its point: a turbine needs a strong rotor). Lifting a load (the windmill-winch challenge): `load_g` on a pinwheel or turbine is a paper cup of pennies (3 g + 2.5 g a penny) on a thread wound on its straw or shaft (`axle_mm` across: a skewer 3 mm, a straw 6 mm, a cotton reel 25 mm): the cup starts on the table under the axle's downwind end and is wound up until 2.2 cm under it, where it holds the rotor still (a turbine that must light an LED takes no load_g); the rotor stops when the cup's torque, load × g × axle radius, passes what its sails give at a standstill (a 20 cm windmill in a 4 m/s breeze lifts at most about 50 g on a 6 mm straw: twice as much on a 3 mm skewer, at half the speed). A waterwheel (flow module) takes `load_g` too: a cup hung under it from a spool on its axle (`axle_mm` 12; `winds` auto: the way the stream turns it); a 140 mL/s tap lifts up to about 350 g on the 12 mm spool (about twice that on a 6 mm one, more slowly); a heavier cup, hanging under the wheel from the start, pulls it backward and falls. Goals: rises {item} (mechanics: its cup ends 5 cm higher), lifts_higher {a, b}. Readings lift_m (how far the cup rose), pull_n (the thread's pull). generator (a small DC generator on a little base with + and − terminals; it touches nothing: place {on: "table", x} beside the machine): link `shaft` to a waterwheel, paper windmill, wind turbine or wheel-and-axle; `ratio` steps it up through a belt (a waterwheel under a 140 mL/s tap turns about 140 rpm: ratio 5 brings the generator to about 700 rpm, enough for an LED); `kind` KidWind generator (2.1 V at 720 rpm, 38 Ω) or hobby motor (a tenth of that). Its + is positive while the shaft turns COUNTER-clockwise as seen: a waterwheel with its stream on the RIGHT turns clockwise, so set leads "swapped" (or wire the LED the other way round). Readings rpm, voltage, current. Battery car (circuits module): a cart, toy-car or truck on the table; a battery on it (place {on: <the car>}); a motor {kind: "geared", drives: "wheels", car: <the car's id>} (it rides on the car over its rear axle: where the motor item itself is placed does not matter); wires battery + → motor + and motor − → battery − (that way round it drives forward, to the right; swapped, backward). Two AA cells and the geared (48:1 "TT") motor drive a cart at about 0.3 m/s (its wheels spin a little at the start); a hobby motor without gears accelerates slowly to far higher speeds. Goal: moves {item: <the car>, min_m}; the motor's rpm, current and voltage are readings. Goals of this module: generates {item, at_least_v?, at_least_mw?} (a turbine's or a small generator's voltage over the run's last 0.5 s; default at least 1 V), generates_more {a, b} (generator a's electrical power more than b's: a fair test of blades), lifts_higher {a, b}. Also: lights {item: an LED or bulb} (circuits), spins / turns {item, at_least_rpm} on a windmill, turbine or generator (it reads rpm), rises {item} (mechanics). Let the rotor spin up: seconds 5-8 for a turbine (it takes 2-4 s to reach its speed).
  - goal generates {item, at_least_v?, at_least_mw?}: a wind turbine's or a small generator's voltage (its size) is at least at_least_v (default 1 V) all through the run's last 0.5 s, and with at_least_mw its electrical power at least that
  - goal generates_more {a, b}: generator a's (a turbine's, a small generator's) electrical power over the run's last 0.5 s is more than b's, by at least 10 % and 0.1 mW: a fair test of blade designs (the same wind, the same load)
  - goal lifts_higher {a, b}: machine a's cup (a windmill's, a turbine's or a waterwheel's load_g) ends higher above where it started than b's, by at least 2 cm and 10 % (a fair test: more sails, a thinner axle, a stronger wind; in a short run, the faster lift)
  - knob pinwheel.pitch: the sails' angle to the wind: about 15-20° turns fastest; steeper sails start harder but turn slower
  - knob pinwheel.diameter: a bigger windmill catches more wind: its torque grows with the cube of its size
  - knob pinwheel.blades: cut from one square, more sails are narrower: a little more starting torque
  - knob pinwheel.load_g: the cup's weight times the straw's radius must be less than the sails' torque, or the windmill stalls
  - knob pinwheel.axle_mm: a thinner axle lifts a heavier cup (less torque for the same weight) but winds in less thread a turn
  - knob pinwheel.yaw: turned away from the wind it meets only the wind's share along its axle: less torque, slower
  - knob pinwheel.height: its sails must be in the fan's jet: the axle at the fan's middle height
  - knob wind-turbine.pitch: pitch 10-30° turns best: steeper blades start strongly but turn slowly; flatter ones turn fast once going but start weakly
  - knob wind-turbine.blade_length: longer blades sweep more wind (its power grows with the area it sweeps), if the wind reaches their tips
  - knob wind-turbine.blades: more blades: more torque at low speed (they start and lift more), a little lower top speed
  - knob wind-turbine.yaw: turned away from the wind it meets only the wind's share along its shaft: less torque, slower, a lower voltage
  - knob wind-turbine.height: its blades must be in the fan's jet: the hub at the fan's middle height
  - knob wind-turbine.load_g: the cup's weight times the spool's radius must be less than the blades' torque
  - knob wind-turbine.generator: the KidWind generator gives about 2 V at 700 rpm; a hobby motor a tenth of that (not enough for an LED)
  - knob generator.ratio: its voltage grows with how fast it turns: a slow waterwheel needs a step-up (ratio 5: 140 rpm → 700 rpm) to light an LED, but the shaft feels the generator's drag ratio times as much
  - knob generator.leads: its + is positive only while its shaft turns counter-clockwise (normal): a clockwise wheel needs its leads swapped, or an LED stays dark
  - knob generator.kind: the KidWind generator gives about ten times the voltage of a hobby motor at the same speed
  - knob waterwheel.load_g: the stream's push on the paddles must beat the cup's weight on its spool
  - knob waterwheel.axle_mm: a thinner spool lifts a heavier cup but more slowly
  - e.g. "A paper windmill lifts a cup of pennies in a fan's wind.": a fan {speed 5, diameter 0.4} standing on the table, a pinwheel {height 0.27 (the fan's middle), facing left, yaw 30, load_g 13 (a cup of 4 pennies)} 45 cm to its right; the cup is wound up on the straw; goal rises {item: windmill}
  - e.g. "A wind turbine in front of a fan lights an LED.": a fan {speed 6, diameter 0.4} standing on the table; a wind-turbine {height 0.27, facing left, yaw 25} 45 cm to its right; an LED on the table to its right, wired turbine + → LED +, LED − → turbine −; seconds 7 (the rotor spins up for 2-4 s); goal lights {item: led}
  - e.g. "Fair test: do blades at 20° or at 45° make more electricity?": a breeze {speed 5} at the table's left end; two wind-turbines the same but for pitch (20 and 45), far apart, each with a 50 Ω resistor wired across its terminals; seconds 8; goal generates_more {a: the 20° turbine, b: the 45° one}
  - e.g. "A waterwheel lifts a cup of pennies.": a waterwheel {load_g 50} with its axle in the air 45 cm up, a tap {flow_ml_s 140} over the right side of its paddles (x offset 0.35 × its diameter), a bucket under it; the stream turns it clockwise and its spool winds the cup up; goal rises {item: wheel}
  - e.g. "A waterwheel turns a generator that lights an LED.": a waterwheel (axle 45 cm up) under a tap {flow_ml_s 140} on its right, a bucket below; a generator {shaft: wheel, ratio 5, leads swapped (the wheel turns clockwise)} on the table to its left, an LED beyond it, wired generator + → LED +, LED − → generator −; goal lights {item: led}
  - e.g. "Build a battery car that drives across the table.": a cart on the table, a battery (2 AA) placed on the cart, a motor {kind geared, drives wheels, car: cart} (it rides over the cart's rear axle), wires battery + → motor +, motor − → battery −; it drives right at about 0.3 m/s; goal moves {item: cart, min_m 0.3}
### pinwheel — Paper windmill · static (fixed in place)
A paper windmill (a pinwheel) on a straw axle through a wooden post, its sails facing the wind: a fan's or a breeze's wind turns it, and a thread tied to the straw can wind up a paper cup of pennies (the windmill-winch challenge). Facts: 20 cm · 4 sails · lifts about 60 g in a 4 m/s wind on a 6 mm straw.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its foot's bottom. Outline at defaults: 0.15 × 0.32 m; from the anchor x −0.05…+0.1, y +0…+0.32.
Props: diameter: m =0.2 [0.1…0.4]; blades: int =4 [2…8]; pitch: ° =18 [5…45]; paper: *copy paper* | card | plastic sheet; height: m =0.3 [0.12…0.6]; facing: *left* | right; yaw: ° =0 [0…60]; load_g: g =0 [0…500]; axle_mm: mm =6 [2…30].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): rpm (Turning, rpm), wind_ms (Wind on it, m/s), tsr (Tip speed ÷ wind), power_mw (Power from the wind, mW), lift_m (Load lifted, m), pull_n (Thread pulls, N).
Notes: has a hinged part, pin joints; also called: pinwheel, windmill, paper windmill, wind, windmill winch, lift, energy, wind energy, sails, turns.
### wind-turbine — Model wind turbine · static (fixed in place)
A classroom wind turbine: blades on a hub, a nacelle with a small generator on an aluminium tower, its leads on the base's + and − terminals. In front of a fan (or in a breeze) it turns, and its generator can light an LED wired to it; a spool on its shaft can lift a cup of pennies. Facts: 3 blades × 15 cm at 20° · KidWind generator · about 2 V in a 5 m/s fan.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its base's bottom. Outline at defaults: 0.21 × 0.472 m; from the anchor x −0.08…+0.13, y +0…+0.472.
Props: blades: int =3 [2…12]; blade_length: m =0.15 [0.05…0.3]; blade_width: m =0.06 [0.02…0.12]; pitch: ° =20 [0…60]; blade_material: *corrugated plastic* | cardboard | balsa; height: m =0.45 [0.2…1.2]; facing: *left* | right; yaw: ° =0 [0…60]; generator: *KidWind generator* | hobby motor | none; load_g: g =0 [0…2000]; axle_mm: mm =6 [2…40].

A small DC generator (the KidWind turbine generator, or a hobby motor) on a little base with + and − terminals. Link it to a turning shaft (a waterwheel, a windmill, a wheel and axle): its voltage grows with how fast it turns, and the current it gives holds the shaft back.
