  - knob bar-magnet.flip: like poles push apart and unlike poles pull together; iron and steel are pulled by either pole, so flipping changes nothing for a clip
  - knob horseshoe-magnet.flip: like poles push apart and unlike poles pull together; iron and steel are pulled by either pole, so flipping changes nothing for a clip
  - knob disc-magnet.flip: like poles push apart and unlike poles pull together; iron and steel are pulled by either pole, so flipping changes nothing for a clip
  - knob magnet-cart.flip: like poles push apart and unlike poles pull together; iron and steel are pulled by either pole, so flipping changes nothing for a clip
  - knob battery-electromagnet.flip: like poles push apart and unlike poles pull together; iron and steel are pulled by either pole, so flipping changes nothing for a clip
  - knob bar-magnet.length: it grows or shrinks about its middle: a longer bar's ends reach farther out (nearer what lies beyond them), and its far pole is farther away, so the near pole's pull is less cancelled
  - knob bar-magnet.width: a bigger pole face carries more pole strength: it pulls harder and reaches farther
  - knob bar-magnet.depth: a bigger pole face carries more pole strength: it pulls harder and reaches farther
  - knob disc-magnet.diameter: a bigger disc has a bigger pole face: a stronger, longer-reaching pull
  - knob ring-magnets.alternate: like faces together push the rings apart so they float; unlike faces pull them together into a stack
  - knob ring-magnets.thickness: thicker rings are stronger and heavier: the gaps change a little
  - knob magnet-cart.magnet_end: the magnet must be at the end facing the other cart to push or pull it
  - knob battery-electromagnet.turns: the coil's field grows with its turns (with few turns the batteries' own resistance keeps the current near 6 A): more turns, a stronger magnet, until the nail's iron is full
  - knob battery-electromagnet.cells: another cell adds 1.5 V but also its own 0.2 Ω: with a short coil the current hardly rises; with a long coil it does
  - knob battery-electromagnet.on: with no current the nail is only soft iron: it pulls nothing
  - knob balloon.rubbed: each stroke adds 10 nC up to 10 strokes (100 nC); the pull on a neutral scrap grows as the charge squared, between charges as their product
  - knob balloon.rubbed_side: the charge stays where it was rubbed: that side must face what it should pull or push
  - knob balloon.thread: a longer thread lets a hung balloon swing farther for the same push
  - knob balloon.y: a scrap's pull falls off about as the fifth power of the distance to the charge: hung a few millimetres lower, a weakly rubbed balloon lifts what it could not
  - knob charged-rod.y: held a few millimetres nearer, a weakly rubbed rod pulls much harder (the pull on a neutral thing falls off about as the fifth power of the distance)
  - knob paper-bits.paper: tissue paper (17 g/m²) is about 5 times lighter than printer paper (80 g/m²) and pulled about as hard (a damp scrap is pulled as a conducting flake of its size): it jumps with about half the charge
  - knob paper-bits.size: a conducting flake's pull grows about as its size cubed and its weight as its size squared: a bigger scrap is pulled more for its weight (3 mm scraps need about 1.4 times the charge 6 mm ones do)
  - knob charged-rod.rubbed: each stroke adds 7 nC on its rubbed half, up to 10 strokes
  - knob charged-rod.material: plastic rubbed with wool goes negative, glass rubbed with silk positive: it flips the charge
  - knob clip-on-thread.thread: the thread sets how far below the magnet the clip hangs: nearer, the pull is much stronger
  - knob barrier-sheet.material: a steel sheet takes the magnet's field into itself: it blocks most of a ceramic magnet's pull (88 % 8 mm from the pole), about half a neodymium one's (it saturates); paper, cardboard, plastic, glass and aluminium let the pull straight through
  - knob compass.north: with no magnet near, the needle points along the Earth's field (north)
  - knob can-on-side.material: a steel can is pulled by a magnet, an aluminium one is not (a charged balloon pulls both)
  - e.g. "A paper clip jumps up to a bar magnet held just above it (G1).": bar-magnet fixed, pole down (place on air, angle_deg -90), its bottom 1 cm above a paper-clip on the table (ceramic; up to 2 cm neodymium); goals lifts {source: magnet, item: clip} + sticks {item: clip, to: magnet}
  - e.g. "Two magnet carts with like poles facing push apart without touching (G2).": two magnet-cart on the table 30 cm apart (middles), A's magnet at its front, B's at its back with flip true, so north faces north; goal repels {a, b}
  - e.g. "Which things does a magnet pick up? A steel clip, a plastic clip, a foil ball and a nail (G3).": one fixed neodymium bar-magnet (length 0.1) on the table per test object, each object 2-3 cm past its pole; goals attracts {source, item} for the steel clip and the nail, not_attracted {source, item} for the plastic clip and the foil ball
  - e.g. "A magnet pulls a clip through a piece of cardboard (G4).": fixed neodymium bar-magnet on the table, a barrier-sheet (cardboard) standing just past its pole, a paper-clip on the far side of the sheet; goal sticks {item: clip, to: sheet} (it is pulled up against the sheet)
  - e.g. "Two magnet carts with unlike poles facing roll together and stick (G2).": two magnet-cart on the table 30 cm apart, A's magnet at its front, B's at its back, no flip (north faces south); goal attracts {source: a, item: b}
  - e.g. "A paper clip on a thread floats under a magnet without touching it (G5).": clip-on-thread (thread 0.1) on the table, a fixed neodymium bar-magnet pole down (angle_deg -90) with its bottom about 1-2 cm above where the clip's top reaches; goal levitates {item: clip}
  - e.g. "Ring magnets float above each other on a pencil (G6).": one ring-magnets item (count 3, alternate true: like faces together) on the table; goal levitates {item: rings}
  - e.g. "A compass points north, but near a bar magnet it turns (G7).": fixed bar-magnet lying on the table, one compass in the air 9 cm above its middle and another far away (1.5 m); goals points {compass: near, angle_deg: 180} (over the bar its field runs north to south pole: right to left) and points {compass: far, angle_deg: 0} (Earth's north, to the right)
  - e.g. "More turns of wire make an electromagnet hold more paper clips (MS-PS2-3).": battery-electromagnet copies 1 m apart (turns 10 and 200), each with a chain paper-clip (count 6, spacing 0.0345, held, angle_deg -90) hanging from its point (place y_m 0.244 and 0.11425); seconds 3, release 0.4; goal holds {magnet: strong, count: 2, items: [chainB]} (items always a list, even of one chain)
  - e.g. "A rubbed balloon picks up little bits of paper (G11).": balloon rubbed 10 on its bottom, on a 30 cm thread, its lowest point about 8 mm above paper-bits (count 5) on the table; goal attracts {source: balloon, item: bits}
  - e.g. "Two rubbed balloons hanging side by side push each other apart (G12).": two balloons rubbed 10 hung 30 cm apart, rubbed sides facing (right and left); goal repels {a: b1, b: b2}
  - e.g. "A charged balloon rolls an empty soda can toward it without touching (G13).": balloon rubbed 10 on its lower right, hung so its rubbed side is 3-4 cm from a can-on-side (aluminium) on the table; goal attracts {source: balloon, item: can}
  - e.g. "Only the rubbed balloon picks up paper; the balloon that was not rubbed does nothing (G11 with a control).": two balloons on 30 cm threads 1 m apart, one rubbed 10 on its bottom and one not rubbed, each 8 mm above its own paper-bits; goals attracts {source: rubbed, item: bits1} and not_attracted {source: plain, item: bits2}

mod_matter.text:
### Matter: particles, states, dissolving, mixtures, conservation of mass, chemical reactions (cold packs, hand warmers, indicators, precipitates, rusting), molecules and crystals
Particle model: particle-box (a clear box on a hot plate) shows a substance (water, wax, iron, gallium, carbon dioxide, air, nitrogen, helium, bromine) as particles: solid (bonded, vibrating), liquid (sliding at the bottom), gas (filling the box). They are a MODEL (drawn huge, moving 1/1250 of the real speed); the readings are real: temp_c, solid/liquid/gas %, pressure_kpa, volume_ml, speed_ms (mean molecular speed √(8RT/πM): air at 20 °C 463 m/s). temp_c sets the start; heater_w heats it (W into a sample of sample_g grams: 1 g of ice at −20 °C needs 42 J to 0 °C, 334 J to melt, 418 J to 100 °C, 2257 J to boil; a 20 W heater with time_lapse 60 does it all in about 2.5 s of run). piston (with load_kg on piston_area_cm2) holds the gas up: more load → smaller volume (Boyle), hotter → bigger (Charles). divider + second (another gas, or 'none' for the same one in two colours) lifted at open_at_s: the gases mix (mixed_pct). The box's readings are the real sample's: pressure_kpa is its gas's nRT/V (exact Boyle and Charles); a loaded piston's volume_ml goes to nRT/P (the drawn piston stops where the drawn particles fill it). A sample can be no denser than its solid or liquid (more is cut, with a warning); a gas squeezed past its vapour pressure gets an event (a real one would partly condense). Mixing (mixed_pct) runs on a MODEL clock: a few run seconds whatever the time-lapse (real gases take about L²/2D: a 20 cm box half an hour): say so. Heating curve plateau: goal holds_at {item: box, temp_c: 0, while: melting} (or 100, boiling). syringe: 60 mL sealed syringe of air whose plunger is pushed from start_ml to push_to_ml (60 → 30 mL: 101 → 203 kPa, exactly 6080 ÷ V; force_n: the push to hold it, 57 N at 30 mL, 284 N at 10 mL, 624 N at 5 mL: past 200 N more than a hand gives, warned). In a vacuum (settings.air false) nothing presses from outside: a balloon closure is not buoyed, a loaded piston carries its load only; an evaporating-dish refuses to run (water boils and freezes there: not modelled). balloon-bath: a 1 L balloon dipped into water at water_temp_c: its volume follows the kelvin temperature (60 °C: 1.136 L; 0 °C: 0.932 L), settling over settle_s lesson seconds. Dissolving: dissolving-glass is a 7 cm glass of water_ml at water_temp_c with solute (salt, sugar dissolve; sand, chalk do not) of solute_g and grain (salt: table/coarse/powder; sugar: granulated/coarse/powder/cube), poured at pour_at_s from a spoon (start_in 'spoon'), from a paper cup beside it ('dish': weighed all along) or already on the bottom ('glass'); stir turns/s from stir_from_s. Faster when hotter, stirred, finer. Saturation: at 20 °C 100 g of water holds 35.9 g of salt or 204 g of sugar; more stays on the bottom. Real times: table salt stirred about 10-30 s; unstirred salt and a sugar cube take minutes: use the scene setting time_lapse (e.g. 30-60) so the run shows them; readings dissolved_g, left_g, saturated, clock_s (lesson seconds). Conservation of mass: stand things on measure's kitchen-scale (its platform's top is 2.6 cm above where the scale stands; it weighs every MOVING item resting on it, stacked included) and compare its grams reading before and after (goal mass_same {scale} / mass_changes {scale, by_g}). Items: dissolving-glass (start_in 'dish' or 'glass': 'spoon' adds the solute's mass when it pours), chocolate-bar (snapped into pieces at snap_at_s), zip-bag (put an ice cube INSIDE it with place {inside: bag}: what melts stays in the bag; ice melts with heat on: a warm room_temp and time_lapse 600), reaction-bottle (baking soda + vinegar; closure open: the CO2 escapes, the scale goes down by co2_g (5 g soda → 2.62 g); cap: no change (the vinegar dissolves part of the gas, co2_dissolved_g, Henry's law; past 900 kPa, e.g. 30 g of soda in 400 mL of 10 % vinegar, the cap POPS (popped, an event) and the gas escapes: the scale goes down); balloon: the balloon fills and the scale reads 1.6 g LESS (buoyancy)), pumped-ball (air has mass: 0 → 0.8 bar adds 5.4 g). Kitchen scale and fixed items: static items are not weighed, so weighed things must be moving items. Mixtures: mixture-dish (sand + iron filings, salt + pepper, rice + beans, sand + paper clips, sand + gravel, sand + salt) has its own magnet wand (wand: true, the default): from wand_from_s it sweeps across with its tip wand_height (1.5 cm) above the dish's floor and lifts out with the iron stuck to it; the sand stays (readings a_out_g/a_left_pct: the iron taken out). Or set wand false and its magnet link to a magnet item held (fixed) just above the dish's rim (a ceramic magnet must come within about 1-2 cm, a neodymium one 3-5 cm). sieve: a mixture in a shaken sieve over a tray: grains smaller than aperture_mm fall through (sand 2 mm through a 4 mm mesh; gravel 7 mm kept). Filtering: filter-funnel (a ring stand, a 75 mm glass funnel lined with filter paper, a beaker under it; a fixed setup standing on the table): a cup of water_ml with solid_g of an undissolved solid (sand; chalk) and dissolved_g of salt or sugar dissolved is poured in at pour_at_s; the water and the dissolved salt run through into the beaker (filtrate_ml, salt_through_g), the sand stays on the paper (kept_g, kept_pct); the paper choice decides what is kept (filter paper 11 µm; coffee filter 20 µm: faster but chalk gets through; none: nothing kept); rinse_ml of clean water after it carries the salt the wet paper held. It takes minutes (100 mL through filter paper: about 20 lesson minutes): time_lapse 100-200 and 10-14 s of run. Evaporating: evaporating-dish (a 9 cm glass dish of water_ml of water with solute_g of salt or sugar; heat 'hot plate' (its own hot plate under it, heater_w: 50 mL boils dry in about 17 min at 300 W), 'sun' (a sunny windowsill: about 3 days) or 'room' (about 11 days)): the water evaporates or boils away and the salt stays: crystals appear once it is saturated and at the end all of it is left (crystals_g); a moving item: on a kitchen-scale the reading falls by the water's mass only. Use time_lapse (hot plate 150; sun or room 100000). Density: density-cube (1 inch cubes of a material: same size, different mass) and equal-mass-block (same mass, size from density); with fluids' water-tank they float or sink by density (below 0.998 g/cm³ floats). Chemical changes (each a moving item a kitchen-scale weighs; with the heat module its temperature is a heat body (a pouch, a pad) or its beaker's water, so a thermometer whose tip touches it (a fixed, upright digital probe placed on it) or stands in the beaker (place inside: it, fixed) reads it; temp_c is its own reading): cold-pack (an instant cold pack lying flat: chemical ammonium nitrate, urea, ammonium chloride (cold) or calcium chloride (a HOT pack); salt_g in a water_ml bag burst at squeeze_at_s, dissolving over dissolve_s lesson s: 30 g of ammonium nitrate in 100 mL goes from 20 °C to about 2 °C (change_c −20 if no heat came in), 30 g of calcium chloride to about 64 °C; time_lapse 30, 8 s; its mass never changes); hand-warmer (iron_g of iron powder rusting from open_at_s, lasting lasts_h: about 8 W, on a table 20 → about 40 °C over 10-15 minutes (time_lapse 120); it GAINS the oxygen's mass, +8.6 g over its life (time_lapse 3600)); steel-wool (wool_g soaked in vinegar/salt water/water/dry rusts over days: rust_pct, gained_g (half of 5 g: +1.07 g), oxygen_ml; time_lapse 86400 = a day per run second; it turns orange-brown); indicator-cup (a beaker of purple red cabbage juice; add vinegar/lemon juice (mL) or baking soda/washing soda (g) at add_at_s, then_add a second at then_at_s: pH by real chemistry, colour band red < 3, pink < 5, purple < 7.5, blue < 9, blue-green < 10.5, green < 12.5, yellow; 10 mL vinegar → pH 2.9 red; 2 g baking soda → 8.3 blue; washing soda → green; soda after vinegar fizzes CO2 (escaped_g) and turns it back; it cools a little); reaction-cup (calcium chloride poured into baking soda solution at mix_at_s: it warms (+6 °C for 5 g + 5 g), turns cloudy white (a precipitate: chalk, solid_g 2.98 g, settling over minutes) and fizzes off carbon dioxide (the scale goes down by escaped_g, 1.15 g): three signs of a chemical change). Goals: warms_by {item, at_least_c} / cools_by {item, at_least_c} (its peak against its start; item a pack, a beaker or a thermometer), color_changes {item, to?} (an indicator's colour band; a precipitate's clear → cloudy white; steel wool's grey → orange-brown), mass_changes / mass_same {scale} for the mass. Models of particles: molecule (molecule water (bent 104.5°), carbon dioxide (straight), methane (tetrahedral), ammonia (pyramid), oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen; style ball-and-stick or space-filling; scale_cm cm per ångström, 2.5; labels: its formula and name over it) and crystal (lattice salt: Na+ and Cl− ions in a cube pattern, (2·cells+1)³ ions; diamond: carbon bonded to four; ice: water in open hexagons held by hydrogen bonds; cells 1-4 repeats a side; scale_cm 1.2). Both rest on the table (place on: table); CPK colours (H white, C black, N blue, O red, Na purple, Cl green); readings atoms, bonds, mass_u, bond_angle_deg / sodium, chloride, carbon, oxygen, hydrogen counts. They are MODELS: say so.
  - goal dissolves {item: a dissolving-glass, before_s?}: everything put into it dissolves (by before_s run seconds if given)
  - goal dissolves_first {a, b}: glass a's crystals are all dissolved before glass b's (if neither finishes: a has dissolved the larger share at the end)
  - goal saturates {item: a dissolving-glass}: at the end its water holds all it can and crystals are left on the bottom
  - goal mass_same {scale: a kitchen-scale, tol_g?}: the scale reads the same (within tol_g, default 1 g) at rest just after the release and at the end
  - goal mass_changes {scale, by_g, tol_g?}: the scale's reading at the end differs from its reading at rest after the release by by_g (negative: down) within tol_g (default 0.2 g or a tenth of by_g)
  - goal state {item: a particle-box, is: solid|liquid|gas|melting|boiling}: the sample's state at the end
  - goal holds_at {item, temp_c, while: melting|boiling, tol_c?}: a heating curve's plateau: while the item melts (boils) its temperature stays at temp_c within tol_c (default 0.5 °C), and it does melt (boil) for at least two frames: a particle-box's sample (water 0 °C melting, 100 °C boiling), heat's ice-cube or meltable (melting), a saucepan's, kettle's or evaporating-dish's water (boiling)
  - goal mixes {item: a particle-box with a divider, at_least?}: its two sides end mixed at least at_least % (default 80); the box mixes on a MODEL clock (a few run seconds whatever the time-lapse): never claim real minutes from it
  - goal pressure {item: a particle-box or syringe, kpa, tol_kpa?}: its gauge reads kpa (within tol_kpa, default 10 %) at the end (mean of the last 1 s); the reading is the real gas's nRT/V (a syringe: exactly 6080 ÷ V mL)
  - goal volume {item: a particle-box, syringe or balloon-bath, ml, tol_ml?}: the gas's volume at the end is ml (within tol_ml, default 5 %)
  - goal separates {item: a sieve, mixture-dish or filter-funnel}: the mixture is separated: through a sieve ≥ 95 % of the small part and ≤ 5 % of the big; out of a dish by its magnet ≥ 90 % of the iron and ≤ 5 % of the rest; in a filter funnel ≥ 95 % of the undissolved solid kept on the paper and ≥ 80 % of the water through
  - goal crystallizes {item: an evaporating-dish, g?, tol_g?}: at the end it holds g grams of crystals (default: all that was dissolved in it) within tol_g (default 2 %, at least 0.05 g)
  - goal warms_by {item: a hand-warmer, a hot pack, a reaction-cup, a thermometer or anything with a temperature, at_least_c}: its temperature rises at least at_least_c above where it starts (its highest against its first)
  - goal cools_by {item: a cold-pack, an indicator-cup, a thermometer or anything with a temperature, at_least_c}: its temperature falls at least at_least_c below where it starts (its lowest against its first)
  - goal color_changes {item, to?}: its colour changes: an indicator-cup's colour is at some moment another than at the start (to: and it ends red, pink, purple, blue, blue-green, green or yellow); a reaction-cup goes from clear to cloudy white (to: white); steel-wool rusts orange-brown, 5 % or more (to: brown)
  - knob dissolving-glass.water_temp_c: warmer water dissolves faster (sugar about 3× from 20 to 60 °C) and holds a little more
  - knob dissolving-glass.stir: stirring sweeps the brine off the crystals: unstirred salt stalls in its own brine on the bottom
  - knob dissolving-glass.grain: smaller pieces have more surface for their mass: powder fastest, a cube slowest
  - knob dissolving-glass.solute_g: more than the water can hold (35.9 g salt per 100 g at 20 °C) stays undissolved
  - knob dissolving-glass.water_ml: more water holds more before it saturates
  - knob particle-box.heater_w: the heat put in (power × time × time_lapse) over the sample's mass decides how far it gets along the heating curve
  - knob particle-box.temp_c: the start temperature: hotter particles move faster; past the melting or boiling point it starts liquid or gas
  - knob particle-box.sample_g: a smaller sample warms, melts and boils sooner with the same heater
  - knob particle-box.load_kg: more load on the piston squeezes the gas smaller (Boyle)
  - knob particle-box.open_at_s: the gases only mix once the divider is up
  - knob syringe.push_to_ml: half the volume doubles the pressure (Boyle); holding it further in takes more push (284 N at 10 mL, 624 N at 5 mL)
  - knob balloon-bath.water_temp_c: the balloon's volume follows its air's kelvin temperature
  - knob reaction-bottle.soda_g: the gas made is the soda's 44/84 of its mass while the vinegar's acid lasts; capped, the pressure rises with it and past 900 kPa the cap pops off (the gas then escapes): less soda keeps it on
  - knob reaction-bottle.react_s: the fizz's time: most of the gas comes off in three times it
  - knob reaction-bottle.closure: open: the gas escapes (scale down); cap: stays (no change); balloon: buoyed (scale a little down). Never change it when it is what the lesson compares
  - knob sieve.aperture_mm: only grains smaller than the holes pass: the holes must be between the two sizes
  - knob sieve.shake_until_s: shaking longer lets the last small grains through
  - knob sieve.shake_mm: a stronger shake stirs the heap so small grains reach the mesh
  - knob mixture-dish.wand_height: a magnet's pull falls off steeply with distance: the wand's tip must pass within about 1 cm of the iron
  - knob mixture-dish.wand_s: a slower sweep gives the filings time to jump up to the tip
  - knob mixture-dish.magnet (a link): only the linked magnet pulls: a stronger one (neodymium) or a nearer one takes more iron
  - knob filter-funnel.funnel_mm: a bigger funnel holds more of the mixture at a time above the paper, so it is all poured and through sooner
  - knob filter-funnel.rinse_ml: the wet paper and the sand hold a few mL of the salty water: a rinse of clean water carries its salt through
  - knob filter-funnel.paper: filter paper keeps grains over 11 µm; a coffee filter runs about 3 times faster but lets chalk through; no paper keeps nothing. Never change it when it is what the lesson compares
  - knob filter-funnel.water_temp_c: warm water is less viscous: it runs through the paper faster (twice as fast at 50 °C as at 20 °C)
  - knob filter-funnel.pour_s: the pourer waits whenever the funnel is full, so pouring faster only helps while there is room above the paper
  - knob evaporating-dish.heater_w: about half the hot plate's power reaches the dish: 300 W boils 50 mL dry in about 17 minutes
  - knob evaporating-dish.water_ml: less water is gone sooner (the salt left is the same)
  - knob evaporating-dish.humidity_pct: drier air takes the water faster (in a room or the sun; a boiling dish does not care)
  - knob evaporating-dish.heat: a hot plate boils it dry in minutes, the sun takes days, a room about 11 days. Never change it when it is what the lesson compares
  - knob pumped-ball.end_bar: the air added is about 6.7 g per bar in a size-5 ball
  - knob chocolate-bar.snap_at_s: the scale must have settled before and after the snap
  - knob cold-pack.salt_g: the heat taken in (or given out) grows with the chemical: 30 g of ammonium nitrate in 100 mL cools it about 20 °C if no heat comes in
  - knob cold-pack.water_ml: less water to cool (or warm) makes a bigger change, as long as the water still dissolves it all
  - knob cold-pack.dissolve_s: dissolving faster gives the room less time to warm it back: its coldest is colder
  - knob cold-pack.chemical: ammonium nitrate cools most (25.7 kJ/mol), urea and ammonium chloride less; calcium chloride heats instead. Never change it when it is what the lesson compares
  - knob cold-pack.squeeze_at_s: it changes temperature only from the squeeze on: earlier leaves the run more time
  - knob hand-warmer.lasts_h: its power is its iron's heat over how long it lasts: half the time, twice the warmth
  - knob hand-warmer.iron_g: more iron gives out more heat for as long, and takes in more of the air's oxygen
  - knob hand-warmer.open_at_s: it warms only once air gets in
  - knob steel-wool.soaked: vinegar rusts it within a day, salt water about a day, plain water days, dry weeks. Never change it when it is what the lesson compares
  - knob steel-wool.wool_g: more iron rusting takes more oxygen: the scale gains more
  - knob indicator-cup.amount: more acid lowers the pH further (redder), more base raises it (bluer, greener)
  - knob indicator-cup.then_amount: the second addition must outweigh the first to turn the colour back: about 0.07 g of baking soda per mL of vinegar
  - knob indicator-cup.add: an acid (vinegar, lemon juice) turns red cabbage red or pink, a base (baking soda, washing soda) blue or green. Never change it when it is what the lesson compares
  - knob reaction-cup.cacl2_g: more calcium chloride warms it more as it dissolves and makes more white solid (while the baking soda lasts)
  - knob reaction-cup.soda_g: more baking soda makes more solid and gas (while the calcium chloride lasts)
  - knob reaction-cup.react_s: the white solid forms over about this many lesson seconds
  - e.g. "An instant cold pack: squeeze it and measure how cold it gets.": cold-pack (30 g ammonium nitrate, 100 mL) on the table, a digital thermometer held upright (fixed) with its tip on the pack; time_lapse 30, 8 s; goal cools_by {pack, at_least_c: 15}
  - e.g. "Which makes a colder pack: ammonium nitrate or calcium chloride? (MS-PS1-6)": two cold-packs side by side, chemical ammonium nitrate vs calcium chloride, same 30 g and 100 mL; time_lapse 30; goals cools_by {a, 15} and warms_by {b, 30}
  - e.g. "Open a hand warmer and watch it warm up over a few minutes.": hand-warmer on the table; time_lapse 120, 8 s (about 14 minutes); goal warms_by {hw, at_least_c: 15}
  - e.g. "Red cabbage juice: add vinegar, then baking soda.": indicator-cup add vinegar 10 mL at 1.2 s, then_add baking soda 3 g at 4 s; time_lapse 5, 7 s; goal color_changes {cup}
  - e.g. "Is it an acid or a base? Three cups of red cabbage juice: vinegar, water only, washing soda.": three indicator-cups: add vinegar 10 mL / none / washing soda 2 g; goals color_changes {a, to: red}, color_changes {c, to: green}
  - e.g. "Mix calcium chloride and baking soda solution: what signs of a chemical reaction do you see? (MS-PS1-2)": reaction-cup on a kitchen-scale; time_lapse 20, 6 s; goals color_changes {cup} (cloudy white), warms_by {cup, 3}, mass_changes {scale, by_g: −1.15}
  - e.g. "Steel wool rusts on a scale over a few days: does it get heavier?": steel-wool (5 g, vinegar) on a kitchen-scale; time_lapse 86400 (a run second is a day), 6 s; goals mass_changes {scale, by_g: 1.07} and color_changes {wool}
  - e.g. "Show models of a water molecule and a carbon dioxide molecule.": two molecule models on the table: molecule water and carbon dioxide (ball-and-stick); no goal
  - e.g. "A model of a salt crystal and of ice.": crystal lattice salt (cells 2) and crystal lattice ice on the table
  - e.g. "Show that mass stays the same when salt dissolves in water on a scale (X3).": kitchen-scale on the table; dissolving-glass (salt 10 g, start_in dish, stir 2) on it; time_lapse 10; goals dissolves {glass} + mass_same {scale}
  - e.g. "Does sugar dissolve faster in hot or cold water? Use sugar cubes (X5).": two dissolving-glass side by side, sugar grain cube, start_in glass, water_temp_c 60 vs 10; time_lapse 60; goal dissolves_first {a: hot, b: cold}
  - e.g. "Put 50 g of salt in 100 mL of water: not all of it dissolves (X4).": dissolving-glass solute_g 50, water_ml 100, stir 2; time_lapse 30; goal saturates {glass} (35.9 g dissolve at 20 °C)
  - e.g. "Snap a 100 g chocolate bar on a kitchen scale: does it still weigh 100 g? (X1)": chocolate-bar (snap_at_s 1.2) on a kitchen-scale; goal mass_same {scale}
  - e.g. "An ice cube melts in a sealed bag on a scale: the mass stays the same (X2).": zip-bag on a kitchen-scale, ice-cube place {inside: bag}; room_temp 25, time_lapse 900; goal mass_same {scale}
  - e.g. "Baking soda and vinegar in an open bottle and a capped bottle on two scales (X7).": a reaction-bottle (closure open) and one (closure cap), each on its own kitchen-scale, react_s 2 so the fizz is over by the end (most gas in 3 × react_s after mix_at_s); goals mass_changes {s1, by_g: −2.62} and mass_same {s2}
  - e.g. "Heat ice in the particle model until it boils away (X8).": particle-box water, temp_c −20, sample_g 1, heater_w 10, time_lapse 60, 10 s; goal state {box, is: gas}
  - e.g. "Heat ice in the particle model: show that the temperature stays at 0 °C while it melts and at 100 °C while it boils (the heating curve's plateaus).": particle-box water, temp_c −20, sample_g 1, heater_w 10, time_lapse 50, 10 s; goals holds_at {box, temp_c: 0, while: melting} and holds_at {box, temp_c: 100, while: boiling}
  - e.g. "Lift the divider between brown bromine gas and air and watch it spread (X9).": particle-box air with divider, second bromine, open_at_s 1; goal mixes {box}
  - e.g. "Push a sealed syringe from 60 mL to 30 mL: what happens to the pressure? (X12)": syringe start_ml 60, push_to_ml 30; goal pressure {syr, kpa: 203}
  - e.g. "A balloon dipped in hot water grows (Charles).": balloon-bath water_temp_c 60, time_lapse 20; goal volume {bath, ml: 1136}
  - e.g. "Separate gravel from sand with a sieve (X10).": sieve mixture sand + gravel, aperture_mm 4; goal separates {sieve}
  - e.g. "Pull the iron filings out of sand with a magnet (X10).": mixture-dish sand + iron filings (its magnet wand sweeps by itself); goal separates {dish}
  - e.g. "A bar magnet held over a dish of sand and paper clips picks out the clips.": an 8 cm mixture-dish of sand + paper clips, wand false, magnet: the bar-magnet's id; a neodymium bar-magnet (15 cm) stood upright (angle_deg 90), fixed in the air over the dish's middle with its lower end 3 cm above the table (y_m 0.105: its centre); goal separates {dish}
  - e.g. "Separate sand from salt water with a filter funnel: the sand stays on the paper and the salt water runs through (X10).": filter-funnel (sand 10 g, salt 5 g dissolved in 100 mL, filter paper, a 10 mL rinse); time_lapse 150, 12 s; goal separates {filter}
  - e.g. "Get the salt back from salt water by evaporating it on a hot plate (X10).": evaporating-dish (5 g salt in 50 mL, hot plate 300 W); time_lapse 150, 10 s; goals dries {dish} + crystallizes {dish}
  - e.g. "Leave a dish of salt water on a sunny windowsill for a few days: the water goes and the salt stays.": evaporating-dish (5 g salt in 50 mL) heat sun; time_lapse 100000 (a run second is about a day), 4 s; goals dries {dish} + crystallizes {dish}
  - e.g. "Pump up a ball on a scale: does air have mass? (X11)": pumped-ball (0 → 0.8 bar) on a kitchen-scale; goal mass_changes {scale, by_g: 5.4}
  - e.g. "Same-size cubes of different materials: which float in water? (density)": water-tank aquarium; density-cube made_of pine and made_of copper inside it; goals floats {pine}, sinks {copper}
### particle-box — Particle model box · static (fixed in place)
A clear box on a hot plate showing a substance as particles (a MODEL: drawn huge and slowed down). Solid: bonded, vibrating; liquid: sliding at the bottom; gas: flying, filling the box, pressing on the walls. Heat it and it melts and boils with the real plateaus; real readouts beside it: temperature, pressure, volume, molecular speed. Facts: 1 g of water at 20 °C, 60 particles, 1 L.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the hot plate's bottom, where it stands. Outline at defaults: 0.26 × 0.247 m; from the anchor x −0.13…+0.13, y +0…+0.247.
Props: substance: *water* | wax | iron | gallium | carbon dioxide | air | nitrogen | helium | bromine; temp_c: °C =20 [-270…3000]; heater_w: W =0 [-2000…20000]; heat_from_s: s =0.5 [0…20]; sample_g: g =1 [0.001…1000]; particles: int =60 [8…160]; width: m =0.2 [0.08…0.5]; height: m =0.2 [0.08…0.5]; volume_ml: mL =1000 [1…100000]; piston: bool =false; piston_start: (× height) =0.6 [0.2…1]; load_kg: kg =0 [0…50]; piston_area_cm2: cm² =7.07 [0.5…500]; divider: bool =false; second: *none* | air | bromine | helium | nitrogen | carbon dioxide; open_at_s: s =1 [0…20].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): temp_c (Temperature, °C), solid_pct (Solid, %), liquid_pct (Liquid, %), gas_pct (Gas, %), pressure_kpa (Pressure, kPa), volume_ml (Volume, mL), speed_ms (Molecules' mean speed, m/s), heat_kj (Heat put in, kJ), mixed_pct (Mixed, %).
Surface: material box acrylic; bounce 0.6, friction 0.5, rolling 0.01, side 0.
Notes: also called: particles, molecules, atoms, particle model, kinetic, states of matter, solid, liquid, gas, melting.
### syringe — Sealed syringe (air) · static (fixed in place)
A 60 mL plastic syringe with its tip sealed, standing upright, its air drawn as particles (a model). Push the plunger in and the same air has less room: the particles hit the walls more often and the gauge's pressure rises (Boyle: 60 → 30 mL doubles it, 101 → 203 kPa; the reading is the real air's p = 60 mL × 101.3 kPa ÷ V). Holding it in takes a push: 57 N at 30 mL, 284 N at 10 mL, 624 N at 5 mL (more than a hand gives). The air stays at its temperature (a slow push). Facts: 60 mL of air pushed to 30 mL.

mod_measure.title: Measuring: lanes, stopwatches, tapes, scales and gauges
mod_measure.text:
### Measuring: lanes, stopwatches, tapes, scales and gauges
Instruments read the run and show their reading on their own face every frame (a stopwatch's LCD, a light gate's and a speed sign's LEDs, a kitchen scale's grams, a spring scale's pointer); after a run each one's readings are listed with the item. Their faces, painted lines, tapes, trails and boards touch nothing (display only); the spring scale's hook, the kitchen scale's platform, the pan balance and the gram masses are real things. LINKS are props naming another item by its id: stopwatch.watch (what it times), stopwatch.start_line / finish_line (a start-line, a finish-line or a lane: a lane's finish is its finish_at mark), measuring-tape.watch (whose front it reads), speed-gate.watch (+ pair: an earlier gate, to time between them), speedometer.watch, spring-scale.hook (the thing hung on its hook by a string), protractor.watch (a ramp, pendulum or lever), motion-trail.watch, graph-board.watch/watch2/watch3 (lines), data-table.watch…watch4 (instruments whose readings it lists). A lane is a long floor 1-60 m (a static board 2 cm thick) with a mark every metre (or as set), big upright metre numbers, a white start line at start_at and a chequered finish line at finish_at; its anchor is its 0 m mark on its top surface, so the d-metre mark is at x = lane.x + d and things race on y = lane.y. Two lanes one above the other (y 0.02 and 0.82, the upper one stands on legs) compare two racers without them meeting. Stopwatch: start = release (the scene's release) | moves (the watched thing has moved 1 mm) | crosses (its front reaches start_line or start_x); stop = crosses (its front reaches finish_line or stop_x) | stops (it comes to rest) | hits (it first touches something new) | at (stop_at seconds after the start) | reads (the watched thing's reading stop_reading reaches stop_value, from the side it started on: a sand timer runs out, hourglass empty 1; ice melts, ice-cube melted 1; a thermometer's reading reaches 50; a candle goes out, flame 0; a balloon pops, popped 1; any reading the thing has) | never. It reads to 0.01 s; meters = how far the thing moved while it ran. counts lesson: its face shows the lesson clock (the run's seconds × the time-lapse) and a reads goal's seconds are that. face_cm sets how big its face is drawn (a real one is 6 cm; 30-40 cm reads in a wide 12 m shot). A kitchen-scale also weighs sand heaped on its platform (granular: a funnel above it, a sand-pile on it) and liquid lying on it as a puddle (flow: a tap or a pitcher spilling onto it), at about 1 g a mL of water; what falls on it pushes it only as it rests there (a stream's own push is not added). Readings: stopwatch seconds, meters, start_s, stop_s (lesson_s with counts lesson); measuring-tape meters (0 to its length; past_end 1 beyond its end); speed-gate speed (= length / blocked time), blocked_s, between_s; speedometer speed, top, mean; spring-scale newtons, grams, over (1: past its range, its hook bottomed out 5 % past full scale); kitchen-scale grams; pan-balance tilt (degrees, right pan down +), heavier (-1 left, 0 level, 1 right), left_g and right_g (what each pan holds); protractor degrees (a ramp's slope from level, a pendulum's turn from hanging straight), swing; motion-sensor distance. Weight and mass: a kitchen-scale and a spring-scale show WEIGHT (their grams are the force ÷ the Earth's 9.81: they are calibrated on Earth), so under settings.gravity moon a 1 kg mass reads 1.62 N and 165 g (1/6), on Mars 3.71 N and 378 g; a pan-balance compares MASSES (both pans feel the same g) and reads the same anywhere: 1 kg balances 1 kg on the Moon too. A pan-balance's pans hang 14 cm either side of its middle under the beam: put a thing IN a pan with place {inside: the balance, x: balance.x - 0.14} (left) or {inside: the balance, x: balance.x + 0.14} (right), gram masses the same (they stack in the pan). It tips 1.5° for each gram of difference, up to its 15° stop (10 g or more), and reads level (heavier 0, |tilt| under 0.5°) within 0.3 g; it settles in a few swings of 2-5 s. A lane has a foam bumper on its far end (end_stop): what races past the finish stops there and stays on the lane. A stopwatch with no watch link that starts at the release and stops at stop_at (or never) is a plain clock; a link that names nothing (a wrong id, itself, the wrong kind of item) is listed in the run's warnings.
  - goal reads {item: an instrument, seconds | meters | mps | newtons | grams | degrees | value, key?, tol?}: the instrument's reading at the end is within tol of the number (a stopwatch's time, a tape's metres, a gate's speed, a scale's grams; any module's instrument by value)
  - goal crosses {item, line (a start-line / finish-line / lane: its finish mark) | x (m), before_s?, after_s?}: the thing's front reaches that line (within the times)
  - goal faster {a, b, line? | x?}: a is faster than b (gets to the line, or over the same distance, sooner)
  - goal farther {a, b}: a ends at least 1 cm farther along +x from where it started than b
  - goal stops_between {item, x0, x1}: the thing's middle ends between x0 and x1 (m)
  - knob motor-car.speed: a motor car's top speed (m/s): faster crosses a line sooner and goes farther in the same seconds (time = distance / speed; it drives about 1.6 % under the setting)
  - knob motor-car.push: how hard its motor pushes (N): more gets it up to speed sooner, up to what its tyres can grip
  - knob lane.finish_at: where the race ends: a longer race takes longer (change it only when the request leaves the distance open)
  - knob stopwatch.stop_at: for a watch that stops after set seconds: a later stop lets the thing go farther
  - knob speed-gate.beam_height: the beam must cross the thing's body to see it pass
  - knob spring-scale.range: a stiffer spring holds a heavier thing without running off its scale (it stretches 10 cm at full scale)
  - knob kitchen-scale.tare: taring takes off what was on it at the release
  - knob pan-balance.damping: a damped beam settles sooner instead of rocking
  - knob gram-mass.grams: a brass mass's size (1 g to 1 kg, exact): a pan balance levels when both pans hold the same grams; a scale reads it
  - e.g. "Red car goes 10 m in 3 s, blue car 10 m in 4 s; stopwatches show it": two 10 m lanes (y 0.02 and 0.82), a motor-car on each with its front at 0 m (red speed 3.39 m/s, blue 2.54 m/s, start speeds equal to those), a stopwatch per car (watch, finish_line = its lane, face_cm 40) above each lane's finish; goals reads seconds 3 and 4 (tol 0.05) and faster {red, blue}
  - e.g. "Same 3 seconds: which car goes farther?": both stopwatches stop = at, stop_at = 3; red 3.39 m/s reaches 10 m, blue 2.71 m/s reaches 8 m in the same 3 s; a measuring-tape along each lane watching its car (or read the lane's numbers); goal farther {red, blue}
  - e.g. "Two balls race 10 m": soccer balls on 10 m lanes, held at 0 m with a start_speed; a rolling ball slows (air drag, rolling resistance), so 10 m in 3 s needs about 3.74 m/s at the start (12 % above 10/3); reads goals let the search tune it
  - e.g. "A car rolls down a ramp; how far does it go?": a plank ramp on a lane or the table, a toy-car at its top, a measuring-tape with its zero at the ramp's foot watching the car; a higher ramp sends it farther (goal farther between two set-ups)
  - e.g. "Weigh an apple with a newton meter": a spring-scale (range 5 N) on: air with hook = the apple hanging 3 cm under it; it reads about 1.8 N (180 g × 9.81)
  - e.g. "Show that mass is kept when the clay is squashed": a kitchen-scale with the clay ball on its platform; it reads the same grams before and after (reads goal on grams)
  - e.g. "Which is heavier, the stone or the sponge?": a pan-balance with one in each pan (inside the balance at x = balance.x ∓ 0.14); it tips toward the heavier (reads goal on tilt -15 or 15)
  - e.g. "Does a 1 kg mass weigh less on the Moon?": settings.gravity moon (air false); a kitchen-scale with a 1 kg gram-mass on it reads about 165 g (1.62 N: a scale shows weight); a pan-balance with 1 kg in each pan still balances (mass is the same); goals reads grams 165 tol 2 and reads tilt 0 tol 1
  - e.g. "Measure the ramp's angle": a protractor at the ramp's foot with watch = the ramp; it reads the slope in degrees
  - e.g. "Time a ball dropped from 1 m": a ball held at y 1 m, a stopwatch watch = the ball, start = release, stop = hits: about 0.45 s (√(2h/g))
  - e.g. "Show a speed-time graph of the car": a graph-board behind the scene, plot = speed, watch = the car
  - e.g. "Time a one-minute sand timer with a stopwatch": an hourglass on the table (its 66 g of fine sand run out in about 60 s), settings.time_lapse 4 and seconds 20 (the run shows a lesson minute in 15 s), a stopwatch with watch = the hourglass, start = release, stop = reads (stop_reading empty, stop_value 1), counts lesson; goal reads {item: stopwatch, seconds: 60, tol: 3}
  - e.g. "Weigh the sand a funnel pours onto a kitchen scale": a kitchen-scale on the table and a sand-funnel standing on the table beside it with its spout over the platform (funnel x = scale x; its heap lands on the platform); the scale's grams rise as the heap grows, to the funnel's poured_g (goal reads {item: scale, grams: the funnel's sand_kg × 1000, tol: 5})
### lane — Lane (with metre marks) · static (fixed in place)
A long floor with a mark every metre (or as set), big numbers, a start line and a finish line. Things race along it; stopwatches link to it to stop at its finish. Two lanes one above the other compare two racers. A foam bumper on its far end stops what runs past the finish. Facts: 10 m · marks every metre · start and finish lines.
Anchor (x, y): its 0 m mark, on its top surface. Outline at defaults: 12 × 0.12 m; from the anchor x −1…+11, y −0.02…+0.1.
Props: length: m =10 [1…60]; marks_every: 10 cm | 50 cm | *1 m* | 2 m | 5 m; labels: bool =true; label_cm: cm =20 [5…50]; start_at: m =0 [0…60]; finish_at: m =10 [0…60] auto (follows length unless set); width: m =0.6 [0.3…1.5]; surface: *gym floor* | vinyl | concrete | carpet | asphalt; color: *pale gray* | pale blue | pale green | pale yellow | white | tan; margin: m =1 [0…5]; end_stop: bool =true.
Notes: also called: track, race, runway, floor, metre, meter, marks, distance, lanes, ruler.
### start-line — Start line · static (fixed in place)
A painted start line across the floor. A stopwatch linked to it starts when the watched thing's front reaches it. Facts: start line · 5 cm wide.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the line, on the floor. Outline at defaults: 0.05 × 0.002 m; from the anchor x −0.025…+0.025, y −0.002…+0.
Props: depth: m =0.6 [0.1…2]; gate: bool =false; sign: bool =true.
Notes: also called: line, race, start, tape, mark, timing, lane, go.
### finish-line — Finish line · static (fixed in place)
A painted finish line across the floor. A stopwatch linked to it stops when the watched thing's front reaches it. Facts: finish line · 5 cm wide.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the line, on the floor. Outline at defaults: 0.05 × 0.002 m; from the anchor x −0.025…+0.025, y −0.002…+0.
Props: depth: m =0.6 [0.1…2]; gate: bool =false; sign: bool =true.
Notes: also called: line, race, finish, tape, mark, timing, lane, checkered.
### stopwatch — Stopwatch · static (fixed in place)
A digital stopwatch timing the thing it watches: it starts at the release (or when it moves, or crosses a start line) and stops when its front crosses the finish line (or when it stops, hits something, after set seconds, or when a reading of the thing it times reaches a value: a sand timer runs out, ice melts, a candle goes out). Its big face shows the time; it touches nothing. Facts: reads 0.01 s · starts at release · stops at the finish.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its face. Outline at defaults: 0.2 × 0.18 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: start: *release* | moves | crosses; stop: *crosses* | stops | hits | at | reads | never; start_x: m =0 [-100…100]; stop_x: m =10 [-100…100]; stop_at: s =3 [0…20]; stop_reading: *empty* | bottom_g | clogged | melted | reading | temp | water_temp | boiling | flame | popped | broken | light | on | lux | liquid_ml | volume_ml | left_ml | flooded | sunk | grams | level | rpm | dissolved_g | any other text (up to 64 characters); stop_value: =1 [-1000…100000]; reaction_s: s =0 [0…0.3]; counts: *run* | lesson; face_cm: cm =20 [6…60]; on_table: bool =false; watch: link → the id of another item (The thing it times); start_line: link → the id of a start-line | finish-line | lane (A start line, or a lane (its start mark)); finish_line: link → the id of a start-line | finish-line | lane (A finish line, or a lane (its finish mark)).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): seconds (Time, s), meters (Distance moved, m), start_s (Started at, s), stop_s (Stopped at, s).
Notes: acts at the scene's release time; also called: timer, clock, time, seconds, race, timing, watch, stop watch, measure.
### measuring-tape — Measuring tape · static (fixed in place)
A steel tape laid along the floor from its zero end. Linked to a thing, it reads where that thing's front is (and where it stopped): how far a car rolled from a ramp's foot. It reads 0 to its length (past_end 1 beyond it). Facts: 5 m · reads to 1 mm.
Anchor (x, y): its zero end, on the floor. Outline at defaults: 5 × 0.0006 m; from the anchor x +0…+5, y −0.0006…+0.
Props: length: m =5 [0.3…30]; from: *left end* | right end; point: *front* | back | centre; numbers: 10 cm | *1 m*; label_cm: cm =4 [1…30]; watch: link → the id of another item (The thing whose place it reads).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): meters (Reads, m), past_end (Past its end: 0 on the tape, 1 past its end).
Notes: also called: tape measure, ruler, distance, how far, metres, meters, length, measure.
### speed-gate — Speed gate (light gate) · static (fixed in place)
A light gate: an infrared beam across the track. It times how long the passing thing blocks the beam and reads its speed = its length / that time; two linked gates read the time between them. Facts: reads speed to 0.01 m/s.
Anchor (x, y): the floor under its beam. Outline at defaults: 0.03 × 0.07 m; from the anchor x −0.015…+0.015, y +0…+0.07.
Props: beam_height: m =0.03 [0.005…1]; face_cm: cm =12 [4…40]; watch: link → the id of another item (The thing it times (else whatever blocks the beam first)); pair: link → the id of a speed-gate (Another gate: this one also reads the time since that one was blocked).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): speed (Speed, m/s), blocked_s (Blocked for, s), between_s (Time from the first gate, s).
Notes: also called: photogate, light gate, speed, timer, beam, velocity, speed trap.
### speedometer — Speedometer (radar sign) · static (fixed in place)
A radar speed sign showing how fast the watched thing moves now (and its top and mean speed). It touches nothing. Facts: m/s or km/h.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its sign. Outline at defaults: 0.3 × 0.225 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: units: *m/s* | km/h; face_cm: cm =30 [8…80]; watch: link → the id of another item (The thing whose speed it shows).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): speed (Speed now, m/s), top (Top speed, m/s), mean (Mean speed, m/s).
Notes: also called: speed, radar, speed gun, velocity, how fast, meter, your speed.
### spring-scale — Spring scale (newton meter) · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A newton meter: a spring in a clear tube with a hook below, held up by a retort stand. Hang a thing on its hook (link it) and the spring stretches until it holds the thing's weight; the pointer reads the force in newtons. It shows weight: on the Moon 1 kg pulls 1.62 N (its grams, worked out with the Earth's 9.81, read 165 g). Past its range the hook bottoms out (over 1). Facts: 2.5-50 N · 10 cm of travel. Moving parts ≈11.3 g.
Anchor (x, y): its top ring. Outline at defaults: 0.025 × 0.31 m; from the anchor x −0.013…+0.013, y −0.31…+0.
Props: range: 2.5 N | 5 N | *10 N* | 20 N | 50 N; hook: link → the id of another item (The thing hung from its hook by a short string).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): newtons (Force, N), grams (As a weight, g), over (Over its range: 0 in range, 1 over its range).
Notes: has springs; also called: newton meter, force meter, spring balance, weigh, weight, force, pull, hooke.
### kitchen-scale — Kitchen scale · static (fixed in place)
A kitchen scale: whatever rests on its platform, directly or stacked, is weighed in grams (the push on the platform divided by the Earth's g, 9.81: it is calibrated on Earth). It reads true at rest; a bouncing thing makes it jump about. It shows weight, so on the Moon a 1 kg mass reads 165 g (a pan balance compares masses and reads the same anywhere). Facts: 0-5 kg · 1 g.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its underside, on the table. Outline at defaults: 0.18 × 0.026 m; from the anchor x −0.09…+0.09, y +0…+0.026.
Props: style: *digital* | mechanical; tare: bool =false; capacity_kg: kg =5 [0.5…30].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): grams (Reads, g), newtons (Force on it, N).
Notes: also called: scale, weigh, mass, grams, balance, kitchen, conservation, weight.
### pan-balance — Pan balance · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
An equal-arm balance: a 30 cm beam on a post with a pan hanging from each end. It tips toward the heavier pan (1.5° a gram, up to its stop) and settles level when both pans hold the same mass, whatever their size. It compares masses, so it reads the same on the Moon (a scale, showing weight, reads 1/6 there). Put things IN its pans: inside the balance at x = its x - 0.14 m (left pan) or + 0.14 m (right pan). Facts: 30 cm beam · ±15° stop. Moving parts ≈1.27 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its base, on the table. Outline at defaults: 0.4 × 0.256 m; from the anchor x −0.2…+0.2, y +0…+0.256.
Props: stop_deg: ° =15 [3…30]; damping: N·m·s =0.02 [0…0.05].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): tilt (Tilt, °), heavier (Heavier side), left_g (Left pan holds, g), right_g (Right pan holds, g).
Notes: has pin joints; container, but NOT usable as a goal container; also called: balance, scale, compare, mass, heavier, lighter, equal arm, weigh, pans.
### gram-mass — Gram mass (brass) · dynamic
A brass laboratory mass (1 g to 1 kg) of exactly its marked mass: put it in a balance pan or on a scale. Facts: 1 g to 1 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its base. Outline at defaults: 0.026 × 0.032 m; from the anchor x −0.013…+0.013, y +0…+0.032.
Props: grams: 1 g | 2 g | 5 g | 10 g | 20 g | 50 g | *100 g* | 200 g | 500 g | 1 kg.
Surface: material brass; bounce 0.6, friction 0.4, rolling 0.002, side 0.
Notes: also called: weight, mass, slotted mass, calibration, brass, grams, kilogram, standard mass.
### protractor — Protractor · static (fixed in place)
A clear 180° protractor. Linked to a ramp it reads the slope from level; to a pendulum or lever, how far it is turned from hanging straight, and how far it swings. It touches nothing. Facts: 180° · 0.5° marks.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its straight edge (its centre mark). Outline at defaults: 0.3 × 0.15 m; from the anchor x −0.15…+0.15, y +0…+0.15.
Props: size_cm: cm =30 [10…100]; watch: link → the id of another item (A ramp, a pendulum, a lever: the thing whose angle it reads).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): degrees (Angle, °), swing (Swing, °).
Notes: also called: angle, degrees, slope, tilt, incline, measure, pendulum.
### plumb-line — Plumb line · static (fixed in place)
A string with a pointed brass bob: it hangs straight down, toward the Earth's centre: it shows which way gravity pulls. Only drawn: it touches nothing. Facts: shows straight down.
Anchor (x, y): where its string is tied (the top). Outline at defaults: 0.004 × 0.5 m; from the anchor x −0.002…+0.002, y −0.5…+0.
Props: length: m =0.5 [0.05…3].
Notes: also called: plumb, vertical, down, gravity, plumb bob, straight down.
### metre-stick — Metre stick · dynamic
A 1 m wooden stick with centimetre marks (lay it beside a thing to measure it; it is a real stick: it can be a lever). Facts: 1 m · cm marks. Moving parts ≈118 g.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its underside. Outline at defaults: 1 × 0.006 m; from the anchor x −0.5…+0.5, y +0…+0.006.
Props: length: m =1 [0.3…2].
Surface: material *varnished hardwood* | domino wood; bounce 0.93, friction 0.45, rolling 0, side 0.
Notes: also called: meter stick, ruler, metre rule, yardstick, measure, centimetres, lever.
### motion-sensor — Motion sensor · static (fixed in place)
An ultrasonic motion sensor: it reads the distance to the nearest thing in front of it (15 cm to 6 m), every step; a graph board can plot it. Facts: 0.15-6 m.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the sensor (it faces to the right; turn it to aim). Outline at defaults: 0.06 × 0.05 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: range_m: m =6 [0.5…10].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): distance (Distance, m).
Notes: also called: ultrasonic, ranger, sonar, distance sensor, position, graph, data logger.
### motion-trail — Motion trail · static (fixed in place)
Draws the path behind the linked moving thing as it goes: a line, dots or ghost copies every strobe_s seconds (a motion diagram: wide spacing = fast). Drawn only. Facts: line, dots or ghosts.
Anchor (x, y): anywhere (it is only drawn behind the thing it follows). Outline at defaults: 0.02 × 0.02 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: color: *red* | blue | green | orange | purple | yellow | black | white; style: *line* | dots | ghosts; strobe_s: s =0.5 [0.05…2]; fade_s: s =0 [0…20]; watch: link → the id of another item (The moving thing whose path it draws).
Notes: also called: trail, path, strobe, motion diagram, trace, track, ghost.
### graph-board — Graph board · static (fixed in place)
A board standing behind the scene that draws, as the run plays, the distance (from where each started) or speed of up to three linked things against time, or a linked instrument's reading. Drawn only. Facts: distance-time · speed-time.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its bottom edge. Outline at defaults: 1.2 × 0.8 m; from the anchor x −0.6…+0.6, y +0…+0.8.
Props: plot: *distance* | speed | reading; width: m =1.2 [0.4…4]; height: m =0.8 [0.3…2]; t_max: s =0 [0…20]; watch: link → the id of another item; watch2: link → the id of another item; watch3: link → the id of another item.
Notes: also called: graph, chart, plot, distance-time, speed-time, position, data, whiteboard.
### data-table — Data table · static (fixed in place)
A board listing the linked instruments' readings (a stopwatch's time, a tape's distance) as the run ends: a fair test's results. Drawn only. Facts: up to 4 rows.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its bottom edge. Outline at defaults: 1 × 0.7 m; from the anchor x −0.5…+0.5, y +0…+0.7.
Props: width: m =1 [0.4…4]; height: m =0.7 [0.3…2]; title: *Results* | Trial results | Times | Distances | Readings; watch: link → the id of another item; watch2: link → the id of another item; watch3: link → the id of another item; watch4: link → the id of another item.
Notes: also called: table, results, data, trials, record, fair test.

mod_mechanics.title: Machines and motion (mechanics): forces, force arrows (free-body diagrams) and energy bars
mod_mechanics.text:
### Machines and motion (mechanics): forces, force arrows (free-body diagrams) and energy bars
ANY ITEM (catalog-wide props): color (none, red, blue, green, yellow, orange, purple, pink, white, black, gray, brown: the look only; a car's or truck's body, not its tyres), glow (true: a soft halo to point it out), and for every moving item start_speed (m/s it already has at the release, a push, kick or launch), start_dir (degrees from the way it faces, counter-clockwise: 0 forward, 180 back, 90 up) and start_spin ("roll": balls and wheels already turning as if rolling). Cars and trucks face right (+x) at angle 0. An egg with props {fragile: true} cracks if it lands hard (peak force over 35 N: about 7 cm or more onto a table breaks it, 80 cm onto a 10 cm foam block does not); goals breaks / survives.
FLOORS, RAMPS, SURFACES: floor (a long ground slab, length up to 60 m, its anchor the middle of its top; material varnished hardwood (gym), concrete, carpet, rubber mat, grass, ice: friction lessons race the same car over different floors). ramp: a plank on `blocks` stacked wooden blocks (5 cm each: blocks 1 vs 3 = rise 5 vs 15 cm), `length` (m), rises "left" (default: the top is length·cos(slope) to the LEFT of its anchor, the foot at the anchor) or "right"; lip true keeps a small stop at the top. A car or cart on a ramp: place {on: <ramp id>, x: the top end + half the car's length + 0.03} (the top end is at the ramp's x − length when it rises left, x + length when it rises right; a 20 cm toy car on a ramp at x 1.0 rising left: x 0.13); it is turned to lie along the slope and rolls down at the release. Put the ramp on the floor item or the table (place {on: <floor id>}); give a floor item an id other than "floor", "ground" or "table" (e.g. "gym-floor"): place.on "floor" means the table. A FAIR TEST of ramp height (1 block vs 3 blocks, the Grade 3 'is this a valid experiment?'): one long carpet floor (length 8: the table alone is too short, its end walls stop the cars), both ramps rising left (the default) so both cars roll right, the 3-block ramp's foot 2.4 m right of the 1-block ramp's (on carpet a toy car rolls about 1 m past a 1-block ramp and 2.5 m past a 3-block one, so the first stops before the second ramp; on wood 3 m and 11 m), the same car (same colour, same clay) on each, only the blocks differ; goal farther {a: the 3-block car, b: the 1-block car} (farther measures the distance along +x).

Two carts pushing apart: a plunger cart and a second cart touching its front (left_of/right_of with align touching), the lighter one leaves faster: v_a/v_b = m_b/m_a (goal recoils {a, b, ratio}).
FORCE METERS AND SENSORS (readings in the run, shown in the digest): a puller's `newtons` is the pull in its cord (a force meter); in mode speed it reels in at its set speed, so its reading is the force that takes: pulling a cart UP A RAMP at a steady 0.1 m/s reads m·g·sin(slope), less than lifting it straight up (m·g) (stand the puller on the floor just past the ramp's top end, faces right when the cart is down to its right, its height (the drum's, up to 1 m) on the slope's line there so the cord runs along it). An edge-pulley's `newtons` is the string's pull on the cart (a force sensor: T = M·a, less than the hanging weight). A dynamics-cart reads its own speed (m/s, + forward) and accel (m/s²): F = M·a with the string's pull. Goal pulls_with {item: the puller or edge pulley, newtons, tol?}: its steady reading; measure's reads {item, newtons} reads the end value.
SIMPLE MACHINES (the lever, wheel and axle, block and tackle and gears hang in the air: place {on: "air", y_m}; their stands are drawn; the screw jack stands on the table or floor): lever-kit (class 1, 2 or 3; load kg at load_at m from the fulcrum, effort kg at effort_at m; its masses hang 25 cm under the beam: y_m about 0.6; balances when load × load_at = effort × effort_at, resolved balanced_by says the effort that balances). wheel-and-axle (wheel_radius, axle_radius: MA = R/r; load on the axle's cord, effort on the wheel's; y_m about 1.4 with drop 0.4). block-and-tackle (strands 2-4 = MA; effort = (load + 0.05 kg block) / strands balances; y_m about 1.6). screw-jack (stands on the floor or table: a handle turning a screw lifts a heavy load on its cap a pitch a turn: load kg, effort N at the handle's end, handle m, pitch mm, turns a second, efficiency (0.3); it lifts when efficiency × effort × 2π·handle/pitch > the load's weight: 10 N on a 20 cm handle with a 5 mm thread lifts up to about 75 kg, at 5 mm/s: give the scene seconds 6-10; goal rises {item} (1 cm by default)). gear-train (teeth_a drives at rpm, teeth_b and teeth_c (0 = only two gears): the last gear turns rpm × teeth_a ÷ teeth_last, each pair turning opposite ways; place in the air at a visible height, y_m about 0.5). Goals: balanced {item} (it holds still), rises {item, min_m?} (its load goes up), gear_speed {item, rpm?, direction?} (a gear train's last gear).
ROLLER COASTER (coaster-track: layout curved ramp, valley, hill or loop; height = the start's height (m), size = the loop's radius; its anchor is the floor under the start and it runs to the right). Put the ball (steel-ball, glass-marble) at the start: place {on: <track id>, x: track x + 0.03}; it rolls at the release. Energy: a rolling ball needs a start about 2.7 × the loop radius above the loop's bottom to go round (height 0.45 m for a 15 cm loop just goes round; 0.35 m falls off). Goal loops {item, track}.
FALLING AND AIR: coffee-filters (count nested: terminal speed about 1 m/s × √count), parachute (canopy m across, load_mass kg: a bigger canopy, a slower fall), paper-sheet (falls slowly flat) vs paper-ball (the same 5 g crumpled, falls fast), feather. Drop them held at the same height (held: true, place {on: "air", y_m}) so they let go together. Vacuum or the Moon: scene settings {air: false} (and gravity "moon"): a feather and a hammer land together.
