### paper-sheet — Sheet of paper · dynamic
A flat A4 sheet of office paper (5 g): flat it drifts down slowly (about 1 m/s); crumpled (the paper ball) it falls fast. Facts: A4 · 5 g.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.297 × 0.001 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: mass: kg =0.005 [0.001…0.05]; held: *long side* | short side.
Surface: material office paper; bounce 0.3, friction 0.4, rolling 0.02, side 0.
Notes: also called: paper, sheet, A4, air resistance, falling, flat, crumpled, drag.
### paper-ball — Crumpled paper ball · dynamic
The same 5 g sheet crumpled into a ball about 6 cm across: it falls nearly as fast as a stone over a metre. Facts: 6 cm · 5 g.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.06 × 0.06 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: diameter: m =0.06 [0.02…0.15]; mass: kg =0.005 [0.001…0.05].
Surface: material office paper; bounce 0.3, friction 0.4, rolling 0.02, side 0.
Notes: also called: paper, crumpled, ball, air resistance, falling, drag.
### feather — Feather · dynamic
A feather: in air it drifts down slowly; in a vacuum (the scene's air off) it falls with a hammer, as on the Moon in 1971. Facts: 30 g falcon feather.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.25 × 0.004 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: kind: *falcon* | craft.
Surface: material feather; bounce 0.1, friction 0.5, rolling 0.05, side 0.
Notes: also called: feather, hammer and feather, apollo, vacuum, air resistance, falling, moon, galileo.
### coaster-track — Roller-coaster track · static (fixed in place)
A curved track of true arcs (no bumps at its joints): a drop from its start platform, then a flat run, a valley (U), a hill or a loop-the-loop. Potential energy turns into motion and back; a ball needs a start 2.7 times the loop's radius high to go round. Facts: 60 cm drop · 15 cm loop.
Anchor (x, y): the floor under its start (the track runs to the right). Outline at defaults: 1.66 × 0.62 m; from the anchor x −0.01…+1.65, y +0…+0.62.
Props: layout: curved ramp | valley | hill | *loop*; height: m =0.6 [0.15…2]; size: m =0.15 [0.04…0.6]; run: m =0.6 [0.1…3]; depth: m =0.05 [0.02…0.2].
Surface: material *steel* | varnished hardwood | hollow plastic; bounce 0.95, friction 0.4, rolling 0.001, side 0.1.
Notes: also called: roller coaster, coaster, loop, loop the loop, track, marble run, half pipe, valley, hill, energy.
### gear-train — Gear train · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
Two or three meshed spur gears on axles: the motor turns the driver; each gear turns the next the other way, its speed times (driver teeth ÷ its teeth): a 12-tooth gear turns a 36-tooth one 3 times slower (and 3 times as hard). Facts: 12 : 36 teeth · 30 rpm. Moving parts ≈1.54 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the middle between its first and last gear's axles. Outline at defaults: 0.192 × 0.144 m; from the anchor x −0.072…+0.12, y −0.072…+0.072.
Props: teeth_a: int =12 [6…80]; teeth_b: int =36 [6…80]; teeth_c: int =0 [0…80]; module: mm =4 [0.5…8]; rpm: rpm =30 [0…300]; turns: *counter-clockwise* | clockwise; torque: N·m =0.5 [0.01…10]; gear_mass: kg =0.02 [0.002…1].
Notes: has 2 hinged parts, a motor; also called: gear, gears, gear train, cog, speed ratio, torque, simple machine, mesh, transmission, rpm.
### wheel-and-axle — Wheel and axle · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A big wheel fixed to a thin axle: an effort weight on a rope round the wheel lifts a heavier load on a rope round the axle. Mechanical advantage R/r: a 15 cm wheel on a 3 cm axle lifts 1 kg with 0.2 kg (just over that to move it). Facts: MA 5 · 1 kg load.
Anchor (x, y): the wheel's axle. Outline at defaults: 0.32 × 0.63 m; from the anchor x −0.15…+0.17, y −0.48…+0.15.
Props: wheel_radius: m =0.15 [0.04…0.4]; axle_radius: m =0.03 [0.01…0.1]; load: kg =1 [0.05…10]; effort: kg =0.25 [0.01…10]; drop: m =0.4 [0.1…1.5]; wheel_mass: kg =0.2 [0.01…3].
Notes: has a hinged part; also called: wheel and axle, windlass, winch, simple machine, mechanical advantage, crank, well, lift, torque.
### block-and-tackle — Block and tackle · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A fixed pulley block above, a moving block below carrying the load: with n rope strands holding it, an effort of 1/n of the load (and the block) holds it up, and the effort moves n times as far as the load rises. Facts: MA 2 · 1 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the fixed top block's middle. Outline at defaults: 0.105 × 0.626 m; from the anchor x −0.03…+0.075, y −0.601…+0.025.
Props: strands: int =2 [2…4]; load: kg =1 [0.05…10]; effort: kg =0.6 [0.01…10]; drop: m =0.5 [0.15…1.5].
Notes: has a pulley; also called: pulley, pulleys, block and tackle, mechanical advantage, simple machine, hoist, crane, lift, strands.
### lever-kit — Lever · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A beam on a fulcrum with a hanging load and an effort (a weight hanging, or pulling up over a pulley): balanced when load × its distance = effort × its distance. Classes 1, 2 and 3. Facts: class 1 · 0.5 kg at 20 cm.
Anchor (x, y): the fulcrum's pin. Outline at defaults: 1 × 0.293 m; from the anchor x −0.5…+0.5, y −0.29…+0.003.
Props: class: *1* | 2 | 3; length: m =1 [0.3…2]; load: kg =0.5 [0.01…10]; load_at: m =0.2 [0.02…1]; effort: kg =0.25 [0.01…10]; effort_at: m =0.4 [0.02…1]; beam_mass: kg =0.12 [0.01…2].
Notes: has a rope, pin joints; also called: lever, fulcrum, simple machine, first class lever, second class lever, third class lever, balance, torque, seesaw, effort.
### balloon-rocket — Balloon rocket · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A blown-up balloon taped to a straw on a taut string: let go, its air rushes out of the neck backward and pushes it forward (Newton's third law) until it is empty, then it coasts. Facts: 4 m string · 25 cm balloon. Moving parts ≈6.08 g.
Anchor (x, y): the floor under the string's start (its left end); the string runs 1 m up, to the right, the balloon waiting at its start. Outline at defaults: 4.18 × 1 m; from the anchor x −0.115…+4.07, y +0…+1.
Props: string: m =4 [0.5…15]; diameter: m =0.25 [0.12…0.4]; pressure: Pa =3000 [1000…6000]; nozzle: m =0.01 [0.004…0.02]; rubber: kg =0.005 [0.002…0.03].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): volume (Air left, m³), thrust (Jet push, N).
Notes: also called: balloon rocket, rocket, action reaction, newton third law, thrust, jet, balloon, string, straw.
### screw-jack — Screw jack · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A screw jack: turning its handle drives a screw up through the nut in its base, lifting a heavy load on its cap a pitch a turn. A 10 N push on a 20 cm handle with a 5 mm thread lifts about 75 kg (ideal advantage 2π·L / pitch = 251, about 30 % efficient), but only 5 mm a turn: force traded for distance. Facts: MA 251 · 30 % · 5 mm a turn. Moving parts ≈22.3 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its base, on the floor. Outline at defaults: 0.4 × 0.23 m; from the anchor x −0.2…+0.2, y −0.009…+0.221.
Props: load: kg =20 [0…300]; effort: N =10 [0.5…200]; handle: m =0.2 [0.05…0.5]; pitch: mm =5 [1…12]; turns: turns/s =1 [0.1…4]; efficiency: =0.3 [0.1…0.9]; lift: m =0.05 [0.01…0.3].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): lift (Lifted, m).
Notes: also called: screw, screw jack, car jack, jack, simple machine, inclined plane, thread, pitch, lift, mechanical advantage.
### energy-bars — Energy bars · static (fixed in place)
A board standing behind the scene with bars of the linked moving thing's energy as the run plays: kinetic (½mv²), potential (mgh), spring (½kx²) and what has turned to heat and sound, their total the start's: energy changes form, the total stays. Drawn only. Facts: KE · PE · heat.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its bottom edge. Outline at defaults: 0.6 × 0.5 m; from the anchor x −0.3…+0.3, y +0…+0.5.
Props: width: m =0.6 [0.3…2]; height: m =0.5 [0.25…1.5]; zero: *lowest* | floor; watch: link → the id of another item (The moving thing whose energy it shows (a pendulum's bob, a ball on a track, a car on a ramp)).
Notes: also called: energy, energy bars, kinetic energy, potential energy, conservation of energy, energy transfer, heat, bar chart, pendulum, roller coaster.

mod_optics.title: Light and optics
mod_optics.text:
### Light and optics
Light items shine in the scene's plane: a flashlight (a cone, lumens, beam_angle), a laser pointer (one thin beam), sunlight (parallel light at an elevation, in a band centred on its marker) and the heat module's desk lamp; a lit arrow is a lit object for lens images. Every optics item points where its `aim` prop says (degrees: 0 = right, 90 = up, 180 = left, -90 = down; leave the item's own angle at 0): a light shines along its aim; a mirror's shiny face, a light meter's sensor and an eye's look face along their aim (mirrors and meters default to 180, facing a light on their left); a lens's axis runs along its aim. Optics items stand on stands (they never fall): place them on "air" with y_m = the height of the beam (or on the table). Light goes straight until it meets something: opaque things (most items: balls, blocks, books, the table) stop it and cast shadows, mirrors reflect it (angle in = angle out; a mirror turned x° turns its beam 2x°; to send a beam arriving in direction A on in direction B, set the mirror's aim to (A + 180 + B) / 2), glass, water, ice and clear plastic bend it (a prism splits white light into a rainbow; a convex lens brings parallel light to a point focal_length behind it; a semicircular block totally reflects past 41°), material panels sort materials (transparent / translucent / opaque), colour filters pass their colour. Measuring: a light-meter reads lux on its sensor (sunlight ≈ 100 000 lx; a 150 lm flashlight at 1 m ≈ 1 600 lx in its beam; twice as far → a quarter), a light-sensor (target) registers whether a light reaches it, a screen shows shadows (its reading: the shadow's size; a point light makes the shadow grow as the object nears the light), an eye sees things that are lit (or lights) in front of it, also by mirrors. Light absorbed heats (each lit item's `light_w`). Liquids bend light too: the water (salt water, oil, syrup, honey, alcohol) in the liquids module's water-tank, beaker, graduated-cylinder, measuring-jug and density-column refracts with its own index (water 1.333, oil 1.47), its surface where the liquid stands now: a laser into an aquarium at 45° goes on at 32° in the water; a coin on the bottom of an opaque jug hidden behind its rim from an eye shows once there is water in it (sees {eye, coin}); a pencil standing in a beaker of water looks broken at the surface. The circuits module's bulbs and LEDs shine as lights too (as bright as their `light` reading: a bulb on 2 cells reads more lux on a light-meter than on 1; they cast shadows on a screen). A flashlight's `color` (white, red, green, blue) mixes on a white screen (red + green = yellow, all three white; two coloured torches make two coloured shadows); its `pattern` blinks a message (SOS in Morse code, or 1s and 0s, dot_s each) that a light-sensor or light-meter it reaches reads back: receives {sensor, light}.
  - goal hits_target {light, target, before_s?}: some of that light source's light reaches the target (straight, or by mirrors, lenses, glass)
  - goal lit {item, at_least_lux?}: at the run's end light falls on it (a light meter: it reads at least at_least_lux, default 1 lx)
  - goal dark {item, at_most_lux?}: at the run's end (almost) no light falls on it (a light meter: at most at_most_lux, default 1 lx)
  - goal shadow_on {occluder, screen}: the occluder's shadow falls on the screen (light that would reach the screen stops on it)
  - goal sees {eye, item}: light from the item (its own, or light it scatters) enters the eye, straight or by mirrors
  - goal brighter {a, b}: at the run's end light meter a reads more than b (other items: a takes in more light than b)
  - goal focused {screen}: a lit object's image on the screen is sharp (a convex lens between them at the right distances: 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i)
  - goal receives {sensor, light, message?}: a blinking flashlight's message (its pattern: a Morse word such as SOS, or 1s and 0s) reaches the light-sensor or light-meter and reads back right (or reads `message`)
  - goal rainbow {screen}: white light split into its colours (a prism) lands on the screen, violet and red apart
  - knob flashlight.aim: points its beam (degrees: 0 right, 90 up)
  - knob flashlight.lumens: the light everywhere in its beam grows with its lumens
  - knob flashlight.beam_angle: a wider cone reaches more, each place dimmer
  - knob flashlight.dot_s: a longer dot sends the same message more slowly (the run must last the whole message)
  - knob measuring-jug.fill_ml: a higher water surface bends the light from what lies on the bottom further over the rim (the coin appears)
  - knob beaker.fill_ml: the water's surface is where light bends: more water covers more of what stands in it
  - knob laser-pointer.aim: points its beam (degrees)
  - knob laser-pointer.power_mw: more power, a brighter spot (same path)
  - knob mirror.aim: turning a mirror by x° turns its reflected beam by 2x°
  - knob curved-mirror.aim: points its face (and its focus)
  - knob curved-mirror.focal_length: its focus is focal_length in front of it
  - knob convex-lens.focal_length: parallel light meets focal_length behind it; an image forms where 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i
  - knob convex-lens.aim: its axis should run along the light
  - knob concave-lens.aim: its axis should run along the light
  - knob prism.aim: how the beam meets its faces sets how much it bends and spreads
  - knob glass-block.aim: a steeper slant bends the beam more
  - knob semicircle-block.aim: past the critical angle the light is totally reflected
  - knob light-meter.aim: a sensor facing the light reads the most
  - knob light-sensor.size: a bigger target catches more of a spread beam
  - knob screen.height: a taller screen catches more of the light and the whole shadow
  - knob eye.aim: it sees only what is in front of it
  - knob sunlight.elevation: a higher sun casts shorter shadows and puts more light on flat ground (∝ sin of its height)
  - knob sunlight.irradiance: how bright the sunlight is (clear noon ≈ 1000 W/m²)
  - knob lit-arrow.aim: points its light at the lens
  - e.g. "Show that light travels in straight lines": a laser-pointer (aim 0) and a light-sensor at the same height 1 m to its right (hits_target); a second laser with a cardboard material-panel between it and its own target: that target stays dark (dark {target})
  - e.g. "Make a shadow on a screen with a ball and a flashlight; nearer the light, a bigger shadow": flashlight aim 0 at y 0.3, a fixed tennis-ball 0.4 m to its right at the same height, a screen 1.2 m to its right (height 0.6): shadow_on {occluder: ball, screen}; its shadow_cm reading grows as the ball nears the light (5 cm card 20 cm from the light, screen at 60 cm: 15 cm)
  - e.g. "Bounce a laser off a mirror onto a target": laser-pointer aim 0; a mirror where the beam passes, aim (0 + 180 + 90)/2 = 135 to send it straight up; a light-sensor above the mirror: hits_target {light: laser, target}
  - e.g. "Show that light bends when it goes into glass (or water)": laser-pointer aimed down at aim -45 onto a glass-block on a stand; it bends to 28° inside and leaves parallel, shifted; a light-sensor on the exit path: hits_target
  - e.g. "Total internal reflection in a glass block": semicircle-block (aim 0: flat face right); a laser aimed through the round side at the middle of the flat face: 40° from the face's normal gets out, 43° is totally reflected back (a tir happening); light-sensors on both paths
  - e.g. "Which materials let light through? glass, wax paper, cardboard, foil": one lane each: flashlight (beam_angle 10) → material-panel → light-meter 5 cm behind it (aim 180); brighter {glass meter, wax meter}, lit {wax meter}, dark {cardboard meter}, dark {foil meter} (glass passes ≈ 92 %)
  - e.g. "A light meter near and far from a lamp: nearer is brighter": the desk lamp (aim 45, beam_angle 60, head_height 0.6) with two light-meters on its beam, 0.5 m and 1 m from the bulb, each aimed back at it: brighter {near, far} (about 4 : 1, 1/d²)
  - e.g. "We see a book because light bounces off it into our eye": a flashlight lighting a hardcover-book, an eye aimed at the book: sees {eye, book}; with the flashlight off (on false) the eye sees nothing (its sees reading 0)
  - e.g. "A convex lens makes an upside-down image": lit-arrow, a convex-lens (f 0.10) 0.30 m to its right, a screen 0.15 m behind the lens (1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i): focused {screen}; the screen's image_cm reading is −½ the arrow's height
  - e.g. "Split white light into a rainbow with a prism": sunlight through a slit (width 0.005) at elevation ≈ 24° from the left onto a flint prism turned apex down (aim 180), a screen beyond it: rainbow {screen}
  - e.g. "A magnifying glass focuses sunlight": sunlight at elevation 90, a convex-lens with aim 90 (axis vertical), a light-meter facing up (aim 90) focal_length below it: lit {meter, at_least_lux: 1000000}
  - e.g. "Black takes in more of the sun's light than white": sunlight on a white card and a black cloth material-panel lying flat (aim 90): brighter {black, white} (black absorbs ≈ 0.97, white ≈ 0.2)
  - e.g. "Colour filters: a red filter lets red light through and stops green": a flashlight (beam_angle 10) through a color-filter (color red) onto a screen, and a green laser-pointer through a second red color-filter onto a light-sensor: hits_target {torch, screen} (the red part passes, ≈ 0.88 of it), lit {sensor} labelled as a little green getting through (≈ 2 %)
  - e.g. "A lamp's light warms the ice cube it shines on": the heat module's lamp (target: the ice-cube it points at) and two ice-cubes on the table, one in its beam and one well away from it: hits_target {lamp, lit cube}, brighter {lit cube, other cube} (light taken in, W; with the heat module the lit cube melts first)
  - e.g. "See over a wall with a periscope": an eye low behind a wall (aim 180), a mirror in front of it at aim 45 and one above it at aim 225, a lit book on the far side above the wall: sees {eye, book}
  - e.g. "Light bends when it goes into water: a laser into an aquarium": a water-tank (aquarium, fill 0.2) on the table, a laser-pointer above its left half aimed down at aim -45 so the beam meets the water's surface: it goes on at 32° from the vertical in the water (n 1.333); a light-sensor on the tank's floor where the bent beam lands: hits_target {laser, sensor}
  - e.g. "The disappearing coin: a coin in a cup shows when water is poured in": a measuring-jug (opaque plastic) with a penny on its bottom, a flashlight above shining down into it, an eye beside it just below the rim's sight line looking at the bottom (aim about -60): with fill_ml 0 sees {eye, penny} fails, with fill_ml 500 it holds (the light from the coin bends over the rim)
  - e.g. "A pencil in a glass of water looks bent": a beaker of water with a chopstick or pencil leaning in it, lit by a flashlight, and an eye looking at it from the side and above: sees {eye, pencil}; the part under the water is seen at a steeper angle than the part above (the digest's beam path through the water shows the bend)
  - e.g. "Mix red, green and blue light; coloured shadows": three flashlights (color red, green, blue, beam_angle 30) a little apart aimed at one white screen, a ball between them and the screen: shadow_on {ball, screen}; where red and green overlap the screen looks yellow, all three white; the ball casts a coloured shadow for each torch
  - e.g. "Send a message with a flashlight (Morse code)": a flashlight with pattern SOS (dot_s 0.2, beam_angle 10) aimed at a light-sensor 1 m away, seconds 6: receives {sensor, light: flashlight} (it reads back SOS; the sensor's pulses reading counts the flashes)
  - e.g. "A bulb with 2 batteries is brighter than with 1": two circuits side by side (each a battery (1 or 2 cells) wired to a bulb), a light-meter 10 cm above each bulb facing down (aim -90): brighter {meter over the 2-cell bulb, meter over the 1-cell bulb}
### flashlight — Flashlight · static (fixed in place)
An LED flashlight (torch), 15 cm long, on a stand. Its beam leaves its lens end in the direction `aim` (degrees: 0 = to the right, 90 = straight up, 180 = left). A cone of white light that spreads and dims with distance (1/d²). `color` red, green or blue makes a one-colour torch: on a white screen red + green look yellow, red + blue magenta, green + blue cyan, all three white, and an object lit by two of them casts two coloured shadows. `pattern` makes it blink a message (Morse code of a word such as SOS, or 1s and 0s of dot_s each): a light-sensor (or light-meter) it shines on counts the flashes (`pulses`) and the goal receives {sensor, light} reads the message back. Facts: 150 lm · 20° beam · 15 cm long.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.15 × 0.03 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: lumens: lm =150 [5…1000] auto (follows color unless set); beam_angle: ° =20 [5…60]; aim: ° =0 [-360…360]; on: bool =true; on_at: s =0 [0…20]; color: *white* | red | green | blue; pattern: *steady* | SOS | HI | 101 | 1100 | any other text (up to 64 characters); dot_s: s =0.2 [0.05…2]; repeat: bool =true.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): on (On).
Notes: also called: torch, light, beam, lamp, coloured light, blink, signal, morse code.
### laser-pointer — Laser pointer · static (fixed in place)
A laser pointer (14 cm pen) on a stand: ONE thin beam in the direction `aim` (degrees, 0 = right). Ideal for mirrors, refraction and hitting targets: the beam is drawn as a bright line, as if through a little mist. Facts: 1 mW · red 650 nm · beam Ø 1.5 mm.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.14 × 0.014 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: color: *red* | green | violet; power_mw: mW =1 [0.1…5]; aim: ° =0 [-360…360]; on: bool =true; on_at: s =0 [0…20].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): on (On).
Notes: also called: laser, beam, light ray.
### mirror — Flat mirror · static (fixed in place)
A flat glass mirror on a stand, silvered on ONE side: its shiny face points in the direction `aim` (degrees: 0 = facing right, 90 = facing up, 180 = facing left); its back is opaque. Angle in = angle out: turning it by 10° turns the reflected beam by 20°. To send a beam that arrives travelling in direction A on in direction B, set aim = (A + 180 + B) / 2 (the face points half way between back along the incoming beam and along the outgoing one). Facts: 20 cm · 90 % reflected · one shiny face.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.006 × 0.2 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: width: m =0.2 [0.05…0.6]; reflectance: =0.9 [0.5…0.99]; aim: ° =180 [-360…360].
Notes: also called: reflect, reflection, periscope.
### curved-mirror — Curved mirror · static (fixed in place)
A round spherical mirror on a stand. Its shiny face points in the direction `aim`. Concave: parallel light meets at its focus, f in front; convex: light spreads as if from a point f behind it. Facts: Concave · f 15 cm · Ø 10 cm.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.0082 × 0.1 m; from the anchor x −0.0042…+0.004, y −0.05…+0.05.
Props: curve: *concave* | convex; focal_length: m =0.15 [0.05…1]; diameter: m =0.1 [0.03…0.3]; aim: ° =180 [-360…360].
Notes: also called: concave, convex, focus, reflect.
### convex-lens — Convex lens · static (fixed in place)
A converging (magnifying) lens on a stand, its axis in the direction `aim` (0: light passes left ↔ right). Parallel light (the sun) meets at its focus, focal_length behind it; an object beyond 2f makes a smaller, upside-down image on a screen at d_i (1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i). Facts: f 10 cm · Ø 5 cm · crown glass.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.007 × 0.05 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: focal_length: m =0.1 [0.03…0.5]; diameter: m =0.05 [0.02…0.15]; glass: *crown glass* | flint glass | acrylic; aim: ° =0 [-360…360].
Notes: also called: magnifying glass, lens, focus, burning glass.
### concave-lens — Concave lens · static (fixed in place)
A diverging lens on a stand, its axis in the direction `aim`: parallel light spreads out as if from a point focal_length in front of it. Facts: f −10 cm · Ø 5 cm · crown glass.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.0081 × 0.05 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: focal_length: m =0.1 [0.03…0.5]; diameter: m =0.05 [0.02…0.15]; glass: *crown glass* | flint glass | acrylic; aim: ° =0 [-360…360].
Notes: also called: lens, diverging, spread.
### prism — Prism · static (fixed in place)
A 60° triangular glass prism on a stand (centred on its middle; apex up at aim 0). White light through it bends and splits into a rainbow (violet bends most). Aim the beam at one slanted face. Facts: 60° · 5 cm edges · crown glass.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.05 × 0.043 m; from the anchor x −0.025…+0.025, y −0.014…+0.029.
Props: edge: m =0.05 [0.02…0.15]; glass: *crown glass* | flint glass | acrylic; aim: ° =0 [-360…360].
Notes: also called: rainbow, spectrum, colours, dispersion.
### glass-block — Glass block · static (fixed in place)
A rectangular clear block (2 cm deep): a beam entering at a slant bends toward the normal inside and leaves parallel to how it came, shifted sideways. Glass `water`: a block of water (bends light less than glass). For light into a real tank of water use the liquids module's water tank or beaker: its water bends light too. Facts: 10 × 6 cm · 2 cm deep · n 1.52.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.1 × 0.06 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: width: m =0.1 [0.02…0.3]; height: m =0.06 [0.02…0.2]; glass: *crown glass* | flint glass | acrylic | water; aim: ° =0 [-360…360].
Notes: also called: refraction, bend light, block, water.

mod_softbody.title: Soft and bendy things (elastic and plastic): squashing clay, bouncing and how high it bounces, bending rulers, stretched and wound rubber bands, coil springs
mod_softbody.text:
### Soft and bendy things (elastic and plastic): squashing clay, bouncing and how high it bounces, bending rulers, stretched and wound rubber bands, coil springs
ELASTIC things squash, bend or stretch under a push and spring back (they store energy and give it back); PLASTIC things (soft-clay) squash and KEEP the dent. soft-clay: a modelling-clay ball (6 cm, 177 g): dropped or hit it flattens where it lands and stays flat, it barely bounces (dropped 1 m: a 7 mm flat); a heavy weight resting on it dents it a little; `softness` firm | normal | soft (warm clay dents deeper). Its force_n reads everything pressing on it (a 1 kg mass on it on the table: about 21 N, the mass's push and the table's). playground-ball (21.6 cm, 0.4 kg, `pressure` 14 kPa, at most 35), exercise-ball (65 cm, 1.1 kg, 4 kPa, at most 10) and foam-ball (7 cm squishy foam, `stiffness` kPa): they flatten where they land or are pressed and spring back round, bouncing. MORE AIR BOUNCES HIGHER: dropped 1 m (its bottom 1 m above the table) a playground ball's first bounce rises 0.27 m at 2 kPa (nearly flat), 0.41 m at 5, 0.55 m at 14, 0.61 m at 30 kPa; an exercise ball 0.20 m at 1 kPa, 0.39 m at 4, 0.46 m at 8. Less pressure (or softer foam) squashes more. Readings: squash_mm, force_n, energy_j (clay also dent_mm: the squash it keeps). Check a bounce with bounces {item, at_least_m?} or bounces_more {a, b}. Bending beams: flex-ruler is a ruler CLAMPED to a 10 × 5 cm wooden block that stands on the table; its anchor is the floor under the block's edge and its free part (`overhang`, default 0.2 m) sticks out to the right of x (`facing` left: to the left) at 5 cm + its thickness above the table. A load bends the end by F·a²·(3L − a)/(6EI) for a load centred a from the block's edge (at the very end, a = L: F·L³/(3EI)), so in a comparison put EVERY load's centre at the same distance from the block's edge: place {on: <ruler id>, x: <ruler x + overhang − (half the widest load's width + 0.01)>} on every ruler (gram-mass widths: 20 g 1.5 cm, 100 g 2.6 cm, 200 g 3.2 cm, 500 g 4.4 cm, 1 kg 5.5 cm; pennies, coin-flat, steel-washer, steel-weight-1kg too). Per 100 g at the end of 20 cm out: a wooden ruler (3.5 mm) about 2 mm, acrylic (3 mm) about 12 mm, aluminium (1.5 mm) about 4.5 mm, steel (0.5 mm) about 42 mm; twice the load twice the bend, twice the overhang 8 times. springboard (a diving board): a board bolted on a stand, its anchor the floor under the stand's edge, the board's top at stand_height + thickness. flex-plank: a plank, card strip or metal strip that rests on what is under it (anchor: the middle of its underside): lay it across two supports (two wooden-blocks or books, `fixed`, its ends resting on them) for a bridge that sags F·L³/(48·E·I) under a load in the middle. Wood and acrylic SNAP past their strength; steel, aluminium and card keep a permanent bend. Readings: bend_mm (the free end's drop, a plank's sag), energy_j, set_deg. band-launcher: a launch board (65 cm long, 12 mm thick: from 35 cm behind its anchor to 30 cm in front) with a rubber band between two posts at its anchor and the pouch (its tips 0.016·cos 25° in front of its back) pulled back `draw` m (default 0.1, at most 0.2: the band is then about 5 times its length; a rubber band SNAPS at 6 times, an event, and then throws nothing); put the thing to launch ON the board just in front of the pouch: place {on: <launcher id>, x: <launcher x − draw + half its length + 0.003>} (a toy-car's half length is 0.1 m; a ball's its radius) and set the band `height` above the board to the middle of the thing's back (a toy car 0.03, a ball its radius). At the release the band throws it forward (+x); tilt the launcher (angle_deg) to shoot up. Stored with 1 medium band: 0.13 J pulled 5 cm, 0.59 J at 10 cm, 1.5 J at 15 cm, 3.0 J at 20 cm (about as the square of the pull); each more band (`bands` 1-4) as much again; a thick `band` twice a medium one. A toy car on the board takes roughly half of it: pulled 15 cm it rolls about 3.8 m on a table, so give a launched car room or an end stop. Readings: stretch_cm, tension_n, energy_j, broken. Rubber-band cars: a toy-car, cart or truck with props {band_turns: 1-30} has a rubber band wound on its 3 mm rear axle that drives it forward when the scene lets go; `band_size` thin | medium (#64, default) | thick. On a table a toy car goes about: medium band 2 turns 0.4 m, 3 turns 0.9 m, 4 turns 1.5 m, 6 turns 3.1 m, 10 turns 7 m; thin band 5 turns 0.6 m, 10 turns 2 m, 15 turns 4 m, 20 turns 6.5 m; thick band 3 turns 1.8 m. So on a 3.7 m table compare few turns (2 vs 5 medium, or 5 vs 10 thin), or the car drives off its end. A band that pulls harder than the tyres grip SPINS THE WHEELS (an event) and the extra turns are wasted: a medium band past about 19 turns, a thick one past about 8; more turns never go less far. A 2 kg truck barely moves on one band. The distance comes from band_turns and band_size: never make a band car go farther with start_speed or a different surface under the other car. Readings: band_turns, band_stretch_cm, band_tension_n, band_energy_j. coil-spring: a coil spring on a base with a platform (anchor: the middle of the base's bottom; the platform's top about 2 cm + length above it): weights put on the platform (place {on: <spring id>}) squash it by weight ÷ stiffness (200 N/m: 4.9 mm per 100 g, 9.8 mm per 200 g: Hooke's law). Its readings are zeroed with its own platform resting on it, as a lab zeroes its scale: compression_mm (what the load squashes it), force_n (k × that: the load's weight), energy_j.
  - goal squashes {item, at_least_mm?}: it ends with a permanent dent at least that deep (default 1 mm): clay that keeps its squash
  - goal springs_back {item}: it squashes, bends or stretches at least 2 mm during the run and keeps no change of shape (no dent, no permanent bend, not snapped)
  - goal bends {item, at_least_mm?, at_most_mm?}: a ruler's, board's or plank's bend at the end (its free end's drop, a plank's sag) is within those mm (default at least 1); a bimetal-strip (the heat module's): its tip moves at least at_least_mm as it heats
  - goal deforms_more {a, b}: a ends more bent (or dented, or a spring more squashed; a ball's squash or a band's stretch at its most) than b, by 5 % and 0.2 mm or more (bends both under 1 mm: by a quarter and 0.02 mm; the result then says small)
  - goal stores {item, at_least_j?}: at its most it holds at least that much elastic energy (default 0.01 J): a stretched band, a bent board, a squashed spring or ball
  - goal bounces {item, at_least_m?, at_most_m?}: after its first landing it rises at least (at most) that high, its bottom over what it landed on (default at least 0.02 m): a dropped ball's first bounce
  - goal bounces_more {a, b}: a's first bounce rises higher than b's (by 5 % and 1 cm or more): a pumped-up ball against a flat one, dropped from the same height
  - knob flex-ruler.overhang: its bend grows as the overhang cubed: 26 % farther out bends it twice as much
  - knob flex-ruler.material: a stiffer material bends less: steel (E 200 GPa) and aluminium (69) at their usual thin gauges bend more than wood (12, 3.5 mm thick); acrylic (3.2) bends most of the thick ones (offered only for a ruler that is not compared with another: changing one of two would be a second difference)
  - knob flex-ruler.width: a wider ruler is stiffer: the bend falls as 1/width
  - knob springboard.length: the bend grows as the free length cubed
  - knob springboard.thickness_mm: the bend falls as the thickness cubed: a board twice as thick bends 8 times less
  - knob springboard.material: steel and aluminium are far stiffer than pine; acrylic and card far softer
  - knob flex-plank.length: a longer span sags more (∝ span³) — keep its ends on their supports
  - knob flex-plank.thickness_mm: the sag falls as the thickness cubed
  - knob flex-plank.width: the sag falls as 1/width
  - knob flex-plank.material: a stiffer material sags less (steel, aluminium, wood, pine, acrylic, card)
  - knob soft-clay.softness: soft clay flows at a lower pressure (0.08 MPa against 0.175 firm), so the same hit dents it deeper
  - knob soft-clay.diameter: a bigger ball is heavier (it lands harder) but spreads its flat wider
  - knob playground-ball.pressure: pumped harder it squashes less and bounces higher (dropped 1 m: 0.27 m at 2 kPa, 0.41 m at 5, 0.55 m at 14, 0.61 m at 30), levelling off past about 30 kPa (35 at most)
  - knob exercise-ball.pressure: pumped harder it squashes less under the same weight and bounces higher (dropped 1 m: 0.20 m at 1 kPa, 0.39 m at 4, 0.46 m at 8; 10 kPa at most)
  - knob foam-ball.stiffness: softer foam squashes more
  - knob band-launcher.draw: more stretch stores more energy (about as the square of the pull-back: 0.6 J at 10 cm, 3 J at 20 cm with one band), so it throws faster and farther; 20 cm at most (the band then 5 times its length: at 6 times it snaps)
  - knob band-launcher.bands: each more band pulls as hard again, storing more energy at the same pull-back
  - knob band-launcher.band: a wider band pulls harder (thin 1.6, medium 6.35, thick 12.7 mm wide)
  - knob coil-spring.stiffness: the squash is the weight divided by the stiffness
  - knob toy-car.band_turns: each turn winds 0.94 cm more band onto its 3 mm axle: more stored energy, a longer drive, until the band pulls harder than the tyres grip (a toy car: a medium band past about 19 turns, a thick one past about 8): then its wheels spin and the extra turns are wasted (offered only for a car that already has a band)
  - knob toy-car.band_size: a wider band stores more at the same turns (thick twice medium, medium 4 times thin) but spins the wheels sooner
  - knob cart.band_turns: each turn winds 0.94 cm more band onto its 3 mm axle: more stored energy, a longer drive, until the band pulls harder than the tyres grip (a toy car: a medium band past about 19 turns, a thick one past about 8): then its wheels spin and the extra turns are wasted (offered only for a car that already has a band)
  - knob cart.band_size: a wider band stores more at the same turns (thick twice medium, medium 4 times thin) but spins the wheels sooner
  - knob truck.band_turns: each turn winds 0.94 cm more band onto its 3 mm axle: more stored energy, a longer drive, until the band pulls harder than the tyres grip (a toy car: a medium band past about 19 turns, a thick one past about 8): then its wheels spin and the extra turns are wasted (offered only for a car that already has a band)
  - knob truck.band_size: a wider band stores more at the same turns (thick twice medium, medium 4 times thin) but spins the wheels sooner
  - e.g. "Does a ruler bend more with more coins on its end?": two flex-rulers (acrylic) at x 0.3 and 1.3, one with 2 pennies, one with 8 pennies on its end (place on the ruler at x + 0.185: the same distance from the block on both); goal deforms_more {a: ruler with 8, b: ruler with 2}
  - e.g. "Clay vs a bouncy ball dropped from 1 m": soft-clay and playground-ball held on air at y_m 1.0, 0.5 m apart; goals squashes {clay}, springs_back {ball}
  - e.g. "A ball pumped up with more air bounces higher": two playground-balls held on air at y_m 1.0, 0.6 m apart, pressure 20 and 3 kPa; goal bounces_more {a: the 20 kPa ball, b: the 3 kPa ball} (from 1 m about 0.59 m against 0.33 m)
  - e.g. "Pull a rubber band back farther to launch a car farther": two band-launchers (draw 0.05 and 0.15) in two lanes, a toy-car on each board in front of its pouch, room in front of each (the 15 cm one throws a car about 3.8 m on a table: an end stop or a long lane); goal farther {a: car of the 0.15 launcher, b: the other}
  - e.g. "Wind a rubber-band car more and it goes farther": two toy-cars in two lanes (one on a shelf plank above the other), props {band_turns: 5, band_size: thin} and {band_turns: 10, band_size: thin} (about 0.6 m and 2 m); goal farther {a: the 10-turn car, b: the 5-turn car}
  - e.g. "Hooke's law: hang more weight, more stretch": three coil-springs (200 N/m) 0.6 m apart with gram-masses 100 g, 200 g and 500 g on their platforms (place on: the spring); readings 4.9, 9.8 and 24.5 mm (zeroed with the platform on); goal deforms_more {a: the 500 g spring, b: the 200 g spring}
### soft-clay — Squashy clay ball · dynamic
A ball of modelling clay that SQUASHES: it flattens where it lands, is hit or pressed, and keeps the dent (it does not spring back or bounce). A heavy weight on it flattens it a little; a hard throw flattens it a lot. Facts: 6 cm · 177 g · keeps its dents.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.06 × 0.06 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: diameter: m =0.06 [0.02…0.2]; softness: firm | *normal* | soft.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): dent_mm (Dent (stays), mm), squash_mm (Squash now, mm), force_n (Pushing force, N).
Surface: material soft clay; bounce 0.05, friction 0.9, rolling 0.3, side 0.
Notes: also called: clay, plasticine, play-doh, squash, squish, dent, flatten, plastic, deform, keeps its shape.
### playground-ball — Playground ball · dynamic
A red rubber playground ball (8.5 inch). It flattens where it lands or is pressed and springs back round; pumped up harder it bounces higher. Facts: 21.6 cm · 0.4 kg · 14.0 kPa.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.216 × 0.216 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: diameter: m =0.216 [0.072…0.432]; mass: kg =0.4 [0.1…1.6]; pressure: kPa =14 [0.5…35].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): squash_mm (Squash, mm), force_n (Pushing force, N), energy_j (Stored energy, J).
Surface: material playground rubber; bounce 0.75, friction 0.7, rolling 0.02, side 0.
Notes: also called: ball, bouncy, bounce, squash, squishy, elastic, springs back, inflated, pumped up, flat ball.
### exercise-ball — Exercise ball · dynamic
A big, soft inflated exercise ball (65 cm). It squashes a lot under a weight or when it lands, and springs back. Facts: 65.0 cm · 1.1 kg · 4.0 kPa.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.65 × 0.65 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: diameter: m =0.65 [0.217…1.3]; mass: kg =1.1 [0.275…4.4]; pressure: kPa =4 [0.5…10].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): squash_mm (Squash, mm), force_n (Pushing force, N), energy_j (Stored energy, J).
Surface: material exercise PVC; bounce 0.65, friction 0.6, rolling 0.02, side 0.
Notes: also called: ball, bouncy, bounce, squash, squishy, elastic, springs back, inflated, pumped up, flat ball.
### foam-ball — Foam ball · dynamic
A squishy foam stress ball (7 cm). Squeeze it and it springs back. Slow foam (memory foam) barely bounces: a soft ball that lands and stays. Facts: 7 cm · 22 g · soft foam.
Anchor (x, y): its middle. Outline at defaults: 0.07 × 0.07 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: diameter: m =0.07 [0.03…0.2]; mass: kg =0.022 [0.005…0.2]; stiffness: kPa =100 [20…1000]; foam: *stress ball* | slow foam.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): squash_mm (Squash, mm), force_n (Pushing force, N), energy_j (Stored energy, J).
Surface: material polyurethane foam; bounce 0.55, friction 0.8, rolling 0.03, side 0.
Notes: also called: stress ball, foam, squishy, squeeze, elastic, springs back, soft, sponge ball, deform, soft ball.
### flex-ruler — Bending ruler · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A ruler clamped to a wooden block, sticking out over the block's edge. A load on its end bends it down (twice the load, twice the bend; twice as long, 8 times the bend), and it springs back straight when the load is gone. Wood and acrylic snap if bent too far; steel and aluminium keep a permanent bend. Facts: 30 cm wooden ruler · 20 cm over the edge. Moving parts ≈14.7 g.
Anchor (x, y): the floor under the block's edge, where the ruler leaves the block. Outline at defaults: 0.304 × 0.066 m; from the anchor x −0.104…+0.2, y +0…+0.066.
Props: overhang: m =0.2 [0.05…0.6]; length: m =0.3 [0.15…1]; thickness_mm: mm =0 [0…10]; width: m =0.03 [0.01…0.08]; facing: *right* | left.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): bend_mm (Bend, mm), energy_j (Stored energy, J), set_deg (Permanent bend, °), broken (Broken).
Surface: material *varnished hardwood* | acrylic | steel | aluminium; bounce 0.93, friction 0.45, rolling 0, side 0.
Notes: also called: ruler, bend, bending, cantilever, flex, springy, deflection, hooke, elastic, diving board.
### springboard — Diving board · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A board bolted on a stand at one end, its far end free (a diving board). A weight on the end bends it down; it springs back and can throw what lands on it. Facts: 1 m pine board · 18 mm · on a 30 cm stand. Moving parts ≈1.8 kg.
Anchor (x, y): the floor under the stand's edge, where the board leaves the stand. Outline at defaults: 1.2 × 0.338 m; from the anchor x −0.2…+1, y +0…+0.338.
Props: length: m =1 [0.2…5]; thickness_mm: mm =18 [1…80]; width: m =0.25 [0.03…0.6]; stand_height: m =0.3 [0.05…1.5]; facing: *right* | left.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): bend_mm (Bend, mm), energy_j (Stored energy, J), set_deg (Permanent bend, °), broken (Broken).
Surface: material *pine* | varnished hardwood | aluminium | steel | acrylic | card; bounce 0.6, friction 0.45, rolling 0.004, side 0.
Notes: also called: diving board, springboard, board, plank, bend, spring, cantilever, bounce, elastic, launch.
### flex-plank — Bendy plank · dynamic
A plank (or a card or metal strip) that rests on whatever is under it. Laid across two supports it is a bridge: it sags in the middle under a load (centre load: F·L³/(48EI)), springs back when unloaded; card creases and wood snaps when overloaded. Facts: 60 cm pine · 6 mm thick · 10 cm wide. Moving parts ≈144 g.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its underside. Outline at defaults: 0.6 × 0.006 m; from the anchor x −0.3…+0.3, y +0…+0.006.
Props: length: m =0.6 [0.1…5]; thickness_mm: mm =6 [0.3…60]; width: m =0.1 [0.01…0.6].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): bend_mm (Bend, mm), energy_j (Stored energy, J), set_deg (Permanent bend, °), broken (Broken).
Surface: material *pine* | varnished hardwood | aluminium | steel | acrylic | card; bounce 0.6, friction 0.45, rolling 0.004, side 0.
Notes: also called: bridge, plank, beam, board, card, strip, sag, bend, span, load.
### band-launcher — Rubber-band launcher · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A launch board with a rubber band stretched between two posts at its front, its pouch pulled back. Put a toy car, a block or a ball on the board just in front of the pouch: when the scene lets go the band snaps forward and flings it off the board's front end (tilt the launcher to shoot up). Pulled farther, it stores more energy. Facts: #64 band · pulled 10 cm · ≈ 0.6 J. Moving parts ≈3.56 g.
Anchor (x, y): the board's bottom under the posts. Outline at defaults: 0.65 × 0.05 m; from the anchor x −0.35…+0.3, y +0…+0.05.
Props: draw: m =0.1 [0…0.2]; bands: int =1 [1…4]; band: thin | *medium* | thick; spread: m =0.1 [0.09…0.3]; height: m =0.03 [0.005…0.3].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): stretch_cm (Band stretch, cm), tension_n (Pull, N), energy_j (Stored energy, J), broken (Snapped).
Notes: also called: rubber band, launcher, slingshot, catapult, elastic, stretch, energy, fling, shoot, launch.
### coil-spring — Coil spring · dynamic, on a fixed frame or pivot (it does not fall)
A coil spring standing on a base with a platform on top, kept upright by a guide. Weights on the platform squash it by weight ÷ stiffness (Hooke's law: twice the weight, twice the squash); it springs back when they are taken off. Facts: 200 N/m · 12 cm. Moving parts ≈44.8 g.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its base's bottom. Outline at defaults: 0.14 × 0.146 m; from the anchor x −0.07…+0.07, y +0…+0.146.
Props: stiffness: N/m =200 [10…5000]; rest_length: m =0.12 [0.03…0.4]; width: m =0.1 [0.04…0.3]; damping: N·s/m =0.5 [0…20].
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): compression_mm (Squashed by, mm), force_n (Spring force, N), energy_j (Stored energy, J).
Notes: has springs; also called: spring, coil, hooke, compress, squash, elastic, springs back, weigh, force, stiffness.

mod_space.title: Gravity and space (other worlds, orbits, the Moon's phases, eclipses, seasons, day and night on a globe)
mod_space.text:
### Gravity and space (other worlds, orbits, the Moon's phases, eclipses, seasons, day and night on a globe)
PLACES (gravity of other worlds): the scene's settings say where it is. settings.gravity: "earth" (9.81 m/s², the standard), "moon" (1.62), "mars" (3.71), "jupiter" (24.79), "none" (0: weightless), or a number of m/s² for other worlds [NASA fact sheets]: Mercury 3.7, Venus 8.87, Saturn 10.44, Uranus 8.87, Neptune 11.15, Pluto 0.62. settings.air false = a vacuum (no drag, no buoyancy: a feather and a hammer fall together). settings.air_density (kg/m³, with air on; left out: a room's 1.2) is a world's own air for drag and buoyancy [NASA fact sheets]: Mars 0.020 (thin: a 1 g craft feather from 2 m lands 1.06 s after the drop, a golf ball 1.03 s; in a vacuum both 1.04 s), Venus 65 (thick: anything lighter than 65 kg/m³, a craft feather or foam, floats up), Jupiter 0.16, Saturn 0.19, Neptune 0.45 (their 1-bar levels). Real places: the Moon, Mercury, Pluto: air false; Mars {gravity: "mars", air_density: 0.02}; Venus {gravity: 8.87, air_density: 65}; Jupiter {gravity: "jupiter", air_density: 0.16}; a space station: gravity "none", air true; outer space: "none", false. (A module's own air processes, balloons and jars, use a room's air.) Same drop on different worlds: fall time √(2h/g) (1 m: Earth 0.452 s, Moon 1.111 s, Mars 0.734 s, Jupiter 0.284 s). Weight W = m·g changes with the place (a spring scale reads it), mass does not (a pan balance reads the same).
ORBIT MODE (sun, planet, moon, satellite): a scene with any of them is in space: NO uniform gravity and NO air, automatically (the machine plane is the plane of the orbits, seen from above). Bodies pull every moving thing with their real gravity at the scene's SCALE, which the heaviest body sets (its `scale`: auto = the Sun's "inner-planets" 1 m = 1 au, 1 s = 40 days; Earth's "earth-moon" 1 m = 300,000 km, 1 s = 2 days; Jupiter's "jupiter-moons" 1 m = 1 million km, 1 s = 12 h; Mars's "mars-moons" 1 m = 20,000 km, 1 s = 2 h; "low-orbit" 1 m = 10,000 km, 1 s = 10 min (the Earth drawn true size, 1.27 m across: satellites, Newton's cannon); "custom" km_per_m + hours_per_s). Real distances in scene metres = km ÷ km per metre: the Moon 384,400 km = 1.28 m (earth-moon); Mercury 0.387 m, Venus 0.723, Earth 1.0, Mars 1.524 (inner-planets); the ISS 6,791 km from Earth's centre = 0.679 m (low-orbit: only 4.2 cm above the 1.274 m Earth, so keep a satellite small there, size ≤ 0.05 m, or it grazes the ground); Io 0.422, Europa 0.671, Ganymede 1.070 (jupiter-moons). Newton's cannon: the Earth (low-orbit, fixed) with cannonballs (satellite kind cannonball, size 0.03-0.04) stacked straight above its top 6 cm apart, the lowest at 0.68 m from its centre: orbit_factor 0.7 falls back, 1.0 circles, 1.45 escapes.
Placing an orbit scene: the central body on "air" (place {on: "air", x, y_m}) at the middle, high enough that every orbit clears the table top (y = 0): centre y ≥ radius + 0.15 m; each orbiting body to its right at its distance (x = centre x + distance, same y), place on "air"; its `primary` link = the body it circles; orbit_factor 1 = a circle (counter-clockwise), 0.7 falls in, 1.2 an ellipse (it swings out to r·f²/(2 − f²)), 1.42 escapes. Set the stage (x0 x1 y0 y1) to hold every orbit with 0.2 m to spare, and seconds ≥ the periods you want to show (≤ 20). Real periods at the scale: Moon 13.7 s (earth-moon); Mercury 2.2 s, Venus 5.6 s, Earth 9.1 s, Mars 17.2 s (inner-planets); ISS 9.3 s (low-orbit); Io 3.5 s, Europa 7.1 s, Ganymede 14.3 s (jupiter-moons). MOON PHASES: the earth-moon scale (Earth at the middle, the Moon 1.28 m out, primary earth, orbit_factor 1) with a sun that only shines (props {pulls: false}) at one side of the stage: its light is parallel, as the real far Sun's, and the moon's phase as Earth sees it is read every moment (new when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun, full when Earth is between); never a pulling Sun near an Earth-Moon pair (the real Sun is 390 times farther away than the Moon: at a visible distance its pull tears them apart). The run shows the sidereal month (27.3 days), the phases in order. Sizes are automatic (true size at the scale, else a visible size, larger than true: say so); `fixed` holds a body still.
SHADOWS (gnomon, a shadow stick standing on the table or floor, its foot its anchor): latitude (Austin 30.27, + north), date (season: an equinox, a solstice, or day_of_year), solar time `hour` (12 = noon). The clock runs at the scene's settings.time_lapse: 3600 sweeps an hour a second (hour 8, seconds 8.5: 8:00 → 16:00). The shadow is drawn on the ground (the machine plane runs east-west: east to the right, north into the picture), shortest at solar noon pointing north (north of the tropics), toward the west in the morning and the east in the afternoon; the noon shadow is short in June, long in December (north). Readings: sun_elevation, sun_azimuth, shadow_m, shadow_dir, day_length_h; goal shadow_length {item, m, at_s?}. Austin, equinox: noon 0.58 m for a 1 m stick (Sun 59.7° up), 9:00 1.30 m; June solstice noon 0.12 m, December 1.36 m.
A geologist's hammer (rock-hammer, Apollo 15's 1.32 kg) for drop races: held (held: true) side by side with a feather, a ball or a paper at the same height, settings Moon + air false: they land together (goal lands_together).
CLASSROOM SUN-EARTH-MOON MODELS (globe, moon-ball: side view on the table, ordinary gravity; NOT orbit mode, so no sun item: a lamp plays the Sun). The light: the desk lamp (heat module) at one end of the table, head_height 0.4, target the globe (or a flashlight, or sunlight); a globe's or ball's lit_by link names it (none: the first light of the scene). globe = a 30 cm classroom globe on a stand, its foot on the table (y 0), its middle 0.40 m up (stand_height 0.25: level with the lamp's bulb), 0.8-1.5 m from the lamp: spin_rpm (6 = one turn, one day, every 10 s), tilt_deg 23.44, lean = where its north pole leans, kept so ("toward the camera" or "away from the camera" with the lamp to one side = an equinox; "toward the light" = the June solstice; "away from the light" = December's; right/left fixed in the room), start_hour (the town's solar time at the start: 6 sunrise, 12 noon, 18 sunset), town_lat (a red pin; Austin 30.27). The half facing the light is day; readings day (1/0), local_time, sun_elevation, noon_elevation, sun_lat (where the light is overhead), day_length_h, turns; events sunrise/sunset. Goals day_night {item: globe, is: "day"|"night", at_s?} or {item, days: n} (n sunrises and sunsets), noon_sun {item, deg, tol?}. Seasons on the table: one globe a run (a globe in line with another shades it: the readings do not see that shadow, the picture does), its middle level with the light: leaning toward the light = June (noon 83.2° at Austin, 13.9 h of day), away from it = December (36.3°, 10.1 h), to the side = an equinox (59.7°, 12.0 h); a light above the globe's middle raises where it is overhead (sunlight comes from 5° up at least). One run with the whole year: the Earth round the Sun in orbit mode with seasons on (below).
moon-ball = a white foam ball (Ø 7.5 cm) on a stick carried round a globe: its anchor is the circle's centre, so give it the globe's x and y (with around = the globe the centre IS the globe's middle); radius 0.6 m, period_s 12 (one trip = one month), start_deg 0 new moon (between the lamp and the globe), 90 first quarter, 180 full (behind the globe), 270 last quarter; it goes counter-clockwise seen from above (first quarter comes toward the camera when the lamp is on the left). tilt_deg 30 with node_deg 90 (the default) carries it above the globe's shadow at full and below the lamp's line at new: no eclipses; tilt_deg 0 (level) or node_deg 0: a lunar eclipse at full (the globe's shadow on the ball) and a solar one at new (the ball's shadow on the globe). Without a globe it goes round its own place (a viewer's eye: the head model). Readings elongation, lit, height, lunar_eclipse (0 none, 1 penumbral, 2 partial, 3 total), solar_eclipse (0, 1 partial, 2 annular, 3 total). Goals phase {item: the ball, name, any?, at_s?}, eclipse {type: "lunar"|"solar", item: the ball, total?, none?}.
ECLIPSES and SEASONS in orbit mode. The Moon's orbit is tilted 5.145° (moon orbit_tilt, automatic by body) and node_deg says where it crosses the Earth's orbit plane, from the Sun's direction at the start (default 90: high at full, low at new: NO eclipse this month, as most months; 0: the nodes line up with the Sun: a solar eclipse at the new moon and a lunar one at the full). Readings height_km, latitude (° above the plane), lunar_eclipse, solar_eclipse from the REAL sizes and distances (the bodies are drawn larger than true; the view lifts the Moon by the same factor so its drawn shadow matches). At the Moon's mean distance (the circle at 384,400 km) a central solar eclipse is annular: a total one needs it nearer (start it at perigee, 363,300 km = 1.211 m at the earth-moon scale, orbit_factor 1.027). Goals eclipse {type, item: the moon, total?, central? (solar: annular or total), none?, at_s?}, solar_eclipse {item, ...}, lunar_eclipse {item, ...}. SEASONS: a planet with seasons true (axis_tilt automatic: Earth 23.44), start_date (the date at the start: where its pole leans from the Sun), town_lat: its axis keeps pointing one way all round its orbit, so the Sun at noon climbs and sinks through the year: readings sun_lat, noon_elevation, day_length_h; goal noon_sun {item: the planet, deg, tol?, at_s?}; and night_lon, the midnight sky's ecliptic longitude (opposite the Sun: the stars change with the seasons): goal night_sky {item: the planet, constellation (the zodiac's 13 or Orion), at_s?, any?}: Orion high at midnight in December-January (night_lon 70-100°), Scorpius and Sagittarius in June-July. Sun at the middle (inner-planets: a year is 9.13 s), Earth 1 m out, start_date march equinox: noon at Austin 59.7° → 83.2° (June, a quarter year: 2.28 s) → 59.7° → 36.3° (December).
  - goal shadow_length {item: gnomon, m, tol?, at_s?}: the shadow stick's shadow is m metres long (within tol, default 2 cm) at the end or at at_s (the clock runs at the scene's time_lapse)
  - goal orbits {item, around?, turns?}: it completes `turns` (default 1) turns round what it circles without falling in (orbit mode)
  - goal falls_in {item, into?}: it falls onto `into` (default: what it circles), e.g. a satellite launched too slowly
  - goal escapes {item}: at the end it is leaving what it circled for good (faster than escape speed, moving away)
  - goal lands_together {a, b, tol_s?}: the two first land (strike anything but each other) within tol_s (default 0.02 s) of each other (a vacuum drop)
  - goal lands_first {a, b}: a lands (strikes anything but b) at least 0.02 s before b (air slows the light, broad one)
  - goal phase {item: moon, name, at_s?, any?}: the moon shows that phase as its planet sees it (needs a sun in the scene), at the end, at at_s, or any: true at some moment
  - goal day_night {item: globe, is?: "day"|"night", at_s?, days?}: it is day (or night) at the globe's town at at_s (default the end); with days n: the town sees n sunrises and n sunsets
  - goal eclipse {type: "solar"|"lunar", item: the moon or moon-ball, total?, central? (solar: annular or total), none? (it never happens), at_s?}: that eclipse happens during the run (or at at_s): the moon's shadow on its planet or globe (solar), the planet's or globe's shadow on the moon (lunar)
  - goal solar_eclipse {item: the moon or moon-ball, total?, central?, none?, at_s?}: its shadow falls on its planet (the globe) during the run
  - goal lunar_eclipse {item: the moon or moon-ball, total?, none?, at_s?}: its planet's (the globe's) shadow falls on it during the run
  - goal noon_sun {item: globe | planet with seasons, deg, tol? (default 1), at_s?}: the noon Sun's height at its town is deg degrees (at the end or at at_s)
  - goal night_sky {item: a planet with seasons, constellation, at_s?, any?}: that constellation stands highest at midnight (opposite the Sun along the ecliptic: the zodiac's 13, and Orion) at the end, at at_s, or any: true at some moment: the stars change with the seasons
  - knob gnomon.hour: the shadow is shortest at solar noon (12) and longer earlier and later; it points west in the morning, east in the afternoon
  - knob gnomon.height: the shadow grows in proportion to the stick's height (shadow = height / tan(sun's height))
  - knob gnomon.season: the noon Sun is highest at the June solstice in the north (shortest noon shadow), lowest in December
  - knob satellite.orbit_factor: 1 = a circle; slower falls in toward what it circles, faster swings out on an ellipse, 1.41× (√2) escapes
  - knob moon.orbit_factor: 1 = a circle; slower falls in toward what it circles, faster swings out on an ellipse, 1.41× (√2) escapes
  - knob planet.orbit_factor: 1 = a circle; slower falls in toward what it circles, faster swings out on an ellipse, 1.41× (√2) escapes
  - knob planet.mass_scale: a heavier body pulls harder: what circles it at the same speed falls in, at the same launch factor it circles faster
  - knob sun.mass_scale: a heavier body pulls harder: what circles it at the same speed falls in, at the same launch factor it circles faster
  - knob moon.mass_scale: a heavier body pulls harder: what circles it at the same speed falls in, at the same launch factor it circles faster
  - knob moon.primary (a link): a body is launched round its primary only
  - knob satellite.primary (a link): a body is launched round its primary only
  - knob moon.node_deg: eclipses come only when the Moon's tilted orbit crosses the Earth's near the Sun line: nodes at 0 or 180° from the Sun give eclipses at this new and full moon, 90° none
  - knob moon.orbit_tilt: the real Moon's orbit is tilted 5.145°: flatter, it is eclipsed every month (change it only when asked)
  - knob planet.start_date: where it is in its year at the start: the June solstice leans its north pole toward the Sun (the noon Sun highest), December's away
  - knob planet.town_lat: the noon Sun is 90° − |latitude − where the Sun is overhead| high
  - knob globe.start_hour: the town's solar time at the start: 6 sunrise, 12 noon (the light highest), 18 sunset, 0 midnight
  - knob globe.spin_rpm: one turn is one day and one night: faster turns pass more days in the run
  - knob globe.lean: toward the light: the north's summer (the noon light high, long days); away: its winter; to the side: an equinox
  - knob globe.town_lat: nearer the pole leaning toward the light the days are longer and the noon light higher
  - knob globe.tilt_deg: the Earth's is 23.44°: with none there are no seasons (the light overhead at the equator all year)
  - knob moon-ball.start_deg: 0 between the light and the globe (new moon), 90 first quarter, 180 behind the globe (full), 270 last quarter
  - knob moon-ball.period_s: one trip round is one month of phases: a longer trip shows each phase longer
  - knob moon-ball.tilt_deg: a level circle puts the ball in the globe's shadow at full (a lunar eclipse) and its shadow on the globe at new (a solar one); tilted 30° it misses both
  - knob moon-ball.node_deg: where the tilted circle crosses the level one: 90° from the light keeps it out of the shadows, 0 or 180 lines the crossings up with the light (eclipses)
  - knob moon-ball.radius: further from the globe the globe's shadow and the ball's matter less
  - e.g. "Drop a hammer and a feather together on the Moon from 1.6 m": settings {gravity: "moon", air: false}; rock-hammer and a feather held at y 1.6; goal lands_together
  - e.g. "Drop a golf ball from 1 m on Earth, the Moon, Mars and Jupiter": four runs, settings.gravity earth / moon / mars / jupiter with air false (the pure √(2h/g) times; a golf ball barely feels Mars's or Jupiter's air over 1 m); fall times 0.452 / 1.111 / 0.734 / 0.284 s
  - e.g. "Drop a feather and a ball on Mars": settings {gravity: "mars", air_density: 0.02} (Mars's thin air); a craft feather (kind craft) and a golf ball held side by side at y 2.0; the feather lands a little later (1.06 s vs 1.03 s): goal lands_first {a: ball, b: feather}; on the Moon (air false) they land together
  - e.g. "Jump with the same push on Earth and on the Moon": two steel balls held on the table with start_speed 3 and start_dir 90 (straight up), one scene with settings gravity earth, one with moon, air false: peaks v²/2g = 0.46 m and 2.78 m
  - e.g. "Show the ISS going around the Earth": planet earth scale low-orbit, fixed, on air at (1.3, 1.5); satellite kind space-station size 0.04 at (1.979, 1.5) (420 km up), primary earth, orbit_factor 1; seconds 10; goal orbits (92.9 minutes = 9.3 s)
  - e.g. "Show the Moon circling the Earth": planet earth on air at (0.9, 1.45), moon at (2.18, 1.45) primary earth, orbit_factor 1, seconds 14, stage x0 -0.6 x1 3.4 y0 -0.2 y1 3.0; goal orbits {item: moon, around: earth}
  - e.g. "Newton's cannon: one ball falls back, one orbits, one escapes": planet earth scale low-orbit (1.27 m across), fixed, on air at (1.3, 1.0); three satellites kind cannonball size 0.03 stacked above its top at y 1.68, 1.74, 1.80 with orbit_factor 1.0, 0.7, 1.45 and primary earth; seconds 11; goals orbits, falls_in, escapes
  - e.g. "Mercury goes round the Sun faster than Earth": sun (inner-planets) at the middle, mercury 0.387 m and earth 1.0 m out, orbit_factor 1; goals orbits for both (Mercury 4 turns in 9.1 s)
  - e.g. "Show the phases of the Moon": sun {pulls: false} on air at the stage's left (x -0.35, y 1.45), earth at (1.6, 1.45), moon 1.28 m from it toward the Sun (x 0.32) with primary earth, orbit_factor 1, seconds 14.5; goals phase {item: moon, name: full moon, any: true} and orbits {item: moon}
  - e.g. "Things float in a space station": settings {gravity: "none", air: true}; items stay where they are let go
  - e.g. "Show how a flagpole's shadow changes from 8 in the morning to 4 in the afternoon in Austin": gnomon height 1 on the table, latitude 30.27, season march equinox, hour 8; settings {time_lapse: 3600}; seconds 8.5; goal shadow_length {item, m: 0.58, at_s: 4} (noon)
  - e.g. "Compare the noon shadow in June and December": two gnomons side by side, hour 12, season june solstice and december solstice: 0.12 m vs 1.36 m at Austin
  - e.g. "Show day and night on a spinning globe lit by a lamp": lamp at (0.25, 0) head_height 0.4, target globe; globe at (1.3, 0) spin_rpm 6, start_hour 6, town_lat 30.27; seconds 20; goal day_night {item: globe, days: 1}
  - e.g. "Why do we have seasons? Compare the noon Sun in June and December": two runs of one scene (a globe in line with another would sit in its shadow): lamp at (0.25, 0) head_height 0.4 target globe; globe at (1.3, 0) town_lat 30.27, spin_rpm 6, seconds 10; run 1 lean "toward the light" (June: goal noon_sun {item: globe, deg: 83.17}), run 2 lean "away from the light" (December: noon_sun 36.29); or the whole year in one run: Earth round the Sun with seasons on
  - e.g. "Moon phases with a ball on a stick around a globe": lamp at (0.2, 0) target globe; globe at (1.3, 0) spin_rpm 0; moon-ball at the globe's (1.3, 0.4) with around globe, radius 0.6, period_s 12, start_deg 0; seconds 12.5; goals phase {item: ball, name: full moon, any: true}, phase {item: ball, name: first quarter, any: true}
  - e.g. "Show a lunar eclipse with the classroom model": as the phases model but the moon-ball tilt_deg 0 (level), start_deg 150, period_s 12, seconds 3; goal eclipse {type: lunar, item: ball, total: true}
  - e.g. "Show a total lunar eclipse with the real Sun, Earth and Moon": sun {pulls: false} on air at (-0.45, 1.45), earth at (1.6, 1.45), moon at (2.88, 1.45) primary earth (the full side), node_deg 0, seconds 3 (the Moon's 1.28 m circle must clear the drawn Sun); goal eclipse {type: lunar, item: moon, total: true}
  - e.g. "Why isn't there an eclipse every month?": sun {pulls: false} at (-0.45, 1.45), earth at (1.6, 1.45), moon at (2.88, 1.45) primary earth with its real tilt (5.145°, automatic) and node_deg 90; seconds 14.5 (a month); goals phase full moon any, phase new moon any, eclipse {type: lunar, item: moon, none: true}, eclipse {type: solar, item: moon, none: true}
  - e.g. "Why do we see different stars in winter and summer?": the seasons scene below (sun at the middle, earth 1 m out with seasons true, start_date december solstice), seconds 9.7; goals night_sky {item: earth, constellation: Orion, at_s: 0} and night_sky {item: earth, constellation: Sagittarius, any: true}
  - e.g. "Show Earth's seasons as it goes around the Sun": sun at (1.4, 1.45) (inner-planets scale), planet earth at (2.4, 1.45) primary sun with seasons true, start_date march equinox, town_lat 30.27; stage x0 0 x1 2.9 y0 0.2 y1 2.7 (Earth's 1 m orbit); seconds 9.7 (a year); goals noon_sun {item: earth, deg: 83.17, tol: 1, at_s: 2.78} (June) and orbits {item: earth}
### sun — Sun · dynamic
The Sun in an orbit scene (seen from above the plane of the orbits): it pulls everything with its real gravity at the scene's scale and lights the planets and moons (their phases). A scene with a space body is in space: no uniform gravity, no air. Facts: 1.99e30 kg · 1 m = 1 au, 1 s = 40 days.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.3 × 0.3 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: diameter: m =0.3 [0.005…3] auto (follows scale, km_per_m unless set); mass_scale: (× real) =1 [0.01…100]; pulls: bool =true; scale: *auto* | inner-planets | earth-moon | low-orbit | jupiter-moons | mars-moons | custom; km_per_m: km =300000 [100…10000000000]; hours_per_s: h =48 [0.01…100000].
Notes: also called: space, orbit, gravity, solar system, astronomy, star, solar, sunlight.
### planet — Planet · dynamic
A planet with its real mass (Earth, Mars, Jupiter ...): it pulls with its real gravity at the scene's scale and, at the release, is launched round what it circles (the Sun) at its Launch speed (1 = a circle). Moons and satellites circle it. With Seasons on, its tilted axis keeps pointing one way all round its orbit: the noon Sun at a town climbs to the June solstice and sinks to December's. Facts: Earth 5.97e24 kg · launched at 1× orbit speed.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.11 × 0.11 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: body: *earth* | mercury | venus | mars | jupiter | saturn | uranus | neptune | pluto; diameter: m =0.11 [0.005…3] auto (follows body, scale, km_per_m unless set); mass_scale: (× real) =1 [0.01…100]; orbit_factor: (× orbit speed) =1 [0…3]; direction: *counter-clockwise* | clockwise; scale: *auto* | inner-planets | earth-moon | low-orbit | jupiter-moons | mars-moons | custom; km_per_m: km =300000 [100…10000000000]; hours_per_s: h =48 [0.01…100000]; seasons: bool =false; axis_tilt: ° =23.44 [0…180] auto (follows body unless set); start_date: *march equinox* | june solstice | september equinox | december solstice; town_lat: ° =30.27 [-90…90]; primary: link → the id of a sun | planet (What it is launched round (none: the body that dominates it, the Sun)).
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): distance (Distance to what it circles, m), distance_km (Real distance, km), speed (Speed round it, m/s), speed_kms (Real speed, km/s), turns (Orbits completed), fell (Fell in), escaped (Escaping), sun_lat (Latitude the Sun is overhead, °), noon_elevation (Noon Sun's height at the town, °), day_length_h (Day length at the town, h), night_lon (Midnight sky's ecliptic longitude, °).
Notes: acts at the scene's release time; also called: space, orbit, gravity, solar system, astronomy, earth, mars, jupiter, saturn, venus.
### moon — Moon · dynamic
A moon with its real mass (Earth's Moon, Io, Titan ...): at the release it is launched round its planet at its Launch speed (1 = a circle). With a Sun in the scene its phase as its planet sees it is read every moment (new, first quarter, full ...), and its eclipses: its orbit is tilted (the Moon's 5.145°), so its shadow (a solar eclipse) or its planet's (a lunar one) falls only near the nodes, where the tilted orbit crosses the planet's. Facts: 7.35e22 kg · circles the Earth in 27.3 days.
Anchor (x, y): its centre. Outline at defaults: 0.347 × 0.347 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: body: *moon* | io | europa | ganymede | callisto | titan | phobos | deimos; diameter: m =0.03 [0.005…3] auto (follows body, scale, km_per_m unless set); mass_scale: (× real) =1 [0.01…100]; orbit_tilt: ° =5.145 [0…90] auto (follows body unless set); node_deg: ° =90 [0…360]; orbit_factor: (× orbit speed) =1 [0…3]; direction: *counter-clockwise* | clockwise; scale: *auto* | inner-planets | earth-moon | low-orbit | jupiter-moons | mars-moons | custom; km_per_m: km =300000 [100…10000000000]; hours_per_s: h =48 [0.01…100000]; primary: link → the id of a planet | sun | moon (What it is launched round (none: the body that dominates it)).

### satellite — Satellite · dynamic
A satellite (or a space station, a probe, Newton's cannonball) launched sideways at the release round a planet or moon at its Launch speed: 1 = a circular orbit, slower falls in, 1.41 or more escapes. Its own weight does not change its orbit. Facts: launched at 1× orbit speed · pulls nothing. Moving parts ≈190 g.

### rock-hammer — Geologist's hammer · dynamic
A geologist's hammer lying on its side (its head upright at the right end). Dropped with a feather where there is no air (the Moon), both land together, as David Scott showed on Apollo 15. Facts: 1.32 kg · 33 cm.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its length, on the handle's axis. Outline at defaults: 0.33 × 0.17 m, centred on the anchor.
Props: mass: kg =1.32 [0.3…3]; length: m =0.33 [0.2…0.5].
Notes: also called: hammer, apollo, moon, drop, gravity, vacuum, feather, falling, galileo, tool.
### gnomon — Shadow stick (gnomon) · static (fixed in place)
A stick standing on level ground in the Sun: its shadow is long in the morning and evening, shortest at solar noon, and points away from the Sun (west in the morning, east in the afternoon, north at noon north of the tropics). Set the place (latitude), the date and the time; with the scene's time-lapse (3600: an hour a second) the shadow sweeps round through the day. The machine plane runs east-west. Facts: 1 m stick · Austin, March equinox, 9:00.
Anchor (x, y): the foot of the stick, on the ground. Outline at defaults: 0.03 × 1 m; from the anchor x −0.015…+0.015, y +0…+1.

Notes: also called: shadow, sun, gnomon, sundial, flagpole, stick, day, night, seasons, noon.
### globe — Classroom globe · static (fixed in place)
A 30 cm classroom globe on its stand, its axis tilted 23.44° (kept pointing one way), turning west to east, a red pin at a town. A lamp (or flashlight, or sunlight) plays the Sun: the half facing it is day, the other half night; the town passes from night to day once a turn. With its pole leaning toward the light it is the north's summer (the noon light high, long days), away from it winter. Facts: Ø 30 cm · tilted 23.44° · 6 turns a minute.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of its base, on the table. Outline at defaults: 0.3 × 0.55 m; from the anchor x −0.15…+0.15, y +0…+0.55.
Props: diameter: m =0.3 [0.1…0.6]; stand_height: m =0.25 [0.03…1]; tilt_deg: ° =23.44 [0…90]; lean: *toward the camera* | away from the camera | right | left | toward the light | away from the light; spin_rpm: turns/min =6 [0…60]; start_hour: h =6 [0…24]; town_lat: ° =30.27 [-90…90]; lit_by: link → the id of a lamp | flashlight | sunlight | sun (The light that plays the Sun (none: the first lamp, flashlight, sunlight or sun in the scene)).

### moon-ball — Moon ball on a stick · static (fixed in place)
A white foam ball on a stick carried round a globe (or round a viewer's eye) under a lamp, as the Moon goes round the Earth: seen from the middle it shows its phases in order (new, crescent, first quarter, gibbous, full ...). Carried level, it is eclipsed at full and shades the globe at new; carried on a tilted circle (as the real Moon's is tilted 5°) it misses the shadows most of the time. Facts: Ø 7.5 cm · 0.6 m out · 12 s a trip.
