mod_staging.title: Filming (fixed camera, starting gates)
mod_staging.text:
### Filming (fixed camera, starting gates)
Render only (the physics is untouched). settings.camera = {x0, x1, y, pitch?, hfov?} fixes the side camera: the machine plane spans x0…x1 m across the picture at height y m (the picture's centre line), looking down pitch° (default 6.843, the Wide shot's) through a lens of hfov° across (default 69.39, the Wide shot's 26 mm; 10-25 for a long track seen almost flat, so its metre marks are evenly spaced). Every run with the same camera is filmed from the same place: lanes run apart (one per run) line up pixel for pixel when stacked. Without it the Wide shot frames each run by itself (and never wider than x -1.5…4.5 m). start_gate: true on a HELD ball, toy vehicle or block (held: true, and the scene's release time) draws a starting gate instead of the pull pin: a dark bar on a post behind the track whose stop touches the item's front (its downhill side) and lifts away at the release; the item still starts exactly at rest at the release. turn_to_camera (degrees, 0-60) on a fan draws it turned toward the camera so its face and turning blades show (30 reads well); its air still blows the way it points.

mod_waves.title: Sound and waves
mod_waves.text:
### Sound and waves
Sound comes from something vibrating: a tuning-fork, plucked-ruler, drum, monochord (one guitar string), rubber-band (shoebox guitar), xylophone-bar, speaker, clapper or bell-jar sounds at its strike_at time (hits × every s apart), as loud as its strength (twice the strength = twice the vibration = 6 dB louder). Its PITCH is set by its own size and tightness: tuning-fork `pitch` (Hz); plucked-ruler `overhang` (shorter = higher, ∝ 1/overhang²; it clamps itself to the table's right edge, or its left edge with edge "left": two rulers = one on each edge); drum `tension` (∝ √tension) and `diameter`; monochord `length` (∝ 1/length), `tension` (∝ √tension), `gauge` (heavier = lower); rubber-band `width` (wider = lower), `length`, `tension`; xylophone-bar `length` (∝ 1/length²); glass-bottle `fill` (tapped: more water = lower; blown: more water = higher). A sound-meter is the LISTENER (no people): it reads dB (A-weighted by default) where its microphone is; sound falls 6 dB per doubling of distance, arrives after distance ÷ 343 m/s, reflects off Wall items (an echo: the meter's `echo` reading is the delay) and is soaked up by a sound-panel (foam, curtain). In a vacuum (scene settings.air false) nothing travels through the air; the bell-jar shows that by pumping its own jar empty. A meter set to listen "touching" and pressed against a steel-rod, wooden-rod, plank or the table also hears what that solid carries (faster than air: steel 5050 m/s); a hydrophone's probe hung under the water of a water-tank (Liquids) hears a source in that water at 1481 m/s. An oscilloscope's microphone (on a little stand 21 cm to its right, or left with mic_side) listens like a meter and its screen draws the wave it hears: louder = taller waves (amplitude: `scale` Pa a square), higher = more waves across its 10 squares (pitch × 10 × `time_base`: 440 Hz at 1 ms a square shows 4.4 waves). Rice grains laid ON a drum's head jump when it is struck (harder = higher). A ball that hits a drum, fork or xylophone bar sounds it. Sound lines and audio in the video are automatic. Waves: a wave-rope (v = √(tension ÷ weight per metre)) or slinky (push and pull = compressions like sound; v = L·√(k/m)) is shaken at its left end by a driver (one pulse or keep shaking at `frequency`); its far end is tied (a pulse comes back upside down), a ring on a pole (same way up) or runs on (nothing comes back): use those two on a rope lying "on the floor" (held up, a free end hangs μgL²/(2T) down onto the table); a ribbon on it only moves across (the wave carries energy, not the rope); driven at f = n·v/(2L) a tied rope shows n standing loops (goal standing {item, loops}): give it a SMALL shake (amplitude ≤ 0.02 m), damping ≥ 1 (the default 1.5 is a real rope's) and ≥ 4 s, and the picture settles within a few seconds; a big shake or damping 0 makes loops that never settle. A rope is cut into segments of ≤ 2.5 cm and ≥ 10 a wavelength (up to 800): waves shorter than about 4 segments do not travel (a warning says so). A held-up rope or Slinky lies on the table where it would sag or swing below it. Rice on a drum (or a ball on a fork) is thrown only by the drum's own strikes (strike_at, hits), never by landing on it; strike it AFTER the scene's release (release + 0.3 s): the head rings only ≈ 0.2 s, so a strike before the grains are let go throws them little. Every drum hit moves its head at the same speed for the same strength (loose or tight: rice jumps alike); harder (strength) throws higher (× strength²); a heavy thing on a drum barely moves. A ripple-tank's dipper makes water waves (wavelength from frequency, depth and the scene's gravity); its duck or cork bobs in place (goal stays_put); a ripple tank always stays level. Goals for waves: wave_reaches, reflects, standing, wavelength {item, m}, wave_speed {item, m_s}, stays_put; for an oscilloscope's picture: trace {oscilloscope, waves_across, squares_high}. Pendulum timing: a pendulum's period is 2π√(L/g) (the `period` goal measures it). A string-telephone is two paper cups with a string between their bottoms, held level (no stand: place it on: air, y_m 0.2-0.5 over the table; its anchor is the string's middle, so its cups reach length/2 + 0.09 m either side: give the stage room). Its own child talks into its LEFT cup (voice: whisper by default, quiet, normal, loud, shout, or none for a speaker or fork put at that cup; talk_at, talk_for). Pulled taut (pull 2-10 N, 5 by default) the string carries the sound to its RIGHT cup: about 24 dB under what goes into the left cup for 3 m of cotton string (3 dB more a metre; steel wire about 16 dB; fishing line 29 but only 0.5 dB more a metre). The ear is a sound-meter with its microphone at the right cup's mouth: meter x = phone.x + length/2 + 0.12, its height = the phone's height over what the meter stands on (within 50 cm of a cup's mouth it hears the string; the voice goes either way). A whisper reaches it through the string (about 39 dB(A)) but not through the air (about 30 dB 3 m away, under a quiet room's 35). Slack (pull 0), drooping (under about 0.2 N) or pinched (pinched true) it carries nothing or little: only the air is left. Its readings: carries (0/1), loss_db, sag_mm, string_ms (≈ 1600 m/s along cotton: faster than the air). Goals: hears {meter, source: the telephone} and, for a slack or pinched one, hears {meter, source, expect: false}.
  - goal sounds {source, pitch_hz?, tol_hz?, at_least_db?}: the source (a tuning fork, drum, ruler, string, bar, speaker, clapper, bell, buzzer) makes a sound during the run, at that pitch (within tol_hz, default 2 %), at least that loud 1 m away
  - goal higher {a, b}: a's note is higher (a higher pitch, more vibrations a second) than b's; both must sound
  - goal louder {a, b, at?}: a is louder than b (two sound meters: their loudest readings; two sources: their level 1 m away, or with at = a sound meter, how loud each is there)
  - goal hears {meter, source, at_least_db?, expect?}: the sound meter hears the source (its sound reaches the meter at least as loud as the quiet room, or at least at_least_db); expect false: it does not (a slack or pinched string-telephone)
  - goal echo {meter, delay_s?, tol?}: the sound meter hears an echo off a wall (delay_s after the first sound, within tol: default 5 ms; delay = extra path ÷ 343 m/s)
  - goal wave_reaches {item, x?, before_s?}: the wave on a wave rope or Slinky (or a ripple tank's ripples) reaches its far end, or x m along it, by before_s if given
  - goal reflects {item, way?}: a pulse on a wave rope or Slinky comes back from its far end, way "upside down" (a tied end), "same way up" (a ring on a pole) or "none" (it must not come back: the rope runs on)
  - goal jumps {item, min_m?}: something of the item (rice grains on a drum's head, a ball by a tuning fork) is thrown up at least min_m (default 5 mm) above where it started
  - goal standing {item, loops?}: a wave rope or Slinky kept shaking shows a standing wave of `loops` loops at the end (a tied line driven at f = n·v/(2L) shows n; give it damping ≥ 1 and a small shake, ≤ 2 cm, and at least 4 s)
  - goal wavelength {item, m?, tol?}: the waves on a wave rope, Slinky or ripple tank are m metres long (speed ÷ frequency; within tol m, default 5 %)
  - goal wave_speed {item, m_s?, tol?}: the waves on a wave rope (√(T/μ)), Slinky (L·√(k/m)) or ripple tank run at m_s m/s (within tol, default 5 %)
  - goal stays_put {item, max_drift_m?, min_bob_mm?}: what rides the waves bobs but goes nowhere: a ripple-tank's duck or cork bobs ≥ min_bob_mm (default 0.5) while drifting ≤ max_drift_m (default 1 cm); a wave rope's or Slinky's ribbon moves ≥ min_bob_mm and travels no more than max_drift_m along (waves carry energy, not the water or rope)
  - goal trace {oscilloscope, waves_across?, squares_high?, tol?}: an oscilloscope's screen at its loudest shows that many waves across (pitch × 10 × time a square) and that many squares high (its pressure ÷ Pa a square), each within tol × it (default 0.1 = 10 %); without numbers, that it shows a wave
  - goal period {item, seconds?, tol?}: the item (a pendulum, a rope pendulum, a swing, a weight on a hanging spring) swings back and forth, once every `seconds` (within tol, default 2 %), measured from the run (frequency = 1 ÷ period)
  - knob plucked-ruler.overhang: the ruler's pitch goes as 1 ÷ overhang²: 15 cm → 35 Hz, 10 cm → 79 Hz
  - knob monochord.length: a string's pitch goes as 1 ÷ its length: half as long is an octave higher
  - knob monochord.tension: pitch goes as √tension: four times the tension is an octave higher
  - knob rubber-band.tension: pitch goes as √tension
  - knob rubber-band.width: a wider band is heavier per length: lower pitch
  - knob xylophone-bar.length: a bar's pitch goes as 1 ÷ length²
  - knob drum.tension: a drum's pitch goes as √(head tension)
  - knob tuning-fork.pitch: the fork's pitch is its own (a shorter-pronged fork is higher)
  - knob drum.strength: twice the strength is twice the head's speed: +6 dB, and grains thrown off 2× faster (4× higher); a loose or a tight head throws them alike
  - knob tuning-fork.strength: twice the strength: +6 dB
  - knob plucked-ruler.strength: twice the strength: +6 dB
  - knob speaker.level: its level 1 m away, in dB
  - knob tuning-fork.strike_at: when it sounds
  - knob drum.strike_at: when it sounds; rice on it jumps only when it is struck after the scene lets things go (the head rings ≈ 0.2 s)
  - knob sound-meter.room: what it reads with nothing sounding
  - knob wave-rope.tension: v = √(tension ÷ weight per metre)
  - knob wave-rope.frequency: wavelength = speed ÷ frequency; a tied rope shows n loops at f = n·v/(2L)
  - knob wave-rope.amplitude: how far the driver moves the rope's end; a standing wave needs ≤ 2 cm to settle into clean loops
  - knob wave-rope.damping: how fast its motion dies away (1/s): a standing wave settles in about 3 ÷ damping seconds
  - knob wave-rope.length: a longer rope: the wave takes longer to cross; a tied rope's loops at f = n·v/(2L)
  - knob slinky.amplitude: how far the driver moves its end
  - knob wave-rope.far_end: tied: a pulse returns upside down; ring on a pole: the same way up; runs on: no reflection
  - knob slinky.stiffness: v = L·√(k/m)
  - knob slinky.frequency: wavelength = speed ÷ frequency
  - knob ripple-tank.frequency: faster dipping: shorter water waves (v = f·λ)
  - knob ripple-tank.depth: shallow water waves run at about √(g·depth)
  - knob ripple-tank.amplitude: how far the dipper bobs: the duck bobs that much where it floats
  - knob oscilloscope.scale: a smaller Pa a square draws the same sound taller
  - knob oscilloscope.time_base: a longer time a square shows more waves across
  - knob glass-bottle.fill: tapped, more water lowers the note; blown, more water (less air) raises it
  - knob bell-jar.air_left: the bell's sound reaching the room falls with the air in the jar
  - knob string-telephone.pull: a taut string carries the voice (2-10 N); under about 0.2 N it droops and carries little, at 0 nothing
  - knob string-telephone.pinched: a pinched string cannot vibrate past the fingers: nothing gets through
  - knob string-telephone.voice: a louder voice into the near cup is louder at the far one, and through the air too
  - knob string-telephone.length: cotton string loses about 3 dB a metre (fishing line 0.5, wire almost none)
  - e.g. "A shorter ruler makes a higher sound": two plucked-ruler items on the table's right edge (one per table or one at a time), overhang 0.15 and 0.10 (35 → 79 Hz); goal higher {a: the 10 cm one, b: the 15 cm one}
  - e.g. "Hit the drum harder and the rice jumps higher and it is louder": two drums (strength 0.5 and 1.0, or hits at different times), rice ON each head (rice y = drum height), struck 0.3 s or more after the release, a sound-meter between them; goals jumps {item: rice}, louder {a: harder drum, b: softer drum}
  - e.g. "The farther away, the quieter the tuning fork sounds": a tuning-fork and sound-meters 1, 2 and 4 m away (microphones at the fork's height); each doubling reads 6 dB less; goals hears {meter, source} and louder {a: near meter, b: far meter}
  - e.g. "An echo off a wall 17 m away comes back a tenth of a second later": a wide stage (x to 20 m), a clapper and a sound-meter just behind it, a Wall 17.15 m away (height 3); goal echo {meter, delay_s: 0.1}
  - e.g. "A guitar string an octave higher when it is half as long": two monochords: length 0.648 and 0.324 (329.6 → 659 Hz); goal higher {a: short, b: long}
  - e.g. "A pulse on a rope reflects upside down from the tied end": a wave-rope (length 4, tension 10 N, weight 0.1 kg/m: 10 m/s), shake one pulse, far_end tied to the post; goals wave_reaches {item: rope, before_s: 1}, reflects {item: rope, way: "upside down"}
  - e.g. "A standing wave with 3 loops on a rope": a wave-rope length 4, tension 10, weight 0.1 (v 10 m/s), keep shaking at f = 3·10/(2·4) = 3.75 Hz, amplitude 0.015, damping 1.5, seconds 6; goal standing {item: rope, loops: 3}
  - e.g. "A duck bobs on ripples but stays where it is": a ripple-tank (depth 0.02, frequency 5, floater duck at 0.6), seconds 4; goal stays_put {item: tank} (readings floater_bob_mm and floater_drift ≈ 0)
  - e.g. "Faster dipping makes shorter water waves": two ripple-tanks, frequency 5 and 10 Hz; goals wavelength {item: each, m: its wavelength reading} (v = f·λ)
  - e.g. "A ball hitting a xylophone bar makes it ring": a xylophone-bar with a ball held above it (or rolling off a ramp onto it); goal sounds {source: bar}
  - e.g. "A bell in a jar goes quiet as the air is pumped out": a bell-jar (pump_at 1, pump_for 4, air_left 0) and a sound-meter 1 m away; the meter's level falls by about 35 dB
  - e.g. "Shorter xylophone bars ring higher": xylophone-bars 0.20 and 0.141 m long (779 → 1558 Hz); goal higher
  - e.g. "A pendulum's swing time depends on its length": pendulums of different length; goal period {item, seconds} (T = 2π√(L/g): 1 m → 2.0 s)
  - e.g. "A bottle xylophone: more water, lower note": four glass-bottles (fill 0.1, 0.35, 0.6, 0.85, play tap) tapped one after another (strike_at 0.4, 0.9, 1.4, 1.9); goals higher {a: emptier, b: fuller}
  - e.g. "On an oscilloscope, a louder sound makes taller waves and a higher sound makes the waves closer together": two speakers far apart (3 m: 440 Hz at 70 dB and 880 Hz at 70 dB, or the same pitch at 60 and 72 dB), an oscilloscope with its microphone 30 cm from each (time_base 1 ms a square: 4.4 and 8.8 waves across); goals hears {meter: scope, source: its speaker}, louder {a: the louder speaker's scope, b: the other}
  - e.g. "A string telephone carries a whisper when the string is pulled tight, and nothing when it is slack": two string-telephones of 3 m cotton string, one above the other (y_m 0.3 and 0.9 over the table, x 1.3), each with its own child whispering; the top one pull 5 N (taut), the bottom one pull 0 (slack); a sound-meter at each right cup (x 2.97, height 0.3 on the table; the top one on: air with height 0.12 at y_m 0.78); goals hears {meter: top meter, source: taut phone}, hears {meter: bottom meter, source: slack phone, expect: false}
  - e.g. "Sound travels faster through water than through air": a water-tank (Liquids), a tuning-fork (box false) standing in its water, a hydrophone beside the tank with its probe under the water (reach over the wall), a sound-meter in the air; the hydrophone's at:fork reading is distance ÷ 1481 m/s
### tuning-fork — Tuning fork · static (fixed in place)
A steel tuning fork standing on its wooden resonance box. Struck at its strike time it hums one steady note (its pitch) that slowly dies away; a ball or a ping-pong ball touching a prong is knocked away by the vibration, and one that hits a prong makes it ring. Facts: 440 Hz · 10.5 cm prongs · rings ≈ 2 s on its box.
Anchor (x, y): the middle of the bottom of its box. Outline at defaults: 0.195 × 0.243 m; from the anchor x −0.098…+0.098, y +0…+0.243.
Props: pitch: Hz =440 [128…2048]; box: bool =true; strength: (×) =1 [0.2…2]; strike_at: s =0.5 [0…20]; hits: int =1 [1…10]; every: s =1 [0.1…10]; show_waves: bool =true.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): sounding (Sound 1 m away, dB), pitch (Pitch, Hz), struck (Times sounded), amp_mm (Vibration, mm).
Notes: also called: sound, pitch, vibration, note, frequency, fork, ring, hum, music.
### plucked-ruler — Plucked ruler · static (fixed in place)
A 30 cm ruler clamped to the table's right edge (or its left edge: edge left) with part of it sticking out past it; it clamps itself to that edge wherever its x is. Plucked, its free end buzzes up and down; the shorter the part that sticks out, the faster it vibrates and the higher its note. Facts: 15 cm over the edge · 35 Hz.
Anchor (x, y): the table's edge, under the ruler (the overhang sticks out past it: right, or left with edge left). Outline at defaults: 0.3 × 0.033 m; from the anchor x −0.15…+0.15, y +0…+0.033.
Props: overhang: m =0.15 [0.05…0.25]; ruler: *plastic* | steel | wood; edge: *right* | left; strength: (×) =1 [0.2…2]; strike_at: s =0.5 [0…20]; hits: int =1 [1…10]; every: s =1 [0.1…10]; show_waves: bool =true.
Readings (the run reports them; goals and edits can use them): sounding (Sound 1 m away, dB), pitch (Pitch, Hz), struck (Times sounded), amp_mm (Vibration, mm).
Notes: also called: sound, pitch, vibration, twang, ruler, overhang, cantilever, buzz.
### drum — Drum · static (fixed in place)
